Mommy smiled. She said, "No, Lily. You have to wait until after dinner. But I have something else for you. Come with me."

Mama: "It's a rag, sweetie. It's for cleaning."

Beth: "I want to use it to clean my room."

Mama: "That's a wonderful idea. But if you clean your room and leave the rag lying here, it will soon become empty again. Remember, it's important to put things away after you use them. That way nothing ever gets lost."

Beth nodded and put the rag away in the cleaning cupboard. She swept and tidied the room until it was nice and clean. She was very proud.

The moral of the story is that we should put things away after we use them, or else they will soon become empty.

Sam and Mia were friends who liked to play outside. One day, it was very hot and they wanted to cool down. They saw a big cooler in the garage that had a button on it. Sam said, "Let's push the button and see what happens. Maybe it will make cold air for us."

Mia said, "No, Sam, we should not touch the cooler. It is not ours and it might be dangerous. We should ask mom or dad first."

Sam said, "Don't be silly, Mia. It is just a cooler. Nothing bad will happen. I want to feel the cold air. It will be fun." He pushed the button and the cooler made a loud noise.

Mia said, "Sam, stop! Turn it off! It is too loud and too powerful. It is not a cooler, it is a blower. It will blow us away!"

But Sam did not listen. He liked the noise and the power. He said, "Look, Mia, it is so cool. It can blow anything away. Watch this!" He pointed the blower at a pile of leaves and they flew in the air.

Mia said, "Sam, please, stop! You are making a mess. And you are hurting the plants and the animals. And you are wasting the power. You do not need the blower. You are being selfish and foolish."

But Sam did not listen. He said, "No, Mia, you are wrong. I need the blower. It is mine and I can do what I want. It is the best thing ever. Watch this!" He pointed the blower at Mia and she flew in the air.

Mia screamed, "Sam, no! Help me! I am scared!" She tried to hold on to something, but it was too late. The blower was too powerful and it blew her away. She landed far away, in a pond, and got wet and cold and hurt.

Sam realized what he had done. He felt sorry and scared. He ran to the pond and looked for Mia. He called her name, but she did not answer. He did not see her. He only saw bubbles and ripples. He cried and cried. He wished he had listened to Mia. He wished he had not touched the cooler. He wished he had not been so greedy and stupid.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not yours and that you do not understand. They might be dangerous and hurt you or others. Listen to your friends and respect their feelings. Share and be kind. Power is not always good. Sometimes, less is more.

Lily: I am a big and strong lion. I can roar and scare everyone. (She roars loudly and stomps around the stage.)

Ben: I am a small and smart mouse. I can run and hide from everyone. (He runs around the stage and squeaks softly.)

Lily: I see you, mouse. You are my lunch. (She chases Ben and tries to catch him.)

Ben: Help, help, lion. Please don't eat me. (He dodges Lily and runs to a corner of the stage.)

Lily: I have you now, mouse. You are trapped. (She pounces on Ben and pins him down.)

Ben: Please, please, lion. Let me go. I can be your friend. (He looks at Lily with big eyes and pleads with her.)

Lily: A friend? A mouse can be a friend to a lion? (She looks confused and tilts her head.)

Ben: Yes, yes, lion. A mouse can be a friend to a lion. I can do something for you. (He smiles and nods.)

Lily: What can you do for me, mouse? (She asks curiously and loosens her grip.)

Ben: I can lie to you. (He says quickly and winks.)

Lily: Lie to me? Why would you lie to me? (She asks suspiciously and frowns.)

Ben: Because lying is fun. I can tell you things that are not true, and you can pretend to believe me. (He says cheerfully and giggles.)

Lily: That sounds silly. How do you lie? (She asks doubtfully and shrugs.)

Ben: It's easy. You just say something that is different from what you see or know. For example, I can say that you are not a lion, but a bunny. (He says playfully and points at her.)

Lily: A bunny? But I am a lion. I have a scarf and a hat and a roar. (She says confusedly and touches her scarf and hat and roars.)

Ben: See? That's a lie. You are not a lion, you are a bunny. You have a fluffy tail and long ears and a hop. (He says teasingly and touches her tail and ears and hops.)

Lily: No, no, mouse. You are lying. I am not a bunny, I am a lion. You are the bunny. You have a shirt and a cap and a squeak. (She says defiantly and touches his shirt and cap and squeaks.)

Ben: Ha, ha, lion. You are lying too. I am not a bunny, I am a mouse. You are the mouse. You have a scarf and a hat and a squeak. (He says mockingly and touches her scarf and hat and squeaks.)

Lily and Ben keep lying to each other and laughing. They forget that they are a lion and a mouse. They have fun playing pretend on the stage. They are friends.

The car flew out of his hand and hit the wall. It broke into pieces. Tom cried and cried. He hurt his knee and his head. He lost his car. His mom heard him and came to help him. She was angry and sad. She said, "Tom, you were very naughty. You did not listen to me. You broke your car and hurt yourself. Now you have no car and no nap. You have to stay in your room and think about what you did."

Tom felt very sorry. He wished he had listened to his mom. He wished he had shared his car. He wished he had napped. He learned a hard lesson. He did not own anything. He only had things to enjoy and care for. He hoped he could get a new car someday. He hoped he could be a good boy. He hoped his mom would forgive him. He lay down on his bed and sobbed. He had a bad day.

Tom is angry. He does not want to listen to Sam. He wants to do what he wants. He runs away from Sam. He goes to the park by himself.

But when he gets to the park, he sees that it is raining. The swings are wet and slippery. The slide is muddy and cold. There is no one else to play with. Tom feels sad and lonely.

After the test, they go outside. The rain has stopped. The sun is shining. The park is dry and bright. They run to the swings and the slide. They laugh and play. They have a great time. They are friends.

Anna and Ben are friends who live in different nations. Anna lives in a nation where people eat rice and fish. Ben lives in a nation where people eat bread and cheese. One day, they talk on the phone and tell each other what they had for lunch.

"I had rice and fish. It was yummy!" Anna says.

"I had bread and cheese. It was yummy too!" Ben says.

They both think that their food is yummy, but they also wonder what the other food tastes like. They decide to try each other's food the next time they visit.

A few weeks later, Anna goes to Ben's nation and Ben goes to Anna's nation. They both bring some of their food to share with each other. They sit down and try a bite of the new food.

Anna tries the bread and cheese. She makes a face and says, "This is not yummy. This is dry and hard."

Ben tries the rice and fish. He makes a face and says, "This is not yummy either. This is wet and slimy."

They both push away their plates and say, "I don't like your food. I only like my food."

They both feel sad and angry. They don't want to talk to each other anymore. They think that their food is better than the other food.

But then, they see a little girl who is hungry and has no food. She looks at their plates and says, "Can I have some of your food, please? I have not eaten for a long time. I don't care what kind of food it is. I just want something yummy."

Anna and Ben look at each other and feel ashamed. They realize that they have been rude and selfish. They remember that food is not just yummy, but also important and precious. They decide to share their food with the little girl and with each other.

They give the little girl some bread and cheese and some rice and fish. They also try some more of each other's food. They find out that the food is not so bad after all. It is just different. They learn to appreciate and respect the different food and the different nation.

They say sorry to each other and hug. They say, "Your food is yummy too. And so are you. You are my friend."

The little girl smiles and says, "Thank you for your food and your friendship. You are yummy too. And so is your nation."

The moral of the story is: Don't judge a food by its look or a nation by its name. Try to understand and enjoy the diversity of the world. Be kind and generous to others who need your help. Be grateful for what you have and share it with others. That is what makes everything yummy.

The moral value of the story is that biting is bad and being kind and gentle is good. The narrative uses foreshadowing or setup and payoff by showing that Tim's biting habit leads to his trouble with the bee and his regret. The story only uses simple words that a 3 year old child would understand.

"Sam, stop!" Ben shouts. "The bull does not like red. He will get angry!"

But Sam ignores Ben. He thinks he is a superhero. He waves the cloth at the bull and says, "Ha ha, bull, you can't catch me!"

The bull sees the cloth. He does not like it. He snorts and lowers his horns. He charges at Sam.

"Sam, run!" Ben screams. He is scared for his friend.

Sam is scared too. He drops the cloth and runs back to the fence. The bull follows him. Sam tries to climb the fence, but he is too slow. The bull reaches him and pushes him with his horns.

"Ow!" Sam cries. He falls to the ground. He hurts his arm and his leg.

Ben runs to Sam. He helps him get up. He sees blood on Sam's arm and leg. He is worried.

"Sam, are you okay?" Ben asks.

Sam is not okay. He is in pain. He is also sorry. He knows he was silly and did not listen to Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sam says. "I was wrong. I should have listened to you. You are a good friend."

Ben hugs Sam. He is glad Sam is sorry. He is also a good friend.

"It's okay, Sam," Ben says. "I forgive you. But don't do that again. The bull is not a toy. He is a dangerous animal."

Sam nods. He agrees. He does not want to play with the bull anymore. He wants to go home.

"What happened?" they ask.

Ben and Sam tell them what happened. They say they are sorry. They promise to be more careful.

Sam and Mia are best friends. They like to play with blocks and make towers. One day, they find a big bottle of glue in the art room. They think glue can make their towers stronger.

"Let's use glue to support our blocks," Sam says. "Then they won't fall down."

"Good idea," Mia says. "You are very dependable. You always have good ideas."

They take some glue and squeeze it on their blocks. Then they stack them up high. They make a big tower with glue. They are very proud of their tower.

But then, the teacher comes in. She sees the glue on the blocks and on the table. She is not happy.

"Who used the glue without asking?" she asks. "Glue is not for blocks. Glue is for paper and art. You made a big mess."

Sam and Mia feel bad. They did not know they did something wrong. They look at each other. They are scared.

"We did it," Sam says. "We wanted to make a strong tower. We are sorry."

The teacher sighs. She is not angry anymore. She is glad they told the truth.

"I understand," she says. "But glue is not a toy. You have to be careful with glue. It can stick to things and make them hard to clean. Next time, ask me before you use glue. OK?"

"OK," Sam and Mia say. They help the teacher clean the blocks and the table. They learn their lesson.

They still like to play with blocks and make towers. But they don't use glue anymore. They use their hands and their brains to support their blocks. They are still best friends. They are still dependable.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play dress-up. One day, they found a big box of costumes in the attic. They tried on different hats, glasses, and wigs. Lily found a funny mustache that stuck to her face. She laughed and said, "Look at me, I'm a detective!"

Ben saw Lily's mustache and felt jealous. He wanted to have a mustache too. He looked for another one in the box, but there was none. He saw a feather boa that was pink and fluffy. He had an idea. He sneaked behind Lily and pulled off her mustache. He replaced it with the feather boa. He said, "Ha ha, now you're a princess!"

Lily felt a tickle on her face. She touched it and saw the feather boa. She was angry and sad. She said, "Hey, that's not fair! You took my mustache! Give it back!"

Ben did not want to give it back. He liked the mustache. He said, "No, it's mine now. You can have the feather boa. It's better for you."

Lily and Ben started to argue and tug at the mustache. They did not notice that their mom came into the attic. She saw them fighting and said, "What are you doing? Why are you being so mean to each other?"

Lily and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They felt ashamed. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were playing dress-up, but we wanted the same thing."

Mom said, "Playing dress-up is fun, but you have to share and take turns. You can't just take something from someone else and replace it with something they don't want. That's not nice. How would you feel if someone did that to you?"

Lily and Ben thought about it. They realized that they would feel hurt and angry. They said, "You're right, mom. We wouldn't like that. We're sorry."

Mom said, "It's okay. I'm glad you understand. Now, why don't you apologize to each other and try to find something else to play with?"

Lily and Ben hugged and said, "We're sorry. We love you." They gave back the mustache and the feather boa. They looked in the box and found a pirate hat and a crown. They smiled and said, "Let's be pirates and kings!"

Mom said, "That sounds like fun. Have fun, but remember to be kind and respectful to each other."

Lily and Ben said, "We will, mom. Thank you." They put on the pirate hat and the crown and pretended to sail the seas and rule the lands. They had a lot of fun and did not fight anymore.

The moral of the story is: Don't be jealous of what others have and don't take things without asking. Share and take turns and be kind and respectful to others.

But as she turned to go, she tripped on a root and fell. The necklace flew out of her hand and landed on her neck. It snapped shut and locked itself. Mom felt a sudden pain in her chest and a coldness in her heart. She looked at Ben and Mia with a cruel glare.

"Mine, mine, mine!" she shouted. "This is my treasure, and you can't have it! Go away, go away, go away!"

She ran away from them, into the woods, where she disappeared. Ben and Mia cried and called for her, but she did not come back. They were alone and afraid. They had lost their mom to the curse of the skull.

Lily looked at the fish and thought. She liked the fish, but she also wanted to catch more. She decided to replace it. She said, "I want to replace it. Maybe I can catch a bigger fish."

The fisherman nodded and helped her unhook the fish. He threw it back into the water and said, "Good choice, Lily. Let's see what else you can catch."

Lily smiled and thanked him. She cast the line again and waited. She had fun fishing with the friendly fisherman.

Spot's mom was happy to see the shiny stone. She put it in a special box to keep it safe. The gloomy sky went away and the sun came out. Spot played with his ball all day long, and he knew that he had a new friend in the bird that settled on the fence.

Lily was very sad, but her friends helped her. They pulled on the cord, and the blanket came back up to Lily. She was so happy to have her warm blanket again. Lily and her friends played together all day, and she never let go of her special blanket again.

Tim climbed into the jeep and sat in the big seat. He pretended to drive the jeep. He turned the wheel left and right. He honked the horn. "Beep! Beep!" Tim was very happy.

Soon, it was time to go home. Tim said goodbye to the jeep. He knew it was a special day. He would always remember the time he got to sit in the shiny, red jeep.

One day, Buzz saw a big flower. He wanted to print his foot on it, like how we paint with our hands. He thought it would be fun. But his friend, Lilly the ladybug, said, "No, Buzz. That is not a good idea. The flower will be sad if you print on it."

Buzz knew Lilly was right. He wanted to be an honest bee and do the right thing. So, instead of printing on the flower, Buzz flew to many other flowers and collected their nectar. He brought it back to his family, and they were very happy.

Buzz learned that being honest and doing the right thing makes everyone happy. And from that day on, he promised to always listen to his friends and be a good bee.

Spot ran and ran, trying to find the mailman. But he got lost. He saw a toilet and thought it might help him find his way. Spot put the letter in the toilet and flushed it. The water went round and round, and the letter was gone.

Spot felt sad. He knew he had made a mistake. The letter was gone, and he couldn't find the mailman. The sun went down, and Spot was still lost. He wished he could go back home and play with his ball again. But Spot couldn't find his way, and the story had a bad ending.

Lily put the honey on Bob's toe and it felt much better. Bob was so happy that he gave Lily a big hug. But then, Bob remembered that he had a picnic planned and all the food would spoil if he didn't go soon. Bob thanked Lily and ran off to his picnic.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He liked to march around the jungle. One day, he saw a little bird. The lion wanted to taste the bird, but the bird was too fast. The lion was sad.

Then, the lion saw a big river. He wanted to drink some water, but the river looked dangerous. The lion was scared. But then he saw a friendly monkey. The monkey told the lion it was safe to drink from the river. The lion was happy and drank some water.

After that, the lion and the monkey became friends. They marched around the jungle together, looking for more friends to play with. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a lot of money, but he didn't like to talk about it. Timmy thought talking about money was boring. 

One day, Timmy went to the park to play. He saw his friend Billy there. Billy wanted to talk about money, but Timmy didn't want to. Timmy thought it was a boring topic. 

Instead, Timmy and Billy played on the swings and talked about their favorite colors. Timmy realized that talking about fun things was much better than talking about money. From then on, Timmy didn't think talking was boring anymore, as long as it was about something fun.

Once upon a time, there was a baby named Timmy. Timmy was very small and couldn't walk yet, so his mommy had to carry him everywhere. One day, Timmy's mommy was going to the park and Timmy was very excited. He loved the park!

As they were walking, Timmy saw a big dog and got scared. He started crying and his mommy picked him up to comfort him. But then, Timmy saw a butterfly and stopped crying. He wanted to follow the butterfly, so his mommy let him down and they followed the butterfly together.

Suddenly, a big boy came and took the butterfly away. Timmy got very angry and started crying again. His mommy picked him up and they went home. Timmy fell asleep in his mommy's arms, dreaming about the butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends, but one day it was too hot to play. Timmy felt miserable because he couldn't go out to play.

Timmy's mom told him to wait until noon when it would be cooler outside. Timmy didn't want to wait, but he listened to his mom. He decided to play inside instead.

Timmy's mom had a surprise for him. She got him a new toy to play with inside. Timmy was so happy he forgot all about being miserable earlier. He played with his new toy until noon, and then he went outside to play with his friends. Timmy learned that sometimes you have to wait to get something good.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with fire. He would light matches and watch them burn. One day, Timmy found a cheap mask in his toy box. He put on the mask and continued playing with fire.

But soon, the mask caught on fire and Timmy got scared. He quickly took off the mask and threw it away. His mom saw what happened and told him, "Timmy, you should never play with fire. It's dangerous and can burn things, like your mask."

Timmy learned his lesson and promised to never play with fire again. He also learned that sometimes buying cheap things can be dangerous and it's better to invest in quality items. From that day on, Timmy always listened to his mom's advice and never played with fire again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved playing with her toys, especially her plastic dolls. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new toy, a magic wand. 

Lily was so excited to play with her new toy. She waved the wand and said, "Abracadabra!" Suddenly, her favorite doll disappeared! 

Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. She went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my doll is gone. I'm fearful." Her mom tried to calm her down and said, "Don't worry, we'll find her." 

But as the days went by, more and more of Lily's toys started disappearing. She knew it was because of the magic wand. One day, Lily waved the wand again and said, "Bring back my toys!" But nothing happened. 

Lily realized that the magic wand was causing all of her toys to disappear. She was sad and didn't know how to make them come back. From that day on, Lily never played with the magic wand again.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in the park. They have a big tube. They want to fly with the tube.

They take the tube to the hill. They hold the tube over their heads. They run down the hill. They hope the tube will catch the wind and make them fly.

But the tube is too heavy. It does not fly. It falls to the ground. Tom and Lily fall too. They are sad.

"Let's try again," Tom says. "Maybe we need more wind."

"Or maybe we need a smaller tube," Lily says.

They look around. They see a small tube. It is from a roll of paper. They pick it up. They go back to the hill.

They hold the small tube over their heads. They run down the hill. The small tube catches the wind. It flies. Tom and Lily fly too. They are happy.

"We did it!" Tom says. "We are successful!"

"Yes, we are!" Lily says. "We are the best flyers in the park!"

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play together. They liked to share their toys and snacks, but sometimes they disagreed. One day, they found a big bowl of blueberries on the table. Anna loved blueberries and wanted to eat them all. Ben liked blueberries too, but he was more modest. He wanted to save some for later and for their mom.

"Let's eat the blueberries!" Anna said, grabbing a handful.

"No, let's not eat them all!" Ben said, holding her hand. "We should share and be nice."

Anna and Ben disagreed. They pulled and pushed the bowl, making a mess. The blueberries rolled and bounced on the floor. Some of them got squished and stained their clothes. Anna and Ben started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the blueberries and the mess and the tears. She was not happy.

"Anna and Ben, what did you do?" she asked. "Why did you disagree and waste the blueberries?"

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They knew they had been greedy and rude. They hugged each other and said sorry to mom.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We like blueberries, but we like you and each other more. Can we have some blueberries later, please?"

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She was glad they learned their lesson. She cleaned up the mess and gave them each a modest amount of blueberries. They ate them happily and thanked mom. They agreed to share and be nice from then on.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun until Ben wanted to play with the doll too.

"Give me the doll, Sara!" Ben said.

"No, it's mine!" Sara said.

They started to fight over the doll. They pulled and pushed and shouted. Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"Stop fighting, Sara and Ben!" Mom said. "You have to share your toys and be nice to each other. Fighting is bad."

"But I want the doll!" Ben said.

"And I want the car!" Sara said.

Mom sighed. She had an idea. She went to the closet and took out a big box. She put it on the floor and opened it.

"Look, Sara and Ben, I have a surprise for you!" Mom said. "It's a new toy for both of you. It's a train set. You can build tracks and bridges and tunnels and make the train go around. Do you like it?"

Sara and Ben forgot about the doll and the car. They ran to the box and looked inside. They saw many pieces of wood and plastic and metal. They saw a red and blue train with a whistle and a smokestack. They saw a hidden switch that made the train move and make sounds.

"Wow, a train set!" Sara and Ben said. "Thank you, Mom!"

They hugged Mom and then started to play with the train set. They worked together and helped each other. They made a long and winding track that filled the living room. They put the train on the track and turned on the switch. They watched the train go around and around. They smiled and laughed.

Mom smiled too. She was happy to see Sara and Ben playing nicely. She sat on the couch and picked up a book. She decided to relax and read for a while. She was glad she had bought the train set. It was a good way to end the fight.

Sara was a spoiled girl who always wanted new toys. She did not like to share with her friends or play with her old toys. She only wanted to watch TV and eat candy.

One day, her mom took her to the park. Sara saw a boy playing with a ball. She wanted the ball, so she ran to the boy and tried to grab it. The boy said, "No, this is my ball. You can't have it."

Sara cried and screamed. She said, "I want the ball! Give it to me now!" Her mom came and said, "Sara, stop being rude. You can't take other people's things. You have to ask nicely and wait for your turn."

Sara did not listen. She kicked the boy and took the ball. The boy was sad and angry. He said, "You are a mean girl. You are not my friend."

Sara did not care. She threw the ball in the air and laughed. She said, "I have the ball. I am the best."

But then, something bad happened. The ball flew too high and hit a branch. The branch broke and fell on Sara's head. Sara fell down and hurt herself. She dropped the ball and cried.

Her mom came and said, "Sara, are you okay? I told you to be careful. You should not be so greedy and selfish. You should learn to be kind and share with others."

Sara felt sorry. She said, "Mom, I am sorry. I was wrong. I hurt the boy and myself. I don't want the ball anymore. I want to say sorry to the boy and be his friend."

Her mom hugged her and said, "That's good, Sara. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, let's go and apologize to the boy and see if he wants to play with you."

Sara nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you for teaching me. I love you."

The end.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. There is a big pond in the park. The pond has ducks and fish. Tom and Lily like to feed the ducks and watch the fish.

One day, Tom and Lily go to the park with their mums. They bring some bread for the ducks. They see a shiny thing in the water. It is a medal. Tom and Lily want to get the medal. They think it is pretty and cool.

"Look, Lily, a medal!" Tom says. "Let's get it!"

"How?" Lily asks. "It is too far."

Tom has an idea. He picks up a stick. He tries to reach the medal with the stick. He pokes the water with the stick. He makes a big splash. The ducks and the fish swim away. The medal moves closer.

"I got it, I got it!" Tom says. He pulls the stick with the medal. He is happy.

"Wow, Tom, you are clever!" Lily says. She claps her hands. She is happy too.

Tom and Lily show the medal to their mums. Their mums are proud of them. They say they can keep the medal. They say it is a reward for being good friends.

Tom and Lily smile. They hug each other. They share the medal. They put it on their necks. They feel like winners. They have fun in the park. They love the medal. They love the pond. They love the ducks and the fish. They love each other.

Tommy and Lily were playing hide and seek in the park. Tommy was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran behind a big tree and waited for Tommy to find her. She was very quiet and still.

Tommy looked around the park and tried to guess where Lily was hiding. He saw a swing, a slide, a bench, and a fountain, but no Lily. He wondered if she was behind the bushes, or under the bridge, or in the sandbox. He decided to check the bushes first.

He walked slowly to the bushes and peeked inside. He saw something furry and brown. He thought it was Lily's hair. He shouted, "I found you, Lily!" and pulled the furry thing out of the bushes.

But it was not Lily. It was a sleeping dog. The dog woke up and barked loudly. Tommy was scared and let go of the dog. The dog ran away, wagging its tail. Tommy was embarrassed. He felt silly for grabbing the wrong thing.

Lily heard the bark and the shout. She came out from behind the tree and saw Tommy. She laughed and said, "That was not me, Tommy. That was a dog. You need to look better." Tommy felt more embarrassed. He said, "Sorry, Lily. I thought it was you. You have good hiding skills." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Tommy. You have good seeking skills. But maybe you need a nap. You look tired." Tommy nodded and said, "Maybe you are right, Lily. Let's go home and have a nap. Then we can play again." Lily agreed and they walked home together, holding hands.

He took a big handful of candy and stuffed it in his mouth. He did not share with Lily. He did not say thank you. He was greedy and rude.

Lily was sad and angry. She had only one candy and Ben had many. She asked him to share, but he ignored her. He just ate more and more candy.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big pile of wood near the swings. They wonder what it is for.

"Maybe someone will make a house with the wood," Tom says.

"Or a boat," Sue says.

They go closer to the wood and touch it. It is rough and hard. Some of the wood has nails and paint on it.

"Be careful, you might get hurt," Tom says.

Sue sees a small piece of wood that looks like a bird. She picks it up and shows it to Tom.

"Look, this wood is a bird. It has a beak and wings and a tail," she says.

Tom smiles and takes the wood bird from Sue. He holds it in his hand and makes it fly.

"Tweet, tweet, I am a wood bird. I can fly in the sky," he says.

Sue laughs and claps her hands.

"That is a funny wood bird. Can I play with it too?" she asks.

Tom nods and gives the wood bird back to Sue. They take turns making the wood bird fly and talk.

They are having so much fun that they do not see a man coming towards them. The man is wearing a dirty coat and a hat. He has a beard and a bag. He looks poor and sad.

"Hey, what are you doing with my wood?" the man says in a loud voice.

Tom and Sue are scared. They drop the wood bird and run away.

"Sorry, mister, we did not know it was your wood," Tom says.

The man picks up the wood bird and looks at it. He sees the beak and the wings and the tail. He remembers something from a long time ago. He remembers when he was a boy and he had a toy bird made of wood. He loved that bird and played with it every day. But one day, he lost it and he never saw it again.

He feels a tear in his eye. He puts the wood bird in his bag and walks away. He thinks maybe he will make a new toy bird with the wood. Maybe he will feel happy again.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a new girl playing with a ball. Lily wanted to play with her, but she felt shy. She did not know how to say hello.

"Mom, can I play with that girl?" Lily asked.

"Of course, honey. Why don't you go and introduce yourself? Tell her your name and ask her if she wants to share the ball," mom said.

Lily nodded and walked to the girl. She saw that the girl had a figure of a princess in her pocket. Lily liked princesses too.

"Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?" Lily said.

The girl looked at Lily and smiled. She was quiet, but not rude.

"I'm Anna. Do you want to play with me?" Anna said.

"Yes, please. Can I see your figure? It's very pretty," Lily said.

Anna took out her figure and showed it to Lily. It was a pink princess with a crown and a dress.

"This is Elsa. She's my favorite. Do you like princesses?" Anna said.

"I love princesses. I have a figure of Belle. She's my favorite. She likes to read books, like me," Lily said.

Lily took out her figure and showed it to Anna. It was a yellow princess with a rose and a book.

"Wow, she's beautiful. I like to read books too. Maybe we can read together sometime," Anna said.

Lily and Anna became friends. They shared the ball and their figures. They had fun in the park. Mom was happy to see Lily make a new friend.

The moral of the story is: Don't be afraid to introduce yourself to new people. You might find something in common and make a good friend.

Lily and Tom were twins who shared a room. They liked to play with their toys and read books before they went to sleep. But sometimes they heard a mysterious noise that scared them. It sounded like a loud beep-beep-beep that came from outside their window.

One night, they heard the noise again. They jumped out of their bed and ran to their mom and dad's room. "Mom, Dad, we heard the noise again!" they cried. "What noise?" their mom asked, rubbing her eyes. "The beep-beep-beep noise!" they said. "It's very loud and scary!"

Their dad got up and put on his robe. He took Lily and Tom by the hand and led them to the window. He pointed to a big truck that was parked on the street. "See that truck?" he said. "That's the garbage truck. It comes every week to collect the trash. The beep-beep-beep noise is the alarm that tells the driver to be careful when he backs up. It's not scary, it's just a safety feature."

Lily and Tom looked at the truck and saw the driver waving at them. They waved back and smiled. They realized that the noise was not mysterious, it was just part of the truck. They thanked their dad for explaining and hugged their mom. They went back to their room and snuggled in their bed. They closed their eyes and fell asleep, without worrying about the noise.

Tim and Kim nod. They unwrap the candy and put it in their mouths. They start to chew.

"Wow, this is fizzy!" Kim says. She feels bubbles in her mouth.

"Did you like it?" he asks.

They play some more. They are happy. They like the fire truck and the fireman and the candy.

Anna and Ben stop arguing. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They say to Mom, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing with trains, but we had a fight. Anna wanted to mark the rails with the marker, but Ben did not like it."

Mom says to Anna and Ben, "I understand that you have different ideas, but you need to respect each other and the toys. You can't mark the rails with the marker, because it will damage them and make them hard to use. You can't yell and push, because it will hurt each other and make me sad. You need to share and take turns, and use your words to solve your problems. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say to Mom, "We understand, Mom. We are sorry, Mom. We will not mark the rails with the marker anymore. We will not yell and push anymore. We will share and take turns, and use our words to solve our problems."

Mom smiles. She says to Anna and Ben, "That's good. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, why don't you clean up the rails and the marker, and then you can play with trains again. But this time, play nicely, okay?"

Anna and Ben smile. They say to Mom, "Okay, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom." They hug Mom. Then they clean up the rails and the marker. They put them back in the box. Then they play with trains again. But this time, they play nicely. They have fun. They are happy.

And don't worry, you can still have pasta sometimes. But not every day. You need to have some variety. You need to have some balance. You need to have some fun."

Sara nodded. She said, "Okay, mom, I understand. I'll eat my vegetables. And I'll have pasta sometimes. But can I have pasta today? Just today? As a reward?"

Sara's mom laughed. She said, "Okay, Sara, just today. You can have pasta today. But tomorrow, you'll have something else. Something new. Something different. Something exciting. Are you ready?"

Sara said, "Yes, mom, I'm ready. I'm ready to try new things. I'm ready to have fun. I'm ready to eat my vegetables. But first, can I have some pasta?"

Sara's mom said, "Yes, Sara, you can have some pasta. But only a little. And with some vegetables. And with some love."

Sara's mom said, "You're welcome, Sara, I love you too. And I love pasta. And I love vegetables. And I love you. Always."

"I'm good," Lily said. "I like your mailbox. It's long and green." 

"Thank you, Lily," Mr. Brown said with a smile. "I like it too. I'm going to check if I have any mail today." 

Lily watched as Mr. Brown opened his mailbox and took out a letter. "I got a letter!" Mr. Brown exclaimed. 

"That's great!" Lily said. "Who is it from?" 

"It's from my sister," Mr. Brown said. "She lives far away and I miss her. I'm so happy to hear from her." 

Lily smiled. She was happy for Mr. Brown. She loved seeing him smile.

The children were happy and thanked her for the beautiful drawing. They played together for a while and had lots of fun. The lady felt happy too, knowing that she had made some new friends and brought joy to their day.

Once upon a time, there was an old cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to eat tuna. One day, Mittens was very hungry and wanted some tuna. But Mittens' owner forgot to buy tuna from the store. Mittens started to yell, "Meow! Meow! Meow!" 

Mittens' owner heard the yelling and knew that Mittens was hungry. So, the owner went to the store and bought some tuna for Mittens. Mittens was very happy and ate all the tuna. Mittens' owner was happy too because Mittens was not yelling anymore. 

From that day on, Mittens' owner always made sure to buy tuna for Mittens so that Mittens would not have to yell again. Mittens was happy and purred with contentment. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion in the jungle. The lion was very strong and brave. One day, the lion saw a little rabbit who was lost. The lion felt compassionate and wanted to help the rabbit find its way back home.

The lion asked the rabbit where it lived, but the rabbit didn't know. The lion thought for a moment and then nodded his head. He decided to take the rabbit on his back and search for its home. They walked and walked until they found a cozy burrow in the ground.

The rabbit was very happy and thanked the lion for being so kind and compassionate. The lion just smiled and nodded his head again. From that day on, the lion and the rabbit became good friends and went on many adventures together.

Later, Tim's mom saw the sock with the face on it. She said, "Tim, did you draw on this sock?" Tim said, "Yes, Mom. I made a friend to play with." His mom was not happy. "You should not draw on things that are not yours," she said.

Tim's mom decided to punish him. She said, "You cannot play with your toys for one day." Tim was sad, but he knew he did something wrong. He said, "I am sorry, Mom. I will not do it again."

From that day on, Tim learned to only draw on paper. He still played with the sock, but he never drew on it again. Tim and the sock were very happy together, and Tim became an even better artist.

The next day, Lily went to the bush again. She looked at it very closely. She saw something shiny behind the leaves. Lily was very excited. She knew she was going to discover something great.

Lily moved the leaves and found a pretty box. She opened the box and saw beautiful, shiny stones inside. Lily was so happy about her discovery. She ran to her mom and showed her the box. Her mom smiled and said, "Lily, you found a treasure in the ordinary bush!"

Tim and Sue went to the switch on the wall. They tried to make the light bright, but it did not work. The light was still dull. They were sad and did not know what to do. 

Then, a nice man came to the house. He saw the switch and the dull light. The man said, "I can help you." He fixed the switch and the light became bright. 

In the end, Tim and Sue were very happy. They thanked the nice man and played in the bright light. They knew they could always ask for help when they needed it.

Tom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, I want to marry you. You are my favorite person. But we need a jacket. It is cold today."

A lady came to the bench and saw Lily and Tom. She was looking for her jacket. She saw the ring on Lily's finger and said, "Oh, what a pretty ring. Where did you get it?"

Lily and Tom looked at each other and said, "We found it in the grass. It is our wedding ring. We are married now."

The lady laughed and said, "You are very cute. But that is my ring. I dropped it by accident. And that is my jacket. I left it here for a moment. Can I have them back, please?"

Lily and Tom felt sad. They liked the ring and the jacket. They did not want to give them back. But they knew it was the right thing to do. They took off the ring and the jacket and gave them to the lady. They said, "We are sorry. We did not know they were yours. Here you go."

The lady smiled and said, "Thank you. You are very nice. And you are still married, even without the ring and the jacket. You have each other. That is the most important thing. You are very lucky."

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "Thank you. You are very nice, too. We are happy. We are married. We have each other. We are very lucky."

One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a boy with a dog. The dog was big and brown. The boy had a rope in his hand. He used the rope to lead the dog.

Lily nodded. She liked dogs. She walked to the boy and the dog. She reached out her hand to touch the dog's fur.

But Rex saw Lily's bracelet. He liked shiny things. He jumped and bit Lily's wrist. He tried to take the bracelet.

"Ow! No! Bad dog!" Lily cried. She felt pain and fear. She pulled her hand back.

"Rex, stop! Drop it! I'm sorry, he doesn't usually do that. He is a regular dog. He just likes to play," the boy said. He pulled the rope to make the dog let go.

Lily's mom ran to her. She saw the blood on Lily's wrist. She saw the bracelet in the dog's mouth.

"Are you okay, Lily? Let me see your wound. That dog hurt you. He is not a regular dog. He is a bad dog. He should not have your bracelet," Lily's mom said. She was angry and worried.

She took the bracelet from the dog. She wrapped Lily's wrist with a cloth. She hugged Lily and kissed her.

"It's okay, mom. I'm okay. The dog didn't mean it. He just liked my bracelet. It's shiny and has many colors," Lily said. She felt sad and brave.

She looked at the boy and the dog. They looked sorry and scared.

"Can I still be your friend?" Lily asked the boy.

The boy smiled. He nodded.

"Yes, you can. I'm sorry, Lily. You are very nice. Can I see your bracelet?" the boy asked Lily.

Lily smiled. She nodded.

"Yes, you can. But you have to be careful. And you have to share it with Rex. He likes it too," Lily said.

Sara was shy. She did not like to talk to new people. She liked to play with her toys and her cat. But her mom said she had to go to school this year. Sara was scared.

The first day of school, Sara held her mom's hand tight. She saw many kids and a big building. She heard loud noises and saw bright colors. She wanted to go home. Her mom gave her a hug and said, "You will be fine, Sara. School is fun. You will make new friends and learn new things. I will be back soon. I love you."

Sara followed her mom to a room with a sign that said, "Mrs. Lee's Class". She saw a lady with a smile and a dress. She said, "Hello, Sara. Welcome to my class. I am Mrs. Lee. You can sit here, next to Ben." She pointed to a boy with brown hair and glasses. He had a book and a car on his desk. He looked at Sara and said, "Hi, Sara. Do you like cars?"

Sara did not say anything. She looked at the floor. She felt shy. She wished she had her cat. She did not want to talk to Ben. She did not want to be in school.

Mrs. Lee started the class. She said, "Today, we will learn about the alphabet. Can you tell me what letter this is?" She showed a card with a big A on it. Some kids raised their hands and said, "A!" Sara did not raise her hand. She did not want to talk.

But then, something happened. Sara saw a picture on the wall. It was a picture of a cat. It looked like her cat. It had black and white fur and green eyes. It had a red collar with a bell. Sara loved her cat. She wanted to see the picture better. She forgot about being shy. She got up from her seat and walked to the wall. She touched the picture and said, "Cat!"

Everyone looked at Sara. Mrs. Lee smiled and said, "Yes, Sara, that is a cat. And what letter does cat start with?" Sara looked at the card and said, "C!" Mrs. Lee said, "Very good, Sara. You are smart. Do you want to tell us your cat's name?"

Sara nodded and said, "His name is Max. He is my best friend. He likes to play and cuddle. He has a bell on his collar. Do you want to hear it?" She shook the picture and made a jingle sound. The other kids laughed and clapped. Ben said, "That's cool, Sara. I like cats too. My cat's name is Fluffy. She is gray and fluffy. Do you want to see her picture?" He took out a photo from his book and showed it to Sara. Sara smiled and said, "She is pretty. Can I see your car too?"

Ben said, "Sure, Sara. It's a red car. It goes fast. Do you want to play with it?" He gave the car to Sara and said, "You can be the driver. I will be the passenger. Where do you want to go?" Sara said, "Let's go to the park. We can see the birds and the flowers and the swings." Ben said, "OK, Sara. Let's go. Vroom, vroom!"

Sara and Ben played with the car and the picture. They talked and laughed. They became friends. Sara was not shy anymore. She liked school. She liked Mrs. Lee. She liked Ben. She was happy. She learned a new word. She learned a new letter. She learned a new thing. She learned that school was fun.

Lily liked to record her voice with her toy. It was a red box with a button and a microphone. She could say anything and the box would repeat it. She thought it was funny and clever.

One day, she found a new place to play with her toy. It was a big chamber under the stairs. It was dark and quiet and had a lot of old things. Lily thought it was a secret place. She took her toy and a flashlight and went inside.

She turned on the flashlight and looked around. She saw a big coat, a hat, a suitcase and a book. She picked up the book and opened it. It had a lot of words and pictures. She tried to read some words, but they were too hard. She decided to record them instead.

She pressed the button and said, "Once upon a time, there was a princess and a dragon." Then she waited for the box to repeat it. But it did not. She pressed the button again and said, "Hello, hello, are you there?" But it did not answer. She shook the box and tapped it, but it was silent.

She felt sad and scared. She wanted to hear her voice. She wanted to leave the chamber. She called, "Mommy, Daddy, where are you?" But no one heard her. She started to cry.

Then she heard a sound. It was a voice. It was her voice. It came from the box. It said, "Once upon a time, there was a princess and a dragon. Hello, hello, are you there? Mommy, Daddy, where are you?"

Lily was surprised and happy. She smiled and said, "I'm here, I'm here, I'm Lily." The box repeated, "I'm here, I'm here, I'm Lily." Lily laughed and said, "You're funny, you're funny, you're my friend." The box repeated, "You're funny, you're funny, you're my friend."

Lily felt comfortable and safe. She hugged the box and said, "I love you, I love you, you're my toy." The box repeated, "I love you, I love you, you're my toy." Lily closed the book and put it back. She took the box and the flashlight and left the chamber. She found her mommy and daddy and told them about her adventure. They were proud and happy. They gave her a big hug and a kiss. They said, "We love you, we love you, you're our Lily." Lily said, "I love you, I love you, you're my mommy and daddy." And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite one was Anna. Anna had long hair, a pink dress and a smile on her face. Lily took Anna everywhere she went, and talked to her all the time.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the hospital. Lily's grandma was sick and needed to see the doctor. Lily was scared of the hospital. It was big, noisy and smelled funny. She did not want to leave Anna behind, so she put her in her backpack.

At the hospital, Lily's mom took her to see her grandma. Her grandma was lying in a bed, with tubes and wires on her. She looked very tired and sad. Lily felt sorry for her grandma, and gave her a hug. Her grandma smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very sweet. You remind me of myself when I was a little girl. I also had a doll that I loved very much. Her name was Lucy. She was my best friend."

Lily was curious about Lucy. She asked her grandma, "Where is Lucy now? Can I see her?" Her grandma sighed and said, "I don't know, Lily. I lost Lucy a long time ago. I was playing with her in the park, and I forgot to take her with me when I left. I was so sad and lonely without her. I never found her again."

Lily felt sad for her grandma too. She thought about how much she loved Anna, and how she would feel if she lost her. She had an idea. She opened her backpack and took out Anna. She said to her grandma, "Grandma, I have something for you. This is Anna. She is my doll and my best friend. But I want you to have her. She can keep you company and make you happy. She can be your new Lucy."

Her grandma was surprised and touched by Lily's gesture. She took Anna and hugged her. She said to Lily, "Oh, Lily, you are so kind and generous. Thank you for giving me Anna. She is beautiful and lovely. She reminds me of you. You are my new Lucy."

Lily and her grandma smiled and hugged each other. Lily felt happy that she made her grandma happy. She learned that sometimes, sharing is caring, and that giving can be better than receiving. She also learned that dolls can be more than toys. They can be friends and memories.

"Let's go, Lila, maybe we can drink and rest there!" Ben said.

One day, Ben and Sam were playing in the park. They were very hungry, so they went to their mom and asked for a sandwich. Mom gave them each a sandwich, but they were different. Ben had a cheese sandwich and Sam had a ham sandwich.

"I want your sandwich!" Ben said to Sam. "I don't like cheese. Give it to me!"

"No!" Sam said. "This is my sandwich. You have your own. Go away!"

Ben and Sam started to fight. They pulled and pushed each other, and tried to grab the other's sandwich. They did not see the old dog that was watching them. The dog was hungry too, and he liked cheese and ham. He saw his chance and ran to the boys. He snatched both sandwiches from their hands and ran away.

"Hey!" Ben and Sam shouted. "That's our sandwich! Come back!"

But it was too late. The dog was gone, and so were their sandwiches. Ben and Sam felt sad and angry. They looked at each other and realized how silly they had been.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sam said. "I should have shared my sandwich with you. I know you don't like cheese."

"I'm sorry, Sam," Ben said. "I should have been happy with my sandwich. I know you like ham."

They hugged and said they were sorry. Mom saw them and smiled. She gave them another sandwich, and this time they cut it in half and swapped. They ate their sandwich happily and thanked mom.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that fighting is bad, and sharing is good. They learned that they should be grateful for what they have, and not be greedy for what they don't. They learned that sometimes an old dog can teach them a new trick.

Tom was a bald man who liked to eat beef. He worked at a farm and took care of the cows. He was very kind to them and gave them hay and water every day. He also liked to talk to them and pet them.

One day, Tom had to go away for a week. He had to visit his sister who was sick. He packed his bag and said goodbye to the cows. "I will miss you, my friends," he said. "Be good and stay healthy. I will be back soon."

The cows mooed and nodded. They liked Tom and they would miss him too. They watched him drive away in his truck.

While Tom was gone, another man came to the farm. He was not bald and he did not like beef. He did not care about the cows and he did not give them enough hay and water. He also did not talk to them or pet them. He was mean and rude.

The cows were unhappy and hungry. They missed Tom and his kindness. They wished he would come back soon.

One day, they heard a familiar sound. It was Tom's truck. They saw him drive up to the farm. He got out of his truck and smiled. He had a big bag of beef for himself and a lot of hay and water for the cows.

"Hello, my friends," he said. "I missed you so much. How are you?"

The cows mooed and ran to him. They licked his face and rubbed their heads against him. They were so happy to see him.

Tom hugged them and gave them the hay and water. He also gave them some treats and praised them. He told them about his sister and how she was feeling better.

The cows listened and nodded. They were glad that Tom was back and that his sister was well. They did not miss the other man at all. They only loved Tom, the bald man who liked to eat beef.

But their dad does not come back soon. He is gone for a long time. Tom and Jen start to feel worried. They wonder what happened to their dad and the cow. They ask their mom, but she does not know. She says maybe there is a lot of traffic, or maybe the market is very busy.

But their dad does not come back at all. He never comes back. Tom and Jen find out that their dad was robbed on the way to the market. The bad men took his money and his car. They also took the cow that he had bought. They hurt their dad and left him on the road.

Tom and Jen are very sad. They cry a lot. They miss their dad. They do not have a cow. They do not have anything. They wish their dad had never gone to buy a cow. They wish he had stayed with them on the farm. They wish everything was different. But it is not. The end.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big statue of a man on a horse. The statue was very wide and tall, and it had a shiny sword in its hand.

"Let's climb on the statue!" Tom said. "It will be fun!"

Sue was scared. She did not want to climb on the statue. She thought it was dangerous and rude.

"No, Tom, we should not climb on the statue. It is not for playing. It is for looking. We might fall or break it. That would be bad."

But Tom did not listen to Sue. He ran to the statue and started to climb on its leg. He wanted to reach the sword and pretend to be a hero.

"Come on, Sue, don't be a baby!" Tom said. "It is easy and fun!"

Sue shook her head. She stayed on the ground and watched Tom. She hoped he would be careful and come down soon.

But Tom was not careful. He climbed higher and higher, until he reached the sword. He grabbed it and tried to pull it out of the statue's hand. He did not know that the sword was very heavy and stuck to the statue.

"Look, Sue, I have the sword!" Tom said. "I am a hero!"

But as he said that, the sword slipped from his hand and fell to the ground. It made a loud noise and broke into pieces. Tom was shocked and scared. He lost his balance and fell from the statue too. He landed on the sword and hurt himself badly. He cried and screamed.

Sue ran to Tom and tried to help him. She was very sad and scared too. She called for help and waited for someone to come.

Soon, a man came and saw what happened. He was angry and sad. He was the man who made the statue. He worked very hard to make it beautiful and strong. He loved the statue and the man on the horse. He was his hero.

He looked at Tom and Sue and said, "Why did you do this? Why did you climb on the statue and break the sword? You were very naughty and foolish. You did not respect the statue or the hero. You hurt yourself and the statue. You should be sorry and learn a lesson."

Tom and Sue were sorry and learned a lesson. They learned that they should not play on things that are not for playing. They learned that they should listen to their friends who are wise and careful. They learned that they should respect the work and the heroes of others. They learned that playing can be fun, but not when it is dangerous and rude.

The little girl picked up the apple and threw it away. She knew that it was important to keep the bedroom clean and free of things that could rot. She was happy to have a big and clean bedroom to play in.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved candy. He ate candy every day, but his mom told him that too much candy was bad for him. Timmy didn't listen and kept eating candy every day.

One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to a meeting with the dentist. Timmy was eager to go because he thought the dentist would give him candy. But when they got there, the dentist weighed Timmy and told him that he was too heavy because he ate too much candy.

Timmy felt sad and realized that he needed to listen to his mom and eat less candy. From that day on, Timmy only ate candy on special occasions and he became healthier. The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to your parents and take care of your body.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play dress up and wear pretty clothes. One day, Lily's mommy said, "Lily, it's time to get dressed for school." Lily put on her good dress and her mommy helped her with her shoes.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toys when the telephone rang. Her mommy answered it and said, "Hello?" It was Lily's grandma on the phone. Lily's mommy said, "Lily, it's your grandma on the telephone. She wants to talk to you." Lily took the phone and said, "Hi grandma! I'm wearing my good dress today!"

Her grandma said, "Oh, you look so pretty! I wish I could see you." Lily smiled and said, "I wish you could too, grandma. Maybe one day you can come and visit me!" They talked for a little while longer before saying goodbye. Lily was happy to talk to her grandma on the telephone and show off her good dress.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy was playing with his ball near his house. Suddenly, the ball went too far and landed in his neighbor's yard. Timmy felt scared to go and get it because he had never talked to his neighbor before.

But then, Timmy's mom told him that it's always good to say sorry when you make a mistake. So, Timmy gathered up his courage and jogged over to his neighbor's house. He knocked on the door and a kind lady answered. Timmy said sorry and asked if he could get his ball back. The lady smiled and handed the ball to Timmy.

From that day on, Timmy and his neighbor became friends. Timmy learned that it's always better to say sorry and be kind to others. He also learned that sometimes, taking a little jog to do the right thing can make a big difference.

The little boy tried to help the driver, but the truck was too big. Soon, other people came to help, but they could not get the truck out. The rocks were never loaded, and the driver lost his job. The moral of the story is to always follow the rules and not take shortcuts that may lead to trouble.
