Once upon a time, in a wild forest, there lived a little bird named Bob. Bob loved to sing loud songs. One day, as he was singing, he saw a small, lost cat named Lily.

Bob flew down and asked, "Why are you sad, Lily?" Lily said, "I can't find my way home. Can you help me search for it?" Bob agreed to help her.

Together, they searched high and low, near and far. They asked other animals if they knew where Lily's home was. Finally, they found Lily's home, and she was very happy. Bob and Lily became the best of friends, and they always helped each other when needed.

Once upon a time, in a wild forest, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia loved to play outside and throw her ball high up in the sky. She would laugh and clap her hands as the ball went up and down.

One sunny day, Mia went outside to play with her ball. The sun was shining bright and warm on her face. She threw the ball up in the air and watched it fly. But this time, the ball went very, very high. So high, it looked like it touched the sun!

Mia waited for the ball to come back down, but it didn't. She was sad and didn't know what to do. Then, a friendly bird saw Mia and wanted to help. The bird flew up, up, up into the sky and brought the ball back to Mia. She was so happy and thanked the bird. From that day on, Mia and the bird became best friends and played together under the bright sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived in a modern house with his mom, dad, and his cat, Fluffy. Tim liked to play with Fluffy and eat snacks.

One day, Tim wanted a snack. He asked his mom for some cookies. But his mom disagreed. She said, "No, Tim. It's almost dinner time." Tim was sad, but he knew his mom was right.

Later, after dinner, Tim's mom gave him a snack. It was a yummy cookie! Tim was happy and shared the cookie with Fluffy. They both enjoyed the treat and played together all night.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat. This boat was not big, but it was very happy. It liked to float on the water and wave to its friends. The boat had many friends like the fish, the birds, and the trees by the water.

One day, the little boat met a new friend. This friend was a big rock. The rock told the boat, "You are foolish to wave to everyone. You should be like me and stay still." The little boat did not like what the rock said, but it wanted to try.

The boat stopped waving to its friends. It tried to be like the rock and stay still. But the boat was not happy. It missed waving to the fish, the birds, and the trees. So, the little boat decided to be itself and not listen to the rock. It started to wave to its friends again and was very happy. The boat learned that being foolish and happy was better than being still and sad.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a group of birds. They were very sad and miserable because they could not rise and fly high in the sky. They wanted to see the world from up above, but their wings were too weak.

One day, a wise old bird came to visit the group. He saw how sad they were and wanted to help. The wise old bird told them to work together and practice flying every day. He said, "If you help each other and never give up, you will rise high one day."

The group of birds listened to the wise old bird and started to practice. They helped each other and worked very hard. After some time, their wings became strong, and they could rise high in the sky. They were so happy to see the world from up above. They thanked the wise old bird for his help.

The moral of the story is that if we work together and never give up, we can achieve our dreams.

Sara and Ben were going to the airport with Mom and Dad. They were very happy because they were going to see Grandma and Grandpa. They had a big bag with toys and books and snacks.

But when they got to the airport, they saw a lot of people and cars and noise. They had to wait in a long line to show their tickets and bags. Sara and Ben did not like waiting. They started to whine and cry and kick.

Mom and Dad tried to calm them down, but they did not listen. They wanted to play and run and eat. They were spoiled and rude. They made Mom and Dad very sad and angry.

Then, something strange happened. A loud voice said: "Freeze! Do not move! There is a problem!" Sara and Ben looked around and saw that everyone was still and quiet. They saw some men with badges and guns running to a door. They heard sirens and dogs.

Sara and Ben were scared. They did not know what was going on. They stopped whining and crying and kicking. They held Mom and Dad's hands and stayed close to them. They wished they had been good and patient. They learned a lesson.

Anna and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play together in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a collar with a tag.

"Look, Anna, a dog!" Ben says. He runs to the dog and tries to pet it.

"Wait, Ben, be careful!" Anna says. She follows him and sees the tag. It has a name and a phone number. "The dog has a name. It is Max. And this is his owner's number. Maybe he is lost."

Anna takes out her phone and calls the number. A woman answers. She sounds worried.

"Hello, is this Max's owner?" Anna asks.

"Yes, yes, this is me. Have you seen my dog? I have been looking for him everywhere. He ran away from the yard this morning. Where are you?" the woman says.

"We are in the park. We found Max. He is safe and friendly. We can stay with him until you come." Anna says.

"Thank you so much, you are very kind. I will be there soon. What are your names?" the woman says.

"I am Anna and this is my brother Ben. We like dogs. Max is a good dog." Anna says.

The woman arrives and hugs Max. She is very happy and grateful. She thanks Anna and Ben and gives them a reward. She also lets them pet Max and play with him for a while.

Anna and Ben are happy too. They are glad they helped Max and his owner. They are grateful for their new friend. They say goodbye to Max and go home with their reward. They tell their mom and dad what happened. They are proud of themselves. They are good brother and sister.

Tim and Sue are playing in the garden. They see a big bee flying near the flowers. Tim is scared of the bee. He thinks it will sting him.

"Look, a bee!" Tim says. "Run away!"

Sue is not scared of the bee. She knows it is harmless. It only wants to get some nectar from the flowers.

"Don't run away, Tim," Sue says. "The bee will not hurt you. It is harmless. It is your friend."

Tim does not believe Sue. He runs to the house. He finds a comb in the bathroom. He thinks the comb will protect him from the bee. He covers his head with the comb.

Sue follows Tim to the house. She sees him hiding under the comb. She laughs.

"Tim, what are you doing?" Sue says. "The comb will not stop the bee. The bee is not interested in you. The comb is for your hair, not for your head."

Tim peeks out from the comb. He sees Sue smiling. He feels silly.

"Really?" Tim says. "The bee is harmless?"

"Yes, Tim," Sue says. "The bee is harmless. Come, let me show you. The bee is beautiful. It has yellow and black stripes. It makes a buzzing sound. It helps the flowers grow."

Tim puts down the comb. He follows Sue to the garden. He sees the bee flying away. He is not scared anymore. He is curious.

"Can I touch the bee?" Tim says.

"No, Tim," Sue says. "The bee does not like to be touched. It might sting you if you bother it. But you can watch it from a distance. It is amazing."

Tim and Sue watch the bee for a while. They learn more about the bee. They have fun. They forget about the comb.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a shiny jewel on the grass. It is red and round and sparkles in the sun.

"Wow, look at this!" Lila says. "It is so pretty!"

"Can I see?" Ben asks. He takes the jewel and holds it in his hand. He whistles. "It is like a star!"

They decide to share the jewel. They take turns holding it and looking at it. They make up stories about where it came from and what it can do. They pretend it is a magic jewel that can grant wishes.

They have a lot of fun with the jewel. They are glad they found it. They are glad they are friends. They put the jewel in a safe place in their pocket. They go home and tell their moms and dads about their adventure. They say they will play with the jewel again tomorrow. They smile and hug. They are happy.

Lily and Ben were brother and sister. They liked to play in the park near their home. They had a ball, a bike and a doll. They had fun in the park every day.

One day, their mom said, "We need to go to the grocery. We have no food at home. We are poor and we have little money. You have to come with me and help me carry the bags."

Lily and Ben did not want to go to the grocery. They wanted to stay in the park and play. They said, "No, mom, we don't want to go. We want to play. Can we go later?"

Their mom said, "No, we have to go now. It is getting dark and the grocery will close soon. Please, be good and come with me. It will not take long."

Lily and Ben were angry and sad. They did not listen to their mom. They ran away from her and hid behind a tree. They thought their mom would not find them and they could play more.

But their mom was worried and scared. She looked for them everywhere. She called their names and asked people if they saw them. She could not find them. She cried and cried.

Lily and Ben heard their mom cry. They felt sorry and guilty. They came out from behind the tree and ran to their mom. They hugged her and said, "We are sorry, mom. We were bad. We love you. Please, don't cry."

Their mom was happy and relieved. She hugged them and said, "I love you too. But you were very naughty. You made me worry and waste time. Now we have no food and no money. We have to go home hungry and sad."

Lily and Ben were ashamed and sad. They learned a lesson. They should have obeyed their mom and helped her. They should have been grateful for what they had. They should have been good and not selfish. They never ran away from their mom again.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play with their toy boats in the pond. They pretended they were sailors, exploring new lands.

One day, they saw a big green island in the pond. It looked like a jungle, with many trees and plants. They wanted to go there and see what was inside.

"Let's sail to the jungle island!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful. There might be animals there," Tom said.

They pushed their boats into the water and started to sail. They used sticks as oars and made boat noises. They felt very brave and happy.

Soon, they reached the shore of the island. They tied their boats to a branch and climbed out. They looked around and saw many flowers and fruits. They also heard some noises, like birds and monkeys.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Lily said.

"Look, there is a path. Let's follow it and see where it leads," Tom said.

They walked along the path, holding hands. They saw more animals, like a frog, a snake, and a butterfly. They were not scared, they were curious.

They came to a clearing, where they saw a big hut. It was made of wood and leaves. It had a door and a window. They wondered who lived there.

"Hello, is anyone home?" Lily called.

Suddenly, a man came out of the hut. He was tall and strong. He had a beard and a hat. He looked surprised and angry.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" he shouted.

Lily and Tom were scared. They realized they had entered someone's home without permission. They had made a mistake.

"We are sorry, sir. We are sailors. We came to explore the jungle island. We didn't mean to bother you," Tom said.

The man looked at them and saw their toy boats. He realized they were just children, playing a game. He felt sorry for them.

He smiled and said, "I see. Well, I am the king of this island. I live here alone, with my animals. I am very powerful, but also very lonely. Do you want to be my friends?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt relieved and happy. They wanted to be friends with the king.

The king invited them into his hut. He showed them his treasures and his pets. He gave them some fruits and juice. He told them stories about his adventures. They had a lot of fun.

They decided to visit the king often, and bring him gifts and news. They also invited him to sail with them sometimes. They became good friends, and the jungle island became their favorite place to play.

Lily wanted to help her mom cook dinner. She saw a big chicken on the table. She thought it looked yummy. She wanted to put some salt on it. She climbed on a chair and reached for the salt. But she was too small. She could not manage to get the salt. She lost her balance and fell off the chair. The chicken fell off the table too. It landed on the floor with a loud thud.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Mom asked. She ran to Lily and hugged her. She was worried.

"I'm okay, Mom. But I'm sorry. I made a mess. I wanted to help you," Lily said. She felt embarrassed. She looked at the chicken on the floor. It was dirty and had some feathers on it.

"It's okay, sweetie. You don't have to be embarrassed. You were trying to be helpful. But next time, please ask me before you touch anything in the kitchen. It can be dangerous. And we can always wash the chicken and cook it again. It's not wasted," Mom said. She smiled and kissed Lily.

"Okay, Mom. I'm sorry. I love you," Lily said. She hugged Mom back.

"I love you too, Lily. Now, let's clean up this mess and make some salad instead. How does that sound?" Mom asked.

"That sounds good, Mom. Can I help you with the salad?" Lily asked.

"Of course you can, Lily. You are my little helper. Come on, let's go to the garden and pick some lettuce and tomatoes," Mom said.

They went to the garden and picked some fresh vegetables. They washed them and chopped them. They made a delicious salad. They also washed the chicken and put it in the oven. They set the table and waited for Dad to come home. They had a nice dinner together. Lily was happy. She forgot about her embarrassment. She was proud of her salad. She told Dad how she helped Mom. Dad praised her and gave her a big hug. Lily smiled. She loved her family.

Sam and Tom were friends. They liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pile of mud. It looked fun to jump in.

"Let's jump in the mud!" Sam said.

"No, it is dirty and wet. We will get in trouble," Tom said.

Sam did not listen. He ran to the mud and jumped in. He laughed and splashed. Tom watched from far away.

"Come on, Tom! Don't be weak. It is fun!" Sam said.

Tom did not want to be weak. He wanted to be fun. He chose to jump in the mud too. He ran to the mud and jumped in. He did not laugh. He did not splash. He felt cold and sticky.

"Help! Help!" Tom cried. "I am stuck in the mud!"

Sam tried to help him. But he was stuck too. The mud was too deep and thick. They could not move. They could not get out.

They called for help. But no one heard them. They were too far from the house. They were too loud in the mud. They were scared and sad.

They wished they did not choose to jump in the mud. They wished they listened to Tom. They wished they stayed clean and dry. But it was too late. The mud was their trap. The mud was their end.

Tom and Lily were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big sign with a symbol on it. The symbol was a red circle with a line across it.

"What is that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it means no."

"No what?" Tom wondered.

They went closer to the sign. They saw a picture of a dog under the symbol.

"Oh, I get it," Lily said. "It means no dogs. We can't bring dogs here."

Tom felt sad. He loved dogs. He had a dog at home. His dog was brown and fluffy. His dog was named Spot.

"Why can't we bring dogs here?" Tom asked.

"Maybe because they are noisy or messy," Lily guessed. "Or maybe some people are scared of them."

Tom shook his head. "That's not fair. Dogs are nice. They make me happy."

Lily nodded. "Me too. I wish we could bring dogs here."

They looked around. They saw a man with a dog. The dog was black and shiny. The dog was named Rex.

The man and the dog did not see the sign. They walked into the park. They seemed happy.

Tom and Lily ran to them. They wanted to pet the dog.

"Hello," Tom said. "Can we play with your dog?"

The man smiled. "Sure, he loves kids. His name is Rex. What are your names?"

"I'm Tom and this is Lily," Tom said.

"Hi, Rex," Lily said. She stroked the dog's fur.

Rex wagged his tail. He licked their faces. He seemed happy too.

Tom and Lily forgot about the sign. They played with Rex. They threw a ball for him. They ran with him. They laughed with him.

They had fun. They were happy.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their toy animals. They liked to pretend they were in the jungle, and make noises like lions and monkeys. Anna had a rhinoceros, which was her favorite toy. It was gray and had a big horn on its nose. Ben had a giraffe, which was very tall and had spots.

"Look at my rhinoceros!" Anna said. "It is very strong and can run fast. It can scare away any bad animals."

"Look at my giraffe!" Ben said. "It is very tall and can see far. It can eat leaves from the trees."

They both thought their toys were the best, and they started to argue.

"My rhinoceros is better than your giraffe!" Anna said.

"No, my giraffe is better than your rhinoceros!" Ben said.

They were so busy fighting that they did not notice a real rhinoceros walking towards them. It was enormous, much bigger than their toys. It had a thick skin and a sharp horn. It made a loud snort, and the children stopped and looked at it.

"Wow!" Anna said. "It is a real rhinoceros!"

"Wow!" Ben said. "It is so big!"

They were both scared and amazed. They did not know what to do. They held their toys close to them.

The rhinoceros looked at them, and then at their toys. It seemed curious and friendly. It came closer and sniffed their toys. It nudged them gently with its horn. It made a soft grunt, as if to say hello.

"Hello, rhinoceros!" Anna said. "We are Anna and Ben. These are our toys. They are rhinoceros and giraffe."

"Hello, rhinoceros!" Ben said. "You are very nice. Do you want to play with us?"

The rhinoceros nodded its head, and the children smiled. They decided to share their toys with the rhinoceros, and play together in the park. They forgot their argument, and became friends. They learned that the rhinoceros was not scary, but gentle and fun. They also learned that it was good to believe in their toys, but also to be open to new things. They had a wonderful time, and the rhinoceros was happy too.

Anna and Ben love to play in the park. They like to run, swing, slide and climb. Sometimes they go on the trail with their mom and dad. The trail is a long path in the woods. They see trees, flowers, birds and bugs.

One day, they saw a little cat on the trail. The cat was black and white and very cute. But the cat was scared and stuck in a bush. It meowed and tried to get out, but the bush had thorns. Anna and Ben wanted to help the cat.

They ran to their mom and dad and told them about the cat. Their mom and dad followed them to the bush. They used a big stick to move the thorns away from the cat. Then they gently lifted the cat out of the bush. The cat was happy and licked their hands.

Anna and Ben asked their mom and dad if they could keep the cat. Their mom and dad said yes, if the cat had no owner. They put a collar on the cat and wrote their phone number on it. They named the cat Spot, because of his black and white spots.

They took Spot home and gave him food, water and a bed. Spot liked his new home and his new friends. He purred and snuggled with Anna and Ben. They rescued Spot from the bush and gave him a lovely family.

Lila was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She liked to draw and color, but she had no one to show her pictures to. She wished she had a friend who liked to draw and color too.

One day, she found a big box in her room. It had a picture of a printer on it. She wondered what it was. She opened the box and saw a printer inside. It had buttons and wires and paper. She wanted to try it.

She plugged the printer into the wall and turned it on. She saw a light blink. She pressed a button and heard a noise. She saw a paper come out of the printer. It had a picture of a flower on it. She liked the picture. She pressed another button and saw another paper come out. It had a picture of a star on it. She liked that too.

She kept pressing buttons and printing pictures. She had a lot of pictures. She put them on the wall and on the floor and on the bed. She made a big collage of pictures. She was happy.

Then she heard a knock on the door. She opened the door and saw a boy. He had a big smile and a backpack. He said, "Hi, I'm Ben. I just moved next door. Do you want to play with me?"

Lila smiled back. She said, "Yes, I do. Come in. I have something to show you. I have a printer. It makes pictures. Do you like to draw and color?"

Ben nodded. He said, "I love to draw and color. Can I see your printer? Can I print some pictures too?"

Lila said, "Of course. Come on. Let's print some pictures together."

They went to the printer and printed more pictures. They shared their crayons and markers and colored the pictures. They talked and laughed and had fun. They became friends.

Lila was not lonely anymore. She had a friend who liked to draw and color too. She was happy.

"Come on, Sam, let's hurry!" Tim says. "Maybe we can find frogs and snakes and other animals."

Sam nods and follows Tim. They run to the swamp. They see a lot of water and mud and plants. They hear noises and splashes.

"Wow, this swamp is so lively!" Sam says. "Look, there is a frog! And there is a bird!"

Tim points to a big log. "And there is a crocodile!" he says.

Sam gasps. He sees a long tail and big teeth. He is scared. He grabs Tim's hand.

"Tim, we have to go!" he says. "The crocodile might eat us!"

Tim nods. He is scared too. They turn around and run away from the swamp. They do not stop until they reach their house.

They tell their mom what they saw. She hugs them and says they are brave. She says they should not go to the swamp again. It is too dangerous.

Tim and Sam agree. They say they are sorry. They say they will play in the yard instead. They are happy to be safe and warm. They still like to look at animals, but not crocodiles.

"Let's paint with the sauce!" Tom said.

Anna loved to play in the garden with her toy animals. She had a rabbit, a duck, a frog and a mole. The mole was her favorite, because he was soft and brown and had a funny nose. She liked to kiss him and hug him and tell him stories.

One day, she saw a real mole in the garden. He was digging a hole under a flower. Anna was very curious and wanted to say hello. She ran to the mole and picked him up. "Hello, mole!" she said. "You look like my toy mole. Do you want to be friends?"

The mole was scared and angry. He did not like to be picked up by a big girl. He wanted to go back to his hole. He bit Anna's finger and scratched her cheek. "Ow!" Anna cried. "You are not nice, mole! You are mean and rude!"

She dropped the mole and ran to her mother, who was sitting on a bench. Her mother saw her finger and cheek and gave her a band-aid and a kiss. "What happened, Anna?" she asked.

"I wanted to be friends with a real mole, but he bit me and scratched me," Anna said. "He was not like my toy mole. He was not charming at all."

Her mother hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. Real moles are not like toy moles. They are wild and shy and don't like to be touched. You should leave them alone and play with your toy mole. He is charming and loves you very much."

Anna nodded and smiled. She went back to the garden and found her toy mole. She kissed him and hugged him and told him stories. She was happy with her charming toy mole.

Tom and Sue like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the machine. The machine is gray and big. It can make sounds and lights. It can also bow and say hello.

One day, Tom and Sue want to play with the machine, but they have a problem. They both want to play with it at the same time. They start to fight and pull the machine. They say, "It is mine! Give it to me!"

The machine does not like to see them fight. It feels sad and scared. It says, "Please stop! You are hurting me! You are hurting each other! You should share and be nice!"

Tom and Sue hear the machine and stop. They look at the machine and see that it is broken. Some parts are loose and some wires are out. They feel sorry and ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, machine! We did not mean to hurt you! We did not mean to hurt each other! We were selfish and mean!"

The machine says, "It is okay. I forgive you. But you should learn to share and be nice. Sharing and being nice are good. Fighting and being mean are bad. Can you promise me that?"

Tom and Sue nod and hug the machine. They say, "We promise, machine! We will share and be nice! We will fix you and play with you together!"

The machine smiles and bows. It says, "Thank you, Tom and Sue! You are good friends! I am happy!"

The end.

Moral value: Sharing and being nice are good. Fighting and being mean are bad.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to look at the view. The view is very pretty. They can see trees, flowers, birds and clouds.

One day, they see a big hole in the ground. It is very deep. They want to know what is inside.

"Let's talk to the hole," says Anna. "Maybe it will talk back."

"OK," says Ben. "Hello, hole. What are you doing here?"

They wait for an answer. But the hole is very quiet. It does not talk.

"Maybe it is shy," says Anna. "Let's try again. Hello, hole. We are Anna and Ben. We are your friends."

They wait for an answer. But the hole is still very quiet. It does not talk.

"Maybe it is angry," says Ben. "Let's go away. It is not nice to talk to a hole that does not talk back."

They turn to leave. But then they hear a voice. It is very loud. It comes from the hole.

"Hello, Anna and Ben. I am the hole. I am sorry I did not talk to you. I was sleeping. I am very tired. I have been here for a long time. I have seen many things. But I have no friends. Will you be my friends?"

Anna and Ben are surprised. They look at each other. They do not know what to say. They are a little scared. But they are also curious.

"OK," they say. "We will be your friends. But you have to be nice to us. And you have to tell us your stories. What have you seen in the hole?"

The hole is happy. It starts to talk. It tells them many stories. Some are funny. Some are sad. Some are scary. Some are strange. Anna and Ben listen. They ask questions. They laugh. They cry. They gasp. They wonder.

They forget about the time. They forget about the view. They only talk to the hole. And the hole talks to them. They become friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks. They have many blocks of different colors and shapes. They can make houses, cars, towers and more.

One day, they want to make a big castle with their blocks. They start to build the walls and the doors. They add more and more blocks to make it strong and tall.

"Look at our castle!" Lily says. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben says. "But we need a flag. A flag will make it look like a real castle."

They look for a flag, but they cannot find one. They only have a red scarf.

"Can we use this scarf as a flag?" Lily asks.

"No, we cannot," Ben says. "It is too big and heavy. It will make our castle fall down."

Lily is sad. She likes the red scarf. She thinks it will make a nice flag.

"Please, Ben, let us try," she says. "Maybe it will not fall down. Maybe it will look good."

Ben is busy. He is adding more blocks to the castle. He does not want to listen to Lily.

"No, Lily, no," he says. "We do not need a flag. We need more blocks. Go and find more blocks."

Lily is angry. She does not like how Ben talks to her. She thinks he is mean and bossy.

"Fine, Ben, fine," she says. "I will find more blocks. But I will also use the scarf as a flag. You will see. It will be great."

She goes and finds more blocks. She brings them to the castle. She helps Ben to add them. But she also takes the scarf and ties it to the top of the castle.

"There, Ben, there," she says. "Now we have a flag. Now our castle is perfect."

Ben looks up. He sees the scarf. He is shocked. He does not like it. He thinks it is ugly and silly.

Ben and Sam liked to play with paper. They could fold it into many shapes, like birds, boats, and hats. They had a big box of paper in their room, and they used it every day.

One day, they found a gear in the garage. It was shiny and round, with teeth on the edge. They wondered what it was for. They decided to take it to their room and play with it.

"Look, Sam, I can fold this paper around the gear, like this," Ben said. He wrapped a piece of paper tightly around the gear, and twisted it. "Now it looks like a wheel."

"Let me try, Ben," Sam said. He took another piece of paper and did the same thing. "This is fun. We can make a car with these wheels."

They made four paper wheels with gears inside, and attached them to a cardboard box. They drew windows and doors on the box, and made a steering wheel with a paper plate. They were very proud of their car.

"Let's go for a ride, Ben," Sam said. He climbed into the box, and held the steering wheel. "Beep beep, I'm the driver."

"OK, Sam, I'll be the passenger," Ben said. He got into the box, and sat next to Sam. "Vroom vroom, we're going fast."

They pushed the box along the floor, pretending to drive on the road. They made noises with their mouths, and laughed. They had a lot of fun.

But they did not see the cat. The cat was sleeping on the couch, and did not like the noise. The cat was angry, and jumped off the couch. The cat ran towards the box, and pounced on it.

The box tipped over, and the paper wheels broke. The gears fell out, and rolled away. The paper tore, and the cardboard bent. The car was ruined.

Ben and Sam cried. They were sad, and scared. The cat hissed, and scratched them. They had cuts, and blood. The car was gone.

Mom heard the noise, and came to the room. She saw the mess, and the cat, and the boys. She was worried, and mad. She picked up the boys, and took them to the bathroom. She cleaned their cuts, and put on bandages. She hugged them, and said:

"I'm sorry you got hurt, Ben and Sam. But you should not have taken the gear from the garage. It was not a toy. It was dangerous. You could have hurt yourself, or the cat, or the paper. You should have asked me first, before you played with it. You should have been careful, and respectful. Do you understand?"

Ben and Sam nodded. They felt sorry, and ashamed. They said:

"We're sorry, Mom. We did not know. We just wanted to have fun. We won't do it again. We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled, and said:

"I love you too, Ben and Sam. But you have to learn from your mistake. Next time, think before you act. And always ask for permission, before you use something that is not yours. That is the right thing to do. OK?"

Ben and Sam said:

"OK, Mom. We will."

Mom kissed them, and said:

"Good. Now, let's go and clean up the room. And then, we can make some new paper shapes. But no more gears, OK?"

Ben and Sam said:

"OK, Mom. No more gears."

The end.

Moral value: Ask for permission, before you use something that is not yours. Be careful, and respectful, with other people's things.

His mom said, "Of course, we can. Let's go outside and have some fun."

They put on their coats and went outside. They played with the ball and laughed. Tommy forgot about the new girl. He was happy with his mom.

Tim and Liz are two little pigs who live on a farm. They like to play in the mud and eat hay. One day, they see a big truck bring a lot of new hay to the barn. They run to the barn and see a pile of hay that is bigger than their house.

"Wow, look at all the hay!" Tim says. "Let's make a hay fort!"

"Good idea!" Liz says. "We can dig a tunnel and hide inside!"

They start to work on their hay fort. They pull and push and roll the hay until they have a big wall. Then they dig a hole under the wall and crawl inside. They make a cozy nest with some hay and smile at each other.

"We did it!" Tim says. "We made a hay fort!"

"We are the best hay builders!" Liz says. "This is our secret place!"

They hear a loud noise outside. They peek out of the hole and see a big machine with a long arm. The machine grabs some hay from the pile and puts it in the truck.

"Oh no!" Tim says. "The machine is taking our hay!"

"Stop!" Liz says. "That's our hay fort!"

They run out of the hole and try to stop the machine. They shout and wave and jump, but the machine does not see them. It keeps taking their hay and putting it in the truck.

"Help!" Tim says. "We need to save our hay fort!"

They look around and see an unusual thing. It is a red thing with wheels and a hose. It says "Fire" on the side.

"Look!" Liz says. "Maybe we can use that thing!"

They run to the red thing and climb on it. They find a button and press it. The hose starts to spray water everywhere.

"Wow!" Tim says. "This is fun!"

They aim the hose at the machine and the truck. They spray water on them and make them wet and dirty.

"Hey!" The machine driver says. "What are you doing?"

"Stop taking our hay!" Tim says. "This is our hay fort!"

The machine driver sees the two little pigs on the red thing. He is surprised and angry. He stops the machine and gets out. He walks to the red thing and tries to take the hose from them.

"Give me that hose!" He says. "You are making a mess!"

"No!" Liz says. "You are making a mess!"

They pull the hose and spray more water on him. He gets wet and slips on the mud. He falls down and groans.

"Ouch!" He says. "You naughty pigs!"

Tim and Liz laugh and cheer. They have saved their hay fort. They jump off the red thing and run back to the barn. They crawl into their hole and cuddle in their nest.

"We did it!" Tim says. "We finished our hay fort!"

"We are the best hay savers!" Liz says. "This is our secret place!"

They hug each other and fall asleep. They dream of hay and mud and water. They are happy.

Tom is a boy who likes to cut paper. He has many scissors and many colors of paper. He can cut shapes and letters and animals. He likes to make spells with his paper cuts. He thinks they are magic.

One day, Tom sees his dad in the bathroom. His dad is bald. He has no hair on his head. Tom thinks his dad needs some hair. He has an idea. He runs to his room and gets his scissors and paper. He cuts some yellow paper into long strips. He thinks they look like hair.

He goes back to the bathroom and sneaks behind his dad. He puts the paper strips on his dad's head. He says a spell: "Hair, hair, grow and shine. Make my dad look very fine." He thinks his spell will work.

But his dad feels something on his head. He turns around and sees Tom. He sees the paper strips. He is not happy. He says: "Tom, what are you doing? Why did you cut paper and put it on my head? That is not hair. That is a mess. You made a big mess."

Tom is scared. He says: "I'm sorry, dad. I wanted to help you. I wanted to give you hair. I made a spell. I thought it was magic."

His dad sighs. He says: "Tom, I love you, but you can't cut paper and put it on my head. That is not how you make hair. That is not how you make magic. You have to be careful with scissors. You have to ask before you use them. You have to clean up your mess."

Tom feels bad. He says: "I'm sorry, dad. I love you too. I will be careful. I will ask. I will clean up."

His dad smiles. He says: "Thank you, Tom. You are a good boy. But you know what? I don't need hair. I like being bald. I think it is cool. Do you like being bald?"

Tom thinks. He says: "No, I don't. I like my hair. It is brown and curly. It is like mom's hair."

His dad says: "That's right. You have mom's hair. And I have dad's hair. Or lack of hair. We are different, but we are both handsome. And we both love you. Now, let's go and clean up this paper. And maybe we can make some real magic later. How about that?"

Tom nods. He says: "OK, dad. That sounds fun. I love you, dad."

He hugs his dad. His dad hugs him back. They go and clean up the paper. They are happy. They are a family.

Lily liked to ride her bike. She had a pink bike with a basket. She put her doll in the basket and rode around the park. She saw many things: trees, flowers, birds, dogs, and people.

One day, she saw a big vase near a bench. It was blue and shiny. It had pretty flowers in it. Lily wanted to look at the vase. She parked her bike and went to the bench. She touched the vase. It was smooth and cold.

But the vase was not strong. It was fragile. When Lily touched it, it fell off the bench and broke. It made a loud noise. Lily was scared. She saw the flowers and the water and the pieces of the vase on the ground. She felt bad. She did not mean to break the vase.

She heard someone say, "Hey, what did you do?" It was a man. He was angry. He had put the vase on the bench. He liked the vase. He said, "That was my vase. You broke it. You are a bad girl."

Lily was sad. She wanted to say sorry, but she did not know how. She ran to her bike and rode away. She cried. She wished she had not touched the vase. She wished she had been more careful. She wished the man had been nicer. She wished she had her doll. But she had left her doll in the basket. She had lost her doll and the vase. She had a bad day.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big ball with spikes. It is red and shiny. They want to play with it.

"Can we have the ball?" Tom asks a man who is sitting on a bench. The man is reading a book.

"No, you can't. This is my ball. I work hard to buy it. It is not for kids. Go away," the man says. He is mean and rude.

Tom and Jen are sad. They go to another part of the park. They find a small ball with no spikes. It is blue and soft. They start to play with it.

"Can we play with you?" a girl and a boy ask them. They are nice and friendly.

"Sure, you can. This is our ball. We share it. It is for everyone. Come on," Tom and Jen say. They are kind and polite.

They have fun together. They throw the ball, catch the ball, and roll the ball. They laugh and smile.

The man who has the big ball with spikes sees them. He feels lonely and bored. He wishes he had friends to play with. He learns a lesson. He learns that being mean and rude makes no one like you. He learns that being kind and polite makes everyone like you. He learns that sharing is better than keeping. He learns that a small ball with no spikes can bring more joy than a big ball with spikes.

Sara liked to sing songs. She sang all the time. She sang in the morning, she sang at lunch, she sang at night. She sang loud and happy. She did not care if anyone else liked her songs.

Tommy did not like Sara's songs. He liked to play with his cars and trucks. He did not like loud noises. He did not like Sara. He thought she was bossy. She always told him what to do and what to play. He wanted to be alone.

One day, Sara came to Tommy's room. She saw his cars and trucks. She wanted to play with them. She said, "Tommy, let me play with your cars and trucks. They are fun. I will sing you a song while we play."

Tommy said, "No, Sara. Go away. These are my cars and trucks. I do not want to play with you. I do not want to hear your song. Your song is bad. It hurts my ears."

Sara did not listen. She grabbed a car and a truck. She started to sing. She sang louder and louder. She sang, "I am Sara, I am the best. I can play with anything I want. You are Tommy, you are not fun. You have to do what I say."

Tommy got angry. He tried to get his car and his truck back. He said, "Stop, Sara. Stop singing. Stop playing. Give me back my car and my truck. They are mine. You are not the best. You are mean and bossy."

Sara did not stop. She held the car and the truck tight. She sang louder and louder. She sang, "No, Tommy. No, no, no. I will not stop. I will not give you back. I will keep your car and your truck. They are mine now. You are silly and dumb."

Tommy got very angry. He could not take it anymore. He screamed. He screamed loud and hard. He screamed, "SARA, GO AWAY! LEAVE ME ALONE! I HATE YOU AND YOUR SONG!"

Sara got scared. She dropped the car and the truck. She ran away. She cried. She cried, "Tommy, why did you scream? Why did you hurt me? I just wanted to play and sing. I do not hate you. I like you."

Tommy did not care. He was happy. He had his car and his truck back. He did not want to play or sing with Sara. He wanted to be alone. He said, "Good. Go away, Sara. Do not come back. Do not sing anymore. Your song is the worst. I do not like you."

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. Spot was a big, brown dog with a leather collar. He liked to run and chase balls and sticks. Tom and Lily loved Spot very much.

One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a small, white cat with him. The cat had a pink bow on her head. She looked very pretty and soft. The boy was holding the cat in his arms.

"Hello," Tom said to the boy. "What is your name?"

"My name is Ben," the boy said. "This is my cat, Fluffy. She is very nice and harmless. Do you want to pet her?"

Tom nodded and reached out his hand. Fluffy rubbed her head against his fingers and purred. Tom smiled and said, "She is very cute."

Lily also wanted to pet Fluffy. She walked over to Ben and said, "Can I pet your cat too?"

Ben nodded and said, "Sure, you can. But be careful, she is very shy. She might scratch you if you scare her."

Lily was not scared. She loved animals and wanted to be friends with Fluffy. She gently stroked Fluffy's fur and said, "Hello, Fluffy. You are very pretty."

Fluffy seemed to like Lily too. She licked Lily's hand and snuggled in Ben's arms. Lily giggled and said, "She is very sweet."

Spot saw Tom and Lily petting Fluffy. He was curious and wanted to join them. He ran over to Ben and barked. He wanted to sniff Fluffy and play with her.

But Fluffy did not like Spot. She saw his big teeth and heard his loud bark. She was scared and angry. She hissed and spat at Spot. She scratched his nose with her claws.

Spot yelped and backed away. He was hurt and confused. He did not understand why Fluffy did not like him. He only wanted to be friendly.

Tom and Lily saw what happened. They ran over to Spot and hugged him. They said, "Poor Spot. Are you okay? Fluffy was mean to you. She is not harmless at all."

Ben saw what happened too. He felt sorry for Spot and said, "I'm sorry. Fluffy is not used to dogs. She is afraid of them. She did not mean to hurt him. She is harmless to people."

Tom and Lily looked at Ben. They were not happy with him. They said, "You should not bring your cat to the park. She is not nice to dogs. She is not harmless to Spot. Spot is our friend. We love him."

Ben looked at Tom and Lily. He was not happy with them. He said, "You should not let your dog run to my cat. He is too big and noisy. He scared her. She is my friend. I love her."

Tom and Lily and Ben did not agree. They started to argue. They said, "My pet is better than your pet. My pet is nicer than your pet. My pet is harmless and your pet is not."

They did not listen to each other. They did not try to understand each other. They only insisted on their own opinions. They were not nice to each other.

Spot and Fluffy watched Tom and Lily and Ben argue. They did not like to see them fight. They did not want to fight either. They wanted to be peaceful and happy.

Spot wagged his tail and licked his nose. He was not angry with Fluffy. He forgave her for scratching him. He wanted to be friends with her.

Fluffy calmed down and stopped hissing. She was not afraid of Spot. She saw that he was gentle and kind. She wanted to be friends with him too.

Spot and Fluffy moved closer to each other. They sniffed each other and touched noses. They made a friendly sound. They became friends.

Tom and Lily and Ben saw Spot and Fluffy being friends. They stopped arguing and looked at them. They felt ashamed and silly. They said, "Sorry. We were wrong. We should not fight. We should be friends too."

They smiled and hugged each other. They said, "Your pet is nice. Your pet is harmless. Your pet is your friend. And you are our friend too."

They played together in the park with Spot and Fluffy. They had fun and learned to respect each other. They were happy.

Sara and Ben like to play in the sand. They have a red bucket and a big shovel. They make a big hill of sand and put the bucket on top. They want to make a castle.

But then, a big dog comes. The dog is black and white and has a long tail. The dog likes to run and jump. The dog sees the red bucket and thinks it is a toy. The dog runs to the hill of sand and jumps on it.

Sara and Ben are scared. They shout at the dog. "No, no, bad dog! Go away!" But the dog does not listen. The dog bites the red bucket and pulls it off the hill. The bucket is cut by the dog's teeth. The sand falls down.

Sara and Ben are sad. They cry. They want their red bucket back. The dog runs away with the bucket. He thinks it is fun. He does not know he is bad.

A man sees what happens. He is the dog's owner. He calls the dog. "Rex, Rex, come here! Drop that bucket!" The dog hears the man and comes back. He drops the red bucket. The man picks it up and sees it is cut. He is sorry.

He goes to Sara and Ben and gives them the bucket. He says, "I'm sorry, kids. My dog is naughty. He did not mean to hurt your bucket. Here, take this. It is a new bucket. It is blue and shiny. You can make a new castle with it."

Sara and Ben stop crying. They look at the new bucket. It is nice. They say, "Thank you, mister. Thank you, Rex." They smile. They take the new bucket and the shovel. They go to a new spot of sand. They make a new hill and a new castle. They are happy.

Anna and Ben went to the big water place with Mom and Dad. They saw many fish and animals in the water. They liked the colors and shapes of the water animals. They saw a big tank with many jellyfish. The jellyfish were pink and blue and purple. They moved slowly and softly in the water. Anna and Ben thought they were charming.

"Can we touch them, Mom?" Anna asked.

"No, sweetie, they are not for touching. They can hurt you with their long arms. They have tiny things that can sting you and make you ouchy. You can only look at them, OK?" Mom said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They looked at the jellyfish some more. They wanted to touch them, but they listened to Mom. They saw a sign that said "Do not touch. Jellyfish display." They did not know what display meant, but they guessed it meant something like show.

They moved on to see other water animals. They saw a turtle, a shark, a starfish, and a seahorse. They liked them all, but they liked the jellyfish best. They wanted to go back to the jellyfish tank. They asked Mom and Dad if they could.

"OK, but only for a little bit. Then we have to go home. It's getting late," Dad said.

Anna and Ben ran back to the jellyfish tank. They saw that there was a small opening at the top of the tank. They wondered what it was for. They climbed on a chair and looked inside. They saw the water and the jellyfish. They were so close. They reached out their hands to touch them.

"Anna! Ben! Stop! Don't touch them!" Mom shouted.

But it was too late. Anna and Ben touched the jellyfish. They felt a sharp pain in their fingers. They screamed and pulled back their hands. They saw red marks and bumps on their skin. They cried and cried. Mom and Dad ran to them and hugged them. They called for help. A man came with a first aid kit. He put some cream and bandages on their fingers. He said they would be OK, but they had to be careful.

Anna and Ben learned a hard lesson. They should not touch the jellyfish. They should only look at them. They were charming, but they were also dangerous. They were sorry they did not listen to Mom. They went home with Mom and Dad. They were sad and sore. They did not like the jellyfish anymore. They liked the turtle best. The turtle was nice and safe. The turtle did not sting. The end.

One day, Lila's brother Tom came into her room. He was older and bigger than Lila, and he liked to tease her. He saw Rosie on the bed and grabbed her. He said, "This doll is ugly and stupid. You are a baby for playing with dolls. I will throw her in the trash."

Tom laughed and ran away with Rosie. Lila chased him, but he was faster. He reached the kitchen and threw Rosie in the garbage bin. Lila cried and tried to get Rosie out, but the bin was too high and heavy.

Lila's mother heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lila crying and Tom smiling. She asked them what happened. Lila told her everything. Tom said, "It was just a joke. She is too sensitive. It's only a doll."

Lila's mother was very angry with Tom. She said, "Tom, you are very rude and cruel. You hurt your sister's feelings and broke her toy. You owe her an apology and a new doll. You are not too old to learn how to be kind and respectful."

"Where is the water, Ben?" Anna asks, panting. "We need water in the desert!"

"I don't know, Anna," Ben says, looking around. "Maybe we can find a cactus. They have water inside."

"Can we drink from the cactus, Ben?" Anna asks, curious.

"I don't know, Anna," Ben says, doubtful. "It might hurt us. Maybe we should ask mom first."

She said, "You are very lucky to meet such a wonderful owl. Maybe you can visit him again someday."

Jill and Tom were friends. They liked to play outside in the sun. One day, they saw a big red truck. It was shiny and loud. They wanted to see it up close.

"Wow, look at that truck!" Tom said. "It is so attractive. I want to touch it."

"Me too," Jill said. "But we have to be careful. It might be hot."

They ran to the truck and looked at it. It had big wheels and a long hose. They saw a man in a yellow hat. He was a firefighter. He smiled at them.

"Hello, kids," he said. "Do you like my truck?"

"Yes, we do," Tom said. "It is the most attractive truck we ever saw."

"Thank you," the firefighter said. "Do you want to see inside?"

"Yes, please," Jill said.

The firefighter opened the door and let them in. They saw many buttons and levers. They saw a radio and a siren. They saw a helmet and a coat.

"This is where I sit and drive," the firefighter said. "And this is where I talk to other firefighters. And this is where I turn on the siren and the lights."

He turned on the siren and the lights. They made a loud noise and flashed. Jill and Tom laughed. They liked the siren and the lights.

The firefighter turned them off. He said, "Do you want to try on the helmet and the coat?"

"Yes, please," Tom said.

The firefighter gave them the helmet and the coat. They were big and heavy. Tom put on the helmet and Jill put on the coat. They looked at each other. They looked funny. They giggled.

The firefighter said, "You look like little firefighters. Do you want to be firefighters when you grow up?"

"Maybe," Jill said. "But it must be hard work."

"It is," the firefighter said. "But it is also fun and important. I help people and animals when there is a fire. I put out the fire and make them safe."

"That is very nice of you," Tom said. "You are a hero."

The firefighter smiled. He said, "Thank you. You are very sweet. But now I have to go. There might be another fire somewhere. Do you want to say goodbye to the truck?"

"Yes, please," Jill said.

They got out of the truck and hugged it. They said, "Goodbye, truck. Thank you for letting us see you. You are very attractive and cool."

The truck honked. It said, "You are welcome, kids. You are very cute and brave."

The firefighter got in the truck and waved. He said, "Goodbye, kids. Have a nice day. And remember, stay away from fire and smoke. They are very hot and bad."

"Goodbye, firefighter," Jill and Tom said. "Have a nice day. And thank you for being a hero."

They held hands and walked home. They yawned again. They said, "We had a great adventure. We saw an attractive truck and met a firefighter. Maybe we will dream about them."

They went home and took a nap. They dreamed about the truck and the firefighter. They smiled in their sleep. They were happy.

She calls her mom. She says, "Mom, can we go to Tom's home? He is in the flood. He is sad."

The moral of the story is: Friends comfort each other in times of trouble. Friends share what they have. Friends are better than regular things.

He waded out into the warm water and felt the waves against his feet. But suddenly, he felt a strong current, pushing and pulling him away from the reef. 

The little boy was scared, but he kept going. He swam against the current and eventually made it back to the reef. But it was too late. The tide had changed and the reef was now bitter and cold. He sighed and sat down in the sand, with his chin in his hands. 

The little boy was sad, but he knew there were some things he couldn't control. He tried to stay positive, stood up and smiled. He shrugged his shoulders and glanced back at the reef one last time, before heading back home.

As the sun began to set, Lily started to get scared. She knew she had to find her way back before it got dark. But she couldn't. She spent the whole night in the woods, cold and alone. The next morning, the rescue team found her, but it was too late. Lily had gotten very sick and she didn't make it.

"Of course," said her mom. "But first, we have to unpack your brain and get ready for the trip."

Lily was confused. "What does that mean?" she asked.

"It means we have to get everything we need for the trip ready in our heads," explained her mom. "We have to think about what we want to do and what we need to bring."

Lily thought hard and said, "I want to go swimming and eat ice cream. And I need my swimsuit and sunscreen."

"Great job, Lily!" said her mom. "You made it easy for us to pack."

On the day of the trip, Lily and Teddy were ready to go. They had everything they needed in their brains and in their bags. They had a fun time swimming and eating ice cream, just like Lily had planned. And when they got home, Lily's mom said, "See, unpacking your brain was easy, wasn't it?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy train on the rail in her backyard. One day, she saw her friend Emma playing with a different toy train.

Lily: "Emma, your train looks different. Can I play with it?"

Emma: "Sure, but you have to return it to me when you're done."

Lily happily played with Emma's train, but she accidentally broke it. She was scared to tell Emma, but she knew it was the right thing to do.

Lily: "Emma, I'm sorry. I broke your train. I will return it to you as soon as I can."

Emma: "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you told me the truth. That's what friends do. And don't worry, we can fix the train together."

The moral of the story is that it's important to be honest and to take responsibility for our actions, even if it's hard. And true friends are always willing to help and forgive.

Timmy quickly made a big castle and then his mom said, "Let's go, Timmy. We need to get you dry." Timmy ran to his mom and said, "I had so much fun making my castle. Can we come back to the shore tomorrow?" His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Timmy. We can come back to the shore anytime you want."

"Eww, get that creepy bug away from me!" he shouted.

"He's not creepy, he's my friend," Lily said.

"I don't care, bugs are gross," her brother replied.

Lily didn't want her brother to harm her harmless friend, so she picked up the caterpillar and put him on a leaf. "You stay here, I'll come back and check on you later," she said.

And so, Lily and her caterpillar friend continued to play in the yard, chewing on their gum and having a great time. The end.

"A temple is a place where people go to pray and thank God," Ben said. "My mom told me about it. She said there are many kinds of temples in the world."

"Wow," Lila said. "It looks very nice. Can we go inside?"

"I don't know, Lila," Ben said. "Maybe we should not. Maybe it is not for us."

"Why not, Ben?" Lila said. "Maybe God wants us to see it. Maybe He has a gift for us."

"Maybe, Lila," Ben said. "But we have to be humble. We have to be respectful. We have to ask first."

"OK, Ben," Lila said. "How do we ask?"

Ben thought for a moment. He remembered what his mom had taught him. He said, "We have to yield. We have to say, 'Please, God, can we see your temple? We are sorry if we bother you. We are grateful for your love. We are your children.'"

Lila nodded. She liked what Ben said. She repeated after him. They both closed their eyes and bowed their heads. They said, "Please, God, can we see your temple? We are sorry if we bother you. We are grateful for your love. We are your children."

They waited for a while. They did not hear anything. They did not feel anything. They opened their eyes and looked at each other.

"Did He answer, Ben?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, Lila," Ben said. "Maybe He did. Maybe He did not. Maybe He is busy. Maybe He is silent."

"Maybe He is happy, Ben," Lila said. "Maybe He is smiling. Maybe He is proud of us."

"Maybe, Lila," Ben said. "Maybe He is."

They smiled at each other. They felt warm and peaceful. They decided to go down the hill and tell their mom about the temple. They hoped to come back someday and see it again. They thanked God for their adventure. They were humble and happy.

Lily and Sam nodded. They learned their lesson. They went back to their sandcastle and played happily. They did not bother the jellyfish anymore. They were polite.

Once there was a bunny who loved to hop. He would hop around his den all day, daydreaming of hopping around the world. One day he decided to hop out of his den to explore.

Unfortunately the bunny had never seen a piano before and he was hopping too hard. Every time he hopped, the keys kept making loud and scary sounds. The bunny hopped faster and faster in fear and the piano's sounds kept getting louder and louder. Finally, the bunny hopped off as fast as he could, but it was too late. The sounds had disturbed a nearby bear who was sleeping under a nearby tree.

Joe carried a large bag and Pat carried a tent in her hands. They walked for a long time until they arrived at the camp.

But then something strange happened. A large group of wild animals gathered around them. They were very angry and they were growling at Joe and Pat.

The two friends were scared but Joe was brave. He tried to be kind and compassionate to the animals but it was no use.

In the end, the animals chased Joe and Pat away from the camp. They had to leave without their tent and bag. They were very sad but they had to keep moving. Joe and Pat never returned to the camp again.

Once upon a time, a nosy little boy named Jimmy was outside playing in the rain. It was really stormy, and lightning kept flashing in the sky. Jimmy liked it, and he kept pointing to the lightning.

"Mommy, look at the lightning! Look at the lightning!" Jimmy shouted. 

"I'm right here, Jimmy," Mommy replied. "But you should be careful! Lightning can be dangerous."

But Jimmy kept pointing and shouting. He pointed at the lightning and called out its name. Suddenly, a loud crash came from behind him.

Mommy gasped. "Oh no, Jimmy," she said. "Go inside right now. That might have been lightning!"

Jimmy was a little scared, but he wasn't too worried. He ran inside, happy to be out of the rain. From inside, Jimmy peeked out the window and kept pointing at the lightning. He wasn't as nosy as before, but he just couldn't help himself.

The butterfly told them about her ripped wings, and the ants decided that they could repair them.

One day, Polly and her mum were out in the garden. Polly saw something unusual poking out of the ground. It was a wire.

"Mummy, what is this wire?" asked Polly.

"It looks like part of a machine," her mum replied.

Polly gave the wire a tug and suddenly she heard a loud noise. A big truck came in and out of the truck came two mechanics carrying tools.

"What can we do for you?" asked the first mechanic.

"We need to reverse this wire," said her mum.

The mechanic pulled out a big wrench and spun it around the wire. He then said, "okay, it's clear now!"

The mechanics left and Polly and her mum went back inside. Polly asked her mum what the wire was, and she said it was part of an old machine.

Polly was glad that the wire was reversed and it was now clear to use.

The father said, "I had a tough day but I found a job that I could do and they gave me some money in return. But I have something even better to show you." 

He then reached back into his pocket and pulled out a shiny golden key. He said, "This will help us in the future. When the time comes, this key will reveal something very special."

The family was so excited that the father was able to get even more for his hard day's work. They couldn't imagine what could be hidden behind the key.

Some days later, the family found out what the key revealed. It opened up a secret, hidden chamber in their tiny house where a huge pile of money had been hidden for generations. This money made their lives so much easier, and it was all thanks to the father's tough day's work.

One day, Sam and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They liked to run and play and laugh.

"Look, Sam, a bee!" Lily said, pointing to a yellow and black insect on a red flower. "It is so pretty and small. Can we call it?"

Sam shook his head. "No, Lily, we cannot call the bee. The bee is busy. It is making honey for its friends. And the bee can sting. It can hurt us if we touch it."

Lily frowned. She wanted to call the bee and make friends with it. She thought the bee was lonely. She did not want to hurt the bee. She just wanted to say hello.

She moved closer to the flower and whispered, "Hello, bee. I am Lily. You are very pretty. Do you want to play with me?"

The bee heard Lily and flew away from the flower. It buzzed in the air and looked at Lily. It did not want to play with Lily. It wanted to find more flowers and more honey. It did not like Lily's voice. It was too loud and scary.

The bee flew towards Lily and tried to sting her. Lily screamed and ran away. She was scared and sad. She did not understand why the bee was angry.

Sam and mom heard Lily and ran to her. They hugged her and checked her for stings. They were glad that the bee did not hurt her.

"Lily, are you okay?" mom asked. "What happened?"

"I tried to call the bee, but the bee did not like me. It tried to sting me. Why, mom? Why did the bee not want to be my friend?" Lily asked, crying.

Mom wiped Lily's tears and smiled. "Lily, the bee is not a regular friend. The bee is a wild animal. It does not know how to talk or play with us. It only knows how to make honey and protect itself. It was afraid of you and thought you were a threat. You have to be careful and respectful of the bee and other animals. They have their own lives and rules. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She understood a little bit. She was still sad, but she was also curious. She wanted to learn more about the bee and other animals. She asked mom many questions and mom answered them. Sam listened and joined the conversation. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot.

They forgot about the bee and enjoyed the rest of the day at the park. They saw many other things and had many other adventures. They were happy and grateful. They loved each other and the world.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the snow. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to slide down the hill on their sleds.

"Let's go, let's go!" Lily urged Ben. "It will be fun!"

Ben was not sure. He saw that the hill was very steep and deep. He was afraid to slide too fast and get hurt.

"I don't know, Lily. It looks scary. Maybe we should find another hill," he said.

Lily did not listen. She pulled Ben by the hand and dragged him to the top of the hill. She put her sled on the snow and jumped on it.

"Come on, Ben! Don't be a baby!" she shouted.

Ben did not want to make Lily angry. He put his sled next to hers and sat on it. He held on tight and closed his eyes.

Lily and Ben slid down the hill very fast. They felt the wind in their faces and the snow under their sleds. They screamed with joy and fear.

But they did not see the big rock at the bottom of the hill. It was covered with snow and looked like a lump of coal. Lily and Ben crashed into the rock and flew off their sleds. They landed on the hard ground and felt a lot of pain.

They cried and cried. They had bruises and cuts on their bodies. They wished they had listened to Ben and found another hill.

A man who lived nearby heard their cries and came to help them. He took them to his house and gave them some hot chocolate and bandages. He told them that they were lucky they did not break any bones.

He also told them a story about a boy who did not listen to his sister and slid down a hill that was too steep and deep. He hit a tree and broke his leg. He had to stay in bed for a long time and missed all the fun.

Lily and Ben felt sorry for the boy. They also felt sorry for themselves. They realized that they had been foolish and reckless. They learned that they should be careful and listen to each other.

They thanked the man for his help and his story. They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They promised to be more wise and kind.

They went back to their house and told their mom what had happened. She was glad they were safe and learned a lesson. She hugged them and kissed them and told them she loved them.

They loved her too. They also loved the snow and the sleds. But they decided to wait until they found a hill that was not too steep and deep.

Ben and Lily liked to collect rocks. They had a big box full of rocks of different shapes and colors. They liked to look at them and make patterns with them. Sometimes they traded rocks with each other.

One day, they decided to go to the well in the woods. They heard that there were many shiny rocks at the bottom of the well. They wanted to see them and maybe take some home. They took a bucket and a rope with them.

When they got to the well, they looked inside. It was very dark and deep. They could not see any rocks. Ben said, "Let's lower the bucket and see what we can find." Lily said, "OK, but be careful. The well is very old and the rope is not very tough."

Ben tied the bucket to the rope and threw it into the well. He waited for a while and then pulled it up. He was excited to see what was inside. He opened the bucket and saw a big frog. The frog was green and slimy. It croaked loudly and jumped out of the bucket. Ben and Lily screamed and ran away.

They left the bucket and the rope behind. They did not want to go back to the well ever again. They decided that they had enough rocks in their box. They learned that some things are better left alone.

Mia and Leo are best friends. They love to play together in the park. One day, they see a big basket of fruit on a bench. There are apples, bananas, oranges and grapes. Mia and Leo are hungry and curious.

"Can we have some fruit?" Mia asks Leo.

"I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone," Leo says.

They look around, but they don't see anyone. The fruit looks yummy and juicy. Mia and Leo decide to take one apple each. They bite into the apples and smile.

"Mmm, this is so good!" Mia says.

"I agree. This is the best fruit ever!" Leo says.

They finish their apples and throw the cores in the trash. They are about to take another fruit, when they hear a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing with my fruit?" the voice says.

Mia and Leo turn around and see a lady with a big hat and a basket. She looks angry and surprised. Mia and Leo feel scared and sorry.

"We are sorry, lady. We were hungry and we saw your fruit. We only took one apple each. Please don't be mad," Mia says.

The lady looks at them and sees their adorable faces. She sees that they are honest and polite. She feels sorry for them and changes her tone.

"It's okay, kids. I understand. You can have some more fruit if you want. But next time, you should ask before you take something that is not yours. Do you understand?" the lady says.

Mia and Leo nod and say thank you. The lady smiles and gives them each a banana and a grape. Mia and Leo are happy and grateful. They eat the fruit and thank the lady again.

"Can we be your friends?" Mia asks the lady.

"Of course, you can. I'm Lila, by the way. What are your names?" the lady says.

"I'm Mia and this is Leo. We love fruit and we love you, Lila," Mia says.

Lila hugs them and says she loves them too. They become friends and share the fruit. They have a fun and sweet day in the park.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park, swing on the swings, and slide on the slide. One day, they saw a big tree with a rope. They wanted to climb the tree and swing on the rope.

"Can we try it, please?" Lily asked Ben.

"Okay, but be careful. The rope looks old and weak," Ben said.

Lily went first. She climbed the tree and grabbed the rope. She swung back and forth, feeling happy and free. But then, the rope broke and Lily fell to the ground. She hurt her knee and started to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts so much!" Lily sobbed.

Ben ran to her and hugged her. He saw her knee was bleeding and had a scratch.

"Don't cry, Lily. I'm here to support you. We'll go to the nurse and she'll make it better," Ben said.

He helped her stand up and walk to the nurse's office. The nurse cleaned her wound and put a band-aid on it.

"There you go, sweetie. You'll be fine soon. Just don't scratch it, or it will itch more," the nurse said.

"Thank you, nurse. And thank you, Ben. You're a good friend," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you're okay. Friends support each other, right?" Ben said.

They smiled and hugged. They learned that climbing trees can be fun, but also dangerous. They also learned that friends support each other when they are hurt or sad. They decided to play something safer next time, like catch or tag.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together in the park. One day, they find a new toy. It is a big ring with shiny stones. Anna puts it on her finger and says, "Look, Ben, I have a pretty ring. Do you like it?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, Anna, it is very pretty. Where did you find it?"

Anna points to a bench. "It was there, under a newspaper. Maybe someone forgot it. Can I keep it?"

Ben shrugs and says, "I don't know. Maybe it belongs to someone else. Maybe they will come back for it."

Anna shakes her head and says, "No, Ben, it is mine now. I like it too much. Do you want to marry me, Ben? Then we can share the ring."

Ben blushes and says, "Marry you, Anna? But we are too young. We are only three. And we don't have a cake or a dress or a priest."

Anna giggles and says, "We don't need those things, Ben. We only need the ring and our love. And we can have a cake later. Come on, Ben, say yes. It will be fun."

Ben thinks for a moment and says, "Okay, Anna, I will marry you. But only if you promise to be nice to me and share your toys and cookies."

Anna smiles and says, "I promise, Ben. And you have to be nice to me and share your toys and cookies too."

Ben agrees and they hug each other. Then they hear a loud noise. It is thunder. The sky is dark and the rain is coming. Anna and Ben run to the playground and hide under the slide. They hold hands and say, "We are married now. We are not afraid of the thunder. We have each other."

"Meow!" the cat said. It was stuck and wanted to come down.

"Wait here, I'll get a ladder!" Tom said. He ran to the shed and found a ladder. He brought it back and leaned it against the tree. Jill climbed up the ladder. She reached for the cat.

"Come here, kitty, don't be afraid!" Jill said. She smiled and put on her sunglasses. She thought they made her look cool.

But the dog did not like the sunglasses. He thought they were shiny and wanted to play with them. He jumped and bit the ladder. The ladder shook and fell. Jill and the cat fell too.

"Ow!" Jill said. She hit the ground and hurt her arm. The sunglasses broke and cut her face. The cat ran away and the dog chased it.

Tom ran to Jill and hugged her. He was sorry and scared. He cried and called for help.

Tom and Anna were impatient. They did not want to wait. They wanted to have fun. They decided to sneak out of the house and go to the creek by themselves. They thought their mom would not notice.

They ran to the creek and jumped in. They laughed and splashed and chased each other. They did not see the big dog that was watching them from the other side. The dog was hungry and angry. It barked and growled and ran towards them.

Tom and Anna were scared. They heard the dog and saw its teeth. They tried to get out of the water and run away. But the dog was faster and stronger. It caught Tom by his leg and bit him hard. Tom screamed and cried.

Anna ran to the house and called for their mom. She told her what happened. Their mom was worried and angry. She grabbed a stick and ran to the creek. She saw the dog and Tom. Tom and Anna felt sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to their mom and to each other. They promised to behave and to never go to the creek without their mom. They learned their lesson. They hoped the dog would not come back.

Anna liked to play in the garden with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a truck and a bear. She loved her toys very much and did not like to share them with anyone.

One day, a big black bird flew over the garden. It was a raven. The raven saw Anna's toys and wanted to have some fun. It swooped down and grabbed the doll with its beak. Then it flew away to a tall tree.

Anna was very angry and sad. She cried and shouted at the raven. "Give me back my doll! You are a bad bird! Go away!"

The raven did not listen. It laughed and said, "Ha ha ha! This is my doll now! You have too many toys! You are a greedy girl!"

Anna ran to the house and told her grandma what happened. Her grandma was elderly and kind. She hugged Anna and said, "Don't worry, my dear. The raven is just a silly bird. It does not know how to play nicely. Maybe it is lonely and bored. Maybe it needs a friend."

Anna thought about what her grandma said. She felt a little sorry for the raven. She said, "Grandma, can I try to talk to the raven? Maybe I can forgive it and share my toys with it."

Her grandma smiled and said, "That is very brave and generous of you, Anna. You can try, but be careful. The raven might not be friendly."

Anna took her ball and her truck and went back to the garden. She looked up at the tree and said, "Hello, raven. I am sorry I yelled at you. I know you like my doll, but it is very special to me. Can we share it? I have other toys you can play with. Do you want to be my friend?"

The raven was surprised and curious. It said, "Really? You are not angry with me? You want to share your toys with me? You want to be my friend?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I forgive you for taking my doll. But can you please give it back to me? I will let you play with it sometimes."

The raven thought for a moment. Then it said, "Okay, okay. You are a nice girl. I will give you back your doll. And I will play with your ball and your truck. And I will be your friend."

She hugged Tom, and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I was jealous of you, and I made a bad wish. I don't want to have all the crayons, I want to have you as my brother. Can you forgive me?"
