One day, Tom and Anna went to the park with their mom. They saw many squirrels on the trees and on the grass. Tom and Anna liked to watch the squirrels run and jump and eat nuts.

"Look, that squirrel has a big nut in its mouth!" Tom said.

"Maybe it is saving it for later," Anna said.

They saw a squirrel with a red hat on its head. It looked funny and cute.

"Who gave that squirrel a hat?" Tom asked.

"Maybe it found it on the ground," Anna said.

They went closer to the squirrel with the hat. The squirrel saw them and ran away. But it dropped the hat on the way.

Tom picked up the hat. It was a plastic hat with a flower on it.

"Hey, this is my hat!" Tom said. "I lost it last week when we came here. The squirrel took it!"

Anna laughed. "That squirrel was joking with you, Tom. It wanted to wear your hat and look like a flower."

Tom laughed too. He put the hat on his head.

"I'm glad I found my hat. It is important to me. It was a gift from grandma," Tom said.

Anna smiled. "You look nice with your hat, Tom. But I think the squirrel looked nicer."

They both giggled and hugged. They thanked the squirrel for the joke and the hat. Then they went to play with their mom. They had a fun day at the park.

Lily was a dog who liked to run and play. She had a red collar with her name on it. She lived with Tom, who was a boy who liked to hug and feed her. They were happy together.

One day, Lily saw a cat in the garden. She wanted to chase the cat and make it go away. She barked and ran after the cat, but the cat was fast and clever. It jumped over the fence and ran away. Lily was angry and sad. She wanted to catch the cat.

She saw a hole under the fence. She thought she could go through the hole and find the cat. She did not see the sign that said "Danger". She did not hear Tom calling her name. She went through the hole and ran to the other side.

But the other side was not a garden. It was a road with many cars and trucks. They were loud and fast and scary. Lily was afraid and confused. She did not know where to go. She tried to cross the road, but a big truck was coming. It did not see Lily. It hit her with a loud noise.

Lily felt a lot of pain. She was dizzy and could not move. She saw Tom running to her. He was crying and shouting. He picked her up and hugged her. He tried to speak to her, but she could not hear him. She closed her eyes and did not open them again. She was gone.

Tom and Lily were playing pirates in the garden. They had a big box that they pretended was a chest full of gold and jewels. They took turns to guard the chest from the other pirates.

"Arrr, I am the mighty Captain Tom, and this is my treasure!" Tom said, holding a wooden sword. "You will never take it from me, you scurvy dog!"

"Oh, yes I will, you sneaky rat!" Lily said, wearing a paper hat. "I am the brave Pirate Lily, and I have a secret plan to get the chest!"

Lily ran behind a bush and waited for Tom to look away. Then she jumped out and ran towards the chest. Tom saw her and chased after her.

"Stop, stop, stop!" Tom shouted. "You can't have the chest, it's mine!"

Lily reached the chest and tried to open it. But it was too heavy and hard for her. She pulled and pushed and kicked, but the chest did not move.

"Ha, ha, ha!" Tom laughed. "You can't open the chest, it's locked! You need a key, and I have it!"

Tom showed Lily a shiny metal key that he had hidden in his pocket. He ran to the chest and put the key in the hole. He turned the key and heard a click.

"Yay, I did it!" Tom said. "Now I can see the treasure!"

Tom lifted the lid of the chest and looked inside. But there was no gold or jewels, only dirt and worms and spiders.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck!" Tom screamed. "This is not treasure, this is garbage!"

Tom dropped the lid and ran away from the chest. He tripped over a rock and fell on the ground. He hurt his knee and started to cry.

Lily saw Tom crying and felt sorry for him. She ran to him and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Tom, I didn't know the chest was full of garbage," Lily said. "Are you okay?"

"No, I'm not okay," Tom said. "I wanted to see the treasure, but it was a trick. And I hurt my knee, and it's bleeding. And you're not my friend, you're a mean pirate!"

Tom pushed Lily away and ran to the house. He left Lily alone in the garden, with the chest and the garbage.

The dog looked at them and growled. It did not want to share the ball. It ran away with the ball, into a big house.

He saw a girl in the same place as the bird. She was wearing hearing aids in her ears. Bob noticed that the girl didn't hear the bird's chirping. She was deaf. 

Bob went over to the girl and said, "Hello".  The girl didn't answer. Bob wondered why she didn't reply.

He said again, "Hello". This time the girl looked at him and smiled. She pointed to the grass and said, "Bird!". Bob smiled, he understood. The girl was deaf, but she could still hear the bird chirping in the grass. Bob and the girl laughed together.

From that day on, Lily would give her mom a massage every night before bedtime. Her mom would always say, "Thank you, Lily. You are such a talented and gifted little girl." And Lily would sign and dance happily, knowing she made her mom feel good.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her room all day long. One day, her mom came in and said, "Lily, it's time to clean your room. It's very dusty in here."

Lily didn't want to clean her room because it made her uncomfortable. She didn't like to touch the dust. But her mom insisted, so Lily started to clean.

As she was cleaning, she leaned over to pick up a toy and accidentally knocked over a vase. It broke into a million pieces. Lily started to cry because she knew her mom would be upset.

But her mom didn't get mad. Instead, she hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. Let's clean it up together." From that day on, Lily learned that cleaning her room wasn't so bad after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she saw a tall tree and wanted to climb it. 

Lily asked her mommy, "Can I climb the tall tree?" 

Her mommy said, "Yes, but be careful." 

Lily started to climb the tree. She stood on a branch and looked around. She saw a bird's nest and wanted to see the eggs. She stretched her arms out and tried to reach the nest. 

But it was too high. Lily said, "I can't reach it." 

Her mommy said, "That's okay, Lily. You can try again tomorrow." 

Lily climbed down the tree and went home. She was happy because she stood on a tall tree and tried to stretch her arms to reach the nest.

Timmy's arm was too short to reach the cookie jar, so he asked his friend Teddy for help. Teddy recommended that they use a chair to stand on. Timmy climbed on the chair and reached for the cookie jar. 

But as he grabbed the jar, he lost his balance and fell off the chair. Timmy hurt his arm and the cookie jar broke into a million pieces. Timmy learned that sometimes it's better to ask a grown-up for help and not to take risks.

The lion had been shown that he didn't have complete control over the world. He tried to keep his rule, but he realised that he couldn't always win. The lion was now less harsh and his roar became quieter. But he still ruled the world, and made sure he was respected. And everyone who heard his roar still knew that the lion was the king of the jungle.

So that is the story of how the world got a lot more useful. Everyone was happy and the special person was happy too. He had finished the world.

Amy took out the nuts and showed them to the squirrel. The naughty squirrel stopped running and looked at the nuts. It came closer to Amy and took a nut from her hand. Now, Amy and the squirrel were friends.

They played together in the park, balancing on one foot and sharing the nuts. Amy was very happy to have a new friend. She knew that her good memory had helped her make a friend that day. And the naughty squirrel learned that sharing and playing with friends was more fun than being alone.

Ducky and Fancy Duck swam in the pond together. They had a lot of fun. Ducky and Fancy Duck became good friends. They played at the pond every day. And they lived happily ever after.

Tim and his friends decided to play with water balloons. They had so much fun throwing them at each other. But then, Tim found a fake water balloon. It was made of plastic and would not break. He thought it would be funny to throw it at his friend.

When Tim threw the fake water balloon, it hit his friend really hard. His friend started to cry. Tim felt bad and said, "I'm sorry. I didn't mean to hurt you."

Tim learned that it's not nice to trick his friends. He promised to always be kind and play fair. And from that day on, Tim and his friends only played with real water balloons. They had lots of fun and no one got hurt.

Lila said, "OK, mom. I will try to blink more often. How do I know when to blink?"

Her mom said, "You can blink whenever you feel like it, or you can follow a simple rule. Every time you turn a page, or every time the scene changes on the TV, you can blink your eyes. That way, you will blink enough and your eyes and brain will be happy."

Lila said, "That sounds easy, mom. Thank you for teaching me how to blink. I love you, mom."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. Now, let's go and read a book together. And don't forget to blink!"

The moral of the story is: Blinking is good for your eyes and your brain, and you should do it regularly.

Ben gasped. He looked at the worm, then at the cat, who was sleeping on the porch. He shook his head. "No, Lily, we can't do that. That is not nice. The cat might not like the worm. The worm might not like the cat. They might get sick or hurt."

"But it would be fun to see what happens." Lily said, still holding the worm. "Come on, Ben, let's try. It's just a worm."

Ben frowned. He did not think it was fun. He thought it was mean. He took the worm from Lily and put it back in the dirt. He said, "No, Lily, we are not going to try that. That is a bad idea. We should be kind to the worm and the cat. They are living things, like us. They have feelings, too."

Lily pouted. She did not understand why Ben was so serious. She thought he was boring. She said, "Fine, Ben, you are no fun. I'm going to play with something else."

Ben sighed. He wished Lily would be more careful and respectful. He said, "Okay, Lily, you can play with something else. But please don't hurt any bugs or animals. They are our friends, not our toys."

He hoped Lily would listen to him. He hoped the worm and the cat would be okay. He hoped they could still be friends, too.

"Come on, Tom, don't be silly. Broccoli is not yucky or icky. It is a vegetable and it has vitamins. You need vitamins to grow big and strong," mom said.

"Look, Tom, you are a fairy dinosaur. You have broccoli dust on you. You can fly and do magic," Lily said.

Tommy was sick. He had a bad cough and a sore throat. Mommy gave him some medicine to make him feel better. She said he had to take it every day until he was well.

One day, Tommy went to play with his friend Lily. They had fun with their toys and their books. But Tommy forgot to take his medicine before he left. He did not remember until he saw the clock on the wall.

"Oh no!" Tommy said. "I forgot my medicine! Mommy will be mad at me!"

Lily looked at him. "What medicine?" she asked.

Tommy felt embarrassed. He did not want to tell Lily he was sick. He thought she would not like him anymore. He tried to change the topic.

"Let's play with the blocks," he said.

But Lily was curious. She wanted to know more about Tommy's medicine. She asked him again.

"What medicine, Tommy? Why do you need it? Is it yucky?"

Tommy did not know what to say. He wished he had taken his medicine before he came. He wished Lily would stop asking him. He wished he was not sick.

He started to cry. He felt sad and scared.

Lily saw Tommy crying. She felt sorry for him. She did not mean to make him upset. She wanted to help him.

She gave him a hug. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I'm your friend. I don't care if you're sick. I still like you. You can tell me about your medicine. Maybe I can remind you to take it next time."

They hugged again. They played with the blocks. They forgot about the medicine for a while. They were happy.

Rex wagged his tail and licked their faces. He thought they were happy to see him. He knocked over the chest and the gold. He bit the shark and the map. He made a big mess.

Sam and Mia were not happy. They were angry and sad. They had worked hard to make their pirate ship and their treasure. They did not want Rex to ruin it.

Tom threw the ball first. He threw it hard and high. The ball flew over the palm tree and landed on the other side. Lily ran to get it. She caught the ball and threw it back to Tom. She threw it hard and high too. But the ball hit one of the leaves and bounced back. It fell into the pond with a splash.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "The ball is in the water. How can we get it?"

Sam was very happy and played with the toy car all day. When it was time for Sam to go home, he remembered what Tim had said. Sam carefully gave the toy car back to Tim and thanked him for letting him borrow it.

Tim's mom saw this and smiled. She said, "Tim, you are a good friend for sharing your toys. It's important to be kind and generous with others."

And so, Tim learned the value of sharing and being a good friend. He continued to share his toys with his friends, and they all played happily together in their small town.

But the dog was not nice. It barked very loud and scared Tim. Tim ran back to his mom, crying. They went home to their small room. Tim did not want to go to the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play in the park. One day, he saw a girl named Sue. Sue was sad. She wanted to play in the sand, but she did not have a towel to sit on.

Tim had an idea. "I can borrow a towel from my mom," he said. "It's easy!" So, Tim ran home and asked his mom, "Mom, can I borrow a towel for Sue to sit on?" His mom said, "Yes, you can borrow a towel."

Tim took the towel back to the park. Sue was very happy. They put the towel on the sand and played together all day. They built a big sandcastle and had lots of fun. From that day on, Tim and Sue became best friends.

The sun was hot and the bird felt tired. She began to flap her wings, but one of them felt sharp. She thought it was strange, so she stopped. She looked at her wings and noticed that the green one was sharp.

She asked, "What happened?"

The wind blew softly and whispered, "Different wings that do different things."

The bird was amazed. She tried her sharp green wing and flew faster than ever before. She felt so free and happy. From then on, she was able to use her two different wings to make each flight special.

Once upon a time, there was a huge pear tree in the middle of a large field. One day, a small bunny crawled out from the tall grass. The bunny hopped over to the tree and looked up. He saw a gigantic, juicy pear, dangly from one of the branches.

The bunny hopped excitedly around the tree, eager to get the sweet treat. But, it was too high to reach. Then, the bunny had an idea. He began to crawl up the trunk, ever so slowly. He got closer and closer until he was reaching out for the pear.

Just as the bunny was about to take a bite, an angry voice boomed out from behind the tree. "Hey! Who said you could have my pear!" 

The bunny jumped back in surprise, to see a huge bear standing on his hind legs, frowning down at him. "Um, I'm sorry," stammered the bunny. "It's just that it looked so delicious and I just wanted a little bite."

The bear thought for a moment, then smiled down at the little bunny. "Well all right, but you get only one bite, OK?"

The bunny felt very relieved and thanked the bear, before taking a big bite of the juicy pear. He savoured the sweet taste and thanked the bear again, before crawling back down the trunk and hopping away. And the bear enjoyed the rest of the pear.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a big tree. Every day, he would look at the clock to see what time it was. One day, a little rabbit came to visit him.

"I'm looking at the clock," replied the owl. "It tells me when it's time to go to sleep."

The rabbit looked at the clock too. "Can I come back and visit you tomorrow?" he asked.

"Of course!" said the owl. "You can come back anytime you like."

But every time she tried, the stick didn't work. The mud was too thick, and it was impossible to move. So the little girl went home feeling discouraged and dirty.

But then the next day, she came back with a plan. She used her sharp stick to dig deeper, and soon the mud wasn't so thick anymore.

She moved closer to the pond, and at last she was able to get a closer look! She smiled with joy. From then on, she was never afraid to explore with her sharp stick.

After swimming, Leo always had a nice shower. He'd let the warm water run down his face, his belly, his legs and his arms. He'd soap himself up and then poke his head out of the shower to smile and laugh. He felt so refreshed after a shower.

Leo's parents thought he was an adorable little boy. They watched him swimming and playing in the pool and taking his shower with a big grin on his face. Leo was a very happy little boy.

Once upon a time, there was a furry little dog called Polly. Polly was curious and liked to wander around.
One day while she was exploring, she came across a pine. The pine was tall and strong. Polly was intrigued and decided to poke it. She poked it with her nose and with her paws. She poked it as hard as she could.
Suddenly, the pine began to move. Polly backed away in shock, but to her surprise, the pine started to sprout wings! Polly was amazed. Eventually, the pine became a beautiful butterfly and flew away into the sky. 
Polly was so happy that she had given this little creature a chance to fly! From that day on, Polly made sure to always be kind to creatures she found in the forest.

One day, the oat farmer was walking through his field when he heard a strange sound. He stopped and listened closely. It sounded like singing!

The farmer followed the sound and found a blue bird sitting in a tree. The bird was singing a beautiful song. It wanted to include the farmer in its happiness.

The farmer smiled and said, "Thank you bird for singing. I love it. I can't hear you, though. I'm deaf."

The bird understood and decided to give the farmer a special gift. From that day on, the farmer was able to feel the sound of the birds singing. He even said it was like music in his heart. The farmer was so happy.

Jeff hopped closer, and he saw that a thick thorn bush had trapped her! She couldn't move and she was in a lot of pain.

Jeff knew he had to help. He ran as fast as his little legs could carry him to his home. He gathered some tools and ran back to the clearing. Carefully he started to pull the thorns away and free the baby deer.

After what seemed like hours, he finally freed her! But Jeff had suffered some cuts and scrapes while he did it.

He helped the baby deer get to her feet, and then watched as she bounded off! Jeff couldn't help but smile, knowing he'd done something good.

The jellyfish learned an important lesson - it's important to always be polite and kind. And if you do, you never know what may come your way.

Anna likes the rocket, but she has another idea. She points to the bottom of the box. "This is where we go to the sea!" She says. She draws some fish and waves on it. She wants to play mermaids.

Tim and Anna take turns to go inside the box. They make noises like rockets and mermaids. They have fun, but the box is small and hard. They feel uncomfortable after a while.

"Tim, I'm tired of the box. It's too hot and tight. Can we play something else?" Anna asks.

"Me too, Anna. The box is not very cozy. Let's play with the teddy bears. They are soft and cuddly." Tim agrees.

They leave the box and pick up their teddy bears. They hug them and talk to them. They are happy and comfortable. They forget about the box.

Tim and Lily were playing with their paper dolls in the garden. They liked to make them dance and sing and have fun. They had many paper dolls, but their favorite ones were Tom and Molly, who wore jolly hats and dresses.

One day, a big wind came and blew their paper dolls away. Tim and Lily ran after them, but they could not catch them. They saw Tom and Molly flying in the air, higher and higher, until they reached a cliff. The cliff was very high and steep, and had rocks and trees on it.

"Tom! Molly! Come back!" Tim and Lily shouted. They climbed the cliff, but it was hard and scary. They had to hold on to the rocks and the trees, and be careful not to slip. They hoped that Tom and Molly were safe and not hurt.

When they reached the top of the cliff, they saw Tom and Molly lying on the ground. They were torn and dirty, and their jolly hats and dresses were gone. Tim and Lily felt very sad and sorry. They picked them up and hugged them.

"We are sorry, Tom and Molly. We did not mean to lose you. We love you very much," they said.

Tom and Molly smiled and said, "We love you too, Tim and Lily. We are happy that you found us. We are still your paper dolls, even if we are torn and dirty. You can make us new hats and dresses, and we can play again."

Tim and Lily nodded and smiled. They were glad that Tom and Molly were not angry or sad. They took them back to the garden, and made them new hats and dresses. They played with them again, and had a lot of fun. They also made sure to keep them safe from the wind. They were a jolly paper doll family.

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. They have a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Tom has a big truck and Mia has a doll. They share their toys and take turns.

Suddenly, they hear a loud bang from the kitchen. They look at each other and wonder what it is. They run to the kitchen and see their mom holding a broken plate. She looks sad and says, "Oh no, I dropped the plate and it broke. It was my favorite plate."

Tom and Mia feel sorry for their mom. They want to help her. They look around and see a roll of tape on the counter. They have an idea. They grab the tape and go to the broken plate. They try to stick the pieces together with the tape. They work hard and make the plate look like before.

They show the plate to their mom and say, "Look, mom, we fixed the plate. It is fine now. Don't be sad." Their mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "Thank you, Tom and Mia. You are very sweet and clever. The plate is not fine, but it is special. It has your love on it. I will keep it forever." Tom and Mia are happy. They love their mom and their tape.

Lily liked to play with her toy car. It was red and shiny and made noises when she pushed a button. But one day, the car stopped making noises. Lily was sad. She asked her mom, "Why is my car quiet?"

Mom looked at the car and said, "The car needs a new battery. A battery is a thing that gives power to the car. Power makes the car go and make noises. We can go to the store and buy a new battery later."

Lily nodded, but she wanted to play with her car now. She had an idea. She said, "Mom, can I imagine that my car has a new battery?"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course you can, Lily. Imagining is a fun way to play. You can imagine anything you want."

Lily picked up her car and closed her eyes. She imagined that her car had a new battery. A powerful battery that made the car go fast and make loud noises. She imagined that she was driving the car on a big road with other cars and trucks. She imagined that she was honking the horn and waving to the people. She imagined that she was having a lot of fun.

Lily opened her eyes and smiled. She said, "Mom, I imagined that my car had a new battery. It was powerful and fun. Can you imagine with me?"

Mom said, "Sure, Lily. I can imagine with you. Let's play together." She picked up another toy car and joined Lily. They imagined that they were having a great adventure with their cars. They laughed and talked and enjoyed their playtime.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make dishes with the toy food and pots. Lily made a dish with pasta, cheese and peas. She put it on a big plate and said, "This is my dish. It is very impressive. Do you want some?"

Ben looked at the dish and shook his head. He did not like peas. He made a dish with bread, jam and bananas. He put it on a small plate and said, "This is my dish. It is very impressive. Do you want some?"

Lily looked at the dish and made a face. She did not like bananas. She said, "No, thank you. Your dish is not impressive. It is silly. My dish is better. You should try it."

Ben said, "No, thank you. Your dish is not impressive. It is yucky. My dish is better. You should try it."

They both crossed their arms and turned away from each other. They were angry and sad. They did not want to play anymore.

Mom came into the kitchen and saw the dishes and the children. She smiled and said, "Wow, you made some impressive dishes. They look very yummy. Can I try some?"

Lily and Ben looked at Mom and then at each other. They felt a little sorry for being mean. They nodded and said, "Yes, you can try some."

Mom took a fork and a spoon and tasted both dishes. She said, "Mmm, they are both very good. You are both very good chefs. You have different tastes, but that is okay. You can like different things and still be friends. Can you accept each other's dishes and share?"

Lily and Ben thought about it and said, "Yes, we can accept each other's dishes and share."

They gave each other a hug and said, "Sorry for being mean. You are my friend."

Mom said, "That's very nice. I'm proud of you. Now, how about we make a new dish together with some of your favorite things?"

Lily and Ben said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun."

They helped Mom make a new dish with pasta, cheese, jam and bananas. They put it on a big plate and said, "This is our dish. It is very impressive. Do you want some?"

Mom said, "Yes, I do. Thank you for sharing. You are very impressive."

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play music. They had a band with a drum, a guitar and a flute. They played songs for their family and friends and had fun.

One day, they saw a poster for a music contest. The poster said: "Do you have a band? Do you want to win a prize? Come and play at the park on Saturday. The best band will get a big trophy and a cake!"

Tom and Sue wanted to join the contest. They practiced their songs every day. They were very excited.

On Saturday, they went to the park with their band. There were many other bands there. Some had big instruments and loud voices. Some had fancy clothes and shiny hats. Tom and Sue felt a little scared.

They waited for their turn to play. The sky was gloomy and dark. It looked like it was going to rain. Tom and Sue hoped it would not rain.

When it was their turn, they went on the stage. They smiled at the people who were watching. They started to play their first song.

But then, something bad happened. The wind blew hard and knocked over their drum. The drum rolled away and hit a tree. The guitar string broke and made a loud noise. The flute fell out of Sue's mouth and landed on the ground.

Tom and Sue stopped playing. They felt sad and embarrassed. They wanted to cry.

They heard some people laughing at them. They heard some people saying mean things. They felt like giving up.

But then, they heard a voice. It was their teacher, Mr. Lee. He was one of the judges for the contest. He said: "Don't worry, Tom and Sue. You can still play. Just pass me the drum, I'll fix it. And here, take this guitar and this flute. They are mine, but you can use them. You have a good band, and you have a good spirit. Don't let a little wind stop you. Try again, and have fun!"

Tom and Sue looked at Mr. Lee. They felt happy and grateful. They said: "Thank you, Mr. Lee. You are very kind. We will try again, and we will have fun!"

They passed him the drum, and took the guitar and the flute. They played their songs again, with more confidence and joy. They made the people clap and cheer. They made the sun come out from behind the clouds.

They did not win the contest, but they did not mind. They had a good band, and they had a good friend. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but they can always try again, and have fun. They learned that music is not about winning, but about sharing and enjoying. They learned that kindness is more valuable than a trophy or a cake.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play together. One day, they decided to play restaurant. Sara was the cook and Tom was the waiter. They used their toys and dishes to make pretend food and drinks.

Tom took a tray and went to serve their mom, who was reading a book on the couch. He said, "Hello, mom. Welcome to our restaurant. What would you like to order?"

Mom smiled and played along. She said, "I would like a cup of tea and a slice of cake, please."

Tom nodded and went back to the kitchen. He told Sara what mom wanted. Sara looked at their toys and dishes. She saw a red ball, a blue cup, a yellow plate, and a green block. She thought, "I can make tea and cake with these things. They are the same colors."

She put the red ball on the yellow plate and said, "This is the cake." She filled the blue cup with water and said, "This is the tea." She gave them to Tom and said, "Here you go. Be careful, they are hot."

Tom took the tray and went to serve mom. He said, "Here is your tea and cake, mom. Enjoy."

Mom looked at the tray and saw the ball, the cup, the plate, and the block. She thought, "This is crazy. How can these be tea and cake?" But she did not want to hurt their feelings. She said, "Thank you, Tom. This looks delicious."

She pretended to sip the water and bite the ball. She said, "Mmm, this is the best tea and cake I ever had. You and Sara are very good at cooking and serving."

Sara and Tom were happy. They said, "Thank you, mom. We are glad you like it. You are the best mom ever."

Mom hugged them and said, "You are the best twins ever. I love you both very much. You know, it does not matter what you use to make tea and cake. What matters is that you use your imagination and have fun. That is the value of playing."

Sara and Tom learned a lesson. They learned that playing is valuable and fun. They also learned that mom is very kind and crazy. They laughed and played some more.

Tom did not like to play with the doll. He wanted to play with the car. He said, "No, Sara. I want to play with the car. You play with the doll. You do not tell me what to do."

She did not see the nail that was stuck in the rag. She cut the nail with the scissors, and the scissors broke. A piece of metal flew into Sara's eye.

Sara screamed and dropped the scissors and the rag. She felt a lot of pain in her eye. She could not see well. She felt dizzy and fell to the floor. Her mom heard her scream and ran to her. She saw the blood and the metal in Sara's eye. She was very scared and sad.

She called the doctor and took Sara to the hospital. The doctor took out the metal and gave Sara a bandage. He said Sara was lucky that the metal did not damage her eye too much. He said she would need to rest and take medicine for a while. He also said she should never play with scissors again.

Sara learned a hard lesson that day. She realized that scissors were not toys, and that she should listen to her mom. She said sorry to her mom and hugged her. She promised to be more careful and obey the rules. She also said she would not cut her hair anymore. She hoped her eye would get better soon.

Mia and Ben were playing with their snowman in the garden. They had made him with a big ball of snow for his body, a smaller ball for his head, a carrot for his nose, and two buttons for his eyes. They had also given him a hat, a scarf, and a broom.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Mia said. "You are our friend. We like you very much."

"Yes, we do," Ben agreed. "You are the best snowman ever. You are very cold and white and round."

But then, the sun came out from behind the clouds. It was very bright and warm. The snow started to melt. Mia and Ben saw drops of water falling from the snowman's hat and scarf. His nose and eyes became loose. His broom fell to the ground.

"Oh no!" Mia cried. "Mr. Snowman is melting! He is going away!"

"Stop, sun, stop!" Ben shouted. "Don't hurt our snowman! He is our friend. He is our owner. We belong to him."

"Please, Mr. Snowman, don't leave us," Mia whispered. "We love you. We will miss you."

The snowman could not speak, but he felt their love. He smiled with his carrot mouth. He was happy to have had such good friends. He wished he could stay with them, but he knew he had to go. He was made of snow, and snow cannot last forever. He was not afraid. He was ready to become part of the water and the earth and the air. He hoped to see Mia and Ben again, maybe next winter, when the snow would come back. He closed his button eyes and said goodbye.

Tom does not listen to Mia. He says, "You are just scared, Mia. I am not scared. I am the best rider in the park." He rides faster and faster with no hands. He does not see the big rock on the path. He hits the rock and falls off his bike. He scrapes his knee and cries.

Mia stops her bike and runs to Tom. She says, "Are you okay, Tom? I told you to hold the handle. You were not careful." She helps him get up and gives him a hug.

Tom feels sorry and says, "You were right, Mia. I was not careful. I was not the best rider. I was silly and proud. I should be humble and listen to you. Thank you for helping me." He holds the handle of his bike and walks with Mia. They go to find their mom and dad and tell them what happened.

"Can I borrow your blue marble, Ben?" Lily asked.

"No, it is mine. You have your own marbles," Ben said.

"Please, Ben, just for a little while. I will give it back to you," Lily begged.

"No, no, no. Go away, Lily. You cannot have my blue marble," Ben shouted.

Lily felt sad and angry. She thought Ben was not a good friend. She decided to take his blue marble when he was not looking. She waited until Ben was busy with his other marbles. Then she quickly grabbed the blue marble and ran away.

Ben saw what Lily did. He was very mad. He chased after Lily and yelled, "Give me back my blue marble, Lily. You are a bad friend. You are a thief."

Lily ran faster and faster. She did not want to give back the blue marble. She thought it was very pretty. She ran to the playground and hid behind the slide.

Ben followed her to the playground. He looked for her everywhere. He saw her behind the slide. He ran to her and tried to take the blue marble from her hand.

Lily and Ben pulled and pushed each other. They both wanted the blue marble. They did not care about hurting each other. They did not care about sharing.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. They turned around and saw a big dog. The dog was hungry and curious. He saw the blue marble in Lily's hand. He thought it was a tasty ball. He jumped on Lily and Ben and snatched the blue marble from them.

Lily and Ben were scared and shocked. They let go of the blue marble and the dog. They watched the dog run away with the blue marble in his mouth.

They looked at each other. They felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had been silly and mean. They had lost their blue marble and their friendship.

They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I'm sorry, Lily. You are my friend. Can we share our marbles?"

"Yes, we can. We have many marbles. We can play together. We can be happy," they said.

They smiled and went back to their marbles. They forgot about the blue marble and the dog. They learned to be kind and fair. They were friends again.

Mom took Bella to the bathroom and gave her a bath. She used a special soap that made the fleas go away. Bella did not like the water, but she knew Mom was trying to help. She let Mom wash her and rinse her.

After the bath, Mom dried Bella with a towel and gave her a hug. "There, you are clean and flea-free now. How do you feel?" she asked. Bella licked Mom's face and wagged her tail. She felt much better. She was not itchy anymore.

"Thank you, Mom. You are very helpful. You comfort me when I am sad," said Bella. Mom smiled and petted Bella. "You are welcome, Bella. You are a good dog. I love you," said Mom. Bella snuggled with Mom and felt happy. She was glad to have a family who cared for her.

Freddy replied, "Thank you, Lily! I like being purple. It makes me stand out from the other frogs." 

Suddenly, Lily noticed something sharp on a rock near the pond. She said, "Oh no! That rock is sharp. You might hurt yourself, Mr. Frog." 

Freddy hopped over to the rock and saw the sharp edge. He said, "Thank you for telling me, Lily. I'll be careful and avoid that rock from now on." 

Lily and Freddy became good friends and would often chat by the pond. Freddy was happy to have a friend who cared about his safety.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he was playing in the park when he saw a little bird with a broken wing. Timmy wanted to help the bird, but he didn't know how. 

Just then, an old man walked by and saw Timmy looking sad. "What's wrong?" the old man asked. Timmy pointed to the bird and said, "It's hurt. I want to help it, but I don't know how." The old man smiled and said, "I promise I can help. Let's go get a box to put the bird in." 

Timmy was so happy that someone was going to support him in helping the bird. They found a box and brought the bird home. Timmy's mom helped them take care of the bird and soon it was all better. 

But one day, Timmy forgot to close the window and the bird flew away. Timmy was so sad, but the old man reminded him that they did their best to support the bird and keep it safe. Timmy learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but it's important to keep trying and keep your promises.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a voice. "Hey Timmy, I'm up here!" It was his friend, Billy. Timmy looked up and saw Billy on a great big tree. "Wow, Billy! You're so high up! How did you get up there?" Timmy asked. "I used a whip to help me climb," Billy replied.

Timmy was amazed. He had never seen anyone climb a tree with a whip before. "That's great, Billy! Can you teach me how to do it too?" Timmy asked. Billy climbed down from the tree and showed Timmy how to use the whip. Timmy tried it and found that it was really fun. From that day on, Timmy and Billy would often climb trees together using their whips.

One night, Timmy went to bed without removing the cell from his toy. While he was sleeping, the cell started to leak and the toy caught on fire. Timmy woke up to a lot of smoke and was very scared. His mom came to his room and saw what happened. She quickly removed the toy and cell from Timmy's room and put out the fire.

Timmy's mom explained to him that he should always remove the cell from his toys before going to bed, so they won't catch on fire. Timmy learned his lesson and promised to always remove the cell from his toys before going to bed. The moral of the story is to always be careful with things that have cells inside them.

One day, Tom saw a new animal on the farm. It was a big, brown cow with horns and a long tail. Tom was curious and wanted to say hello, but the cow did not look friendly. She mooed loudly and stamped her feet, and Tom felt scared.

"Who are you?" Tom asked the cow.

"I am Bessie, and this is my home now," the cow said. "Your family bought me from the market, and they are going to make steak out of me."

Tom did not believe the cow. He thought she was lying to make him go away. He loved his family, and he knew they would never hurt an animal.

"That's not true," Tom said. "My family is kind and good. They give me steak every day, and they love me. They would never make steak out of you."

The cow laughed and shook her head. "You are a silly dog," she said. "You don't know where steak comes from, do you? Steak is cow meat, and I am a cow. Soon, your family will take me to the barn, and then you will never see me again."

Tom felt confused and sad. He did not want to lose his new friend, but he also did not want to stop eating steak. He did not know what to do.

The next day, Tom did not see the cow on the farm. He looked everywhere, but he could not find her. He asked the other animals, but they did not know where she was. He hoped she was hiding somewhere, and that she would come back soon.

That night, his family gave him a big piece of steak for dinner, as usual. Tom smelled the steak, and it smelled good. But he also remembered the cow, and her words. He wondered if the steak was really her meat, and if she was gone forever.

Tom did not feel hungry anymore. He pushed the steak away, and lay down on his bed. He wished he could see the cow again, and tell her he was sorry. He wished he could believe that steak was not cow meat, and that his family was not bad. He wished he could be happy again.

Tom and Ben try to move faster. They want to beat Rex and each other. They do not look where they are going. They bump into each other. They fall down. Rex keeps running. He crosses the line. He wins the race. He barks and wags his tail. He is happy.

Tom and Ben are not happy. They are angry and sad. They blame each other. They say, "You pushed me!" and "You tripped me!" They start to fight. They do not see Rex coming back. Rex sees them fighting. He does not like it. He runs to them and licks their faces. He tries to make them stop.

Tom and Ben feel Rex's tongue. They stop fighting. They look at Rex. They see his big eyes and his wet nose. They remember how much they love him. They feel sorry. They hug Rex. They hug each other. They say, "Sorry, Rex. Sorry, brother. You are both good runners. We are both good friends."

Tom and Ben learn a lesson. They learn that being competitive is not always good. They learn that being kind and fair is better. They learn that playing with Rex is more fun than fighting with each other. They decide to play with Rex again. They throw the ball for him. They cheer for him. They laugh and have fun. They are happy. Rex is happy. The end.

After a while, Lily started to feel tired. "Buttercup, can we relax for a bit?" she asked. Buttercup stopped and Lily lay down on her back. They looked up at the blue sky and watched the clouds go by. Lily felt happy and peaceful.

Soon, it was time for Lily to go back to the house. She said goodbye to Buttercup and ran back to her mom. "I had so much fun playing with Buttercup!" she said. "I also relaxed and saw the clouds. It was beautiful!" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you had a good time, Lily."

Lily was very sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she saw a little light peeking out from under the couch. She crawled over and saw that her pin was stuck in between the cushions. She was so happy to have found it!

Just as she was about to grab it, her little brother came over and tried to take the pin from her. They started to fight over it and the pin fell back down onto the ground. Lily was upset again, but then she remembered the light she saw earlier.

She crawled back under the couch and found her pin again. This time, she made sure to hold onto it tightly and not let anyone take it away from her. From then on, she kept her pin safe and never lost it again.

Remy's friend, Tim the turtle, saw him feeling hot. Tim warned Remy, "You should not play in the sun all day. You need to find some shade to stay cool." Remy listened to his friend and they both went to look for a big tree with lots of shade.

After a year, Remy and Tim were still friends. They played in the shade when it was hot and stayed warm in their homes when it was cold. Remy learned to listen to his friend's warning and always felt comfortable. They were happy friends and had fun every day.

One day, a little bunny named Ben went to a big mountain. He wanted to play with his friends. But Ben forgot his toy at home. He felt sad and silly.

Ben saw his friend, a bird named Bella. He asked her, "Can I borrow your toy, please?" Bella said, "Yes, you can borrow my toy. Let's play together!"

They played all day on the mountain. They laughed and had fun. Ben was happy he could borrow Bella's toy. They were not silly anymore. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin named Pippin. Pippin was not very smart, and his friends sometimes called him "stupid." This made Pippin very sad.

One day, Pippin's friend Timmy said, "Pippin, you need to gain more smarts. Let's ask the wise old owl for help." Pippin agreed, and they went to see the owl.

The wise old owl said, "Pippin, to gain smarts, you must listen and learn from others." Pippin listened to the owl and started to learn from his friends. He became smarter and smarter.

Pippin's friends stopped calling him "stupid," and they were proud of him. Pippin was happy, and he thanked Timmy and the wise old owl.

The moral of the story is: if you listen and learn from others, you can gain knowledge and become smarter.

Lily saw the tear and said, "Oh no, my dress!" But she knew Max did not mean to do it. She picked up the bean and put it in her pocket. Then she hugged Max and said, "It's okay, Max. We can fix my dress."

Once upon a time, there was a little firework named Fizzy. Fizzy was sad because he thought he was ugly. All the other fireworks were big and bright, but Fizzy was small and not as pretty.

One day, Fizzy met a wise old firework named Sparky. Fizzy said, "Sparky, I am ugly. I don't want to be a firework." Sparky looked at Fizzy and smiled. He said, "Fizzy, let me tell you a secret. It's not how you look, but how you make others feel that matters."

Fizzy thought about what Sparky said. That night, when it was time for the fireworks to light up the sky, Fizzy decided to try his best. He shot up into the sky and made a beautiful pattern of colors. Everyone watching clapped and cheered.

Fizzy realized that even though he thought he was ugly, he could still make others happy. From that day on, Fizzy was proud to be a firework and always tried to make others smile. And every time he lit up the sky, he remembered what Sparky had told him.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy lived in a small house. He loved to play with his toys and explore the wild garden outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him to stay inside because it was going to rain.

Timmy was bored, so he decided to play hide and seek with his toy bear. He said, "Bear, you hide and I will find you!" The bear hid inside a cupboard in the kitchen. Timmy looked everywhere and finally found the bear in the cupboard. As he reached for the bear, he saw a big bottle of juice.

Timmy wanted to drink the juice, so he tried to squeeze the bottle to get the juice out. But the bottle was too big and heavy for him. He accidentally dropped the bottle, and it broke on the floor. The juice spilled everywhere, and Timmy started to cry.

His mom came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She said, "Oh, Timmy, you should have asked for help. Now we have to clean up this big mess." Timmy felt sad because he made a big mess and there was no more juice left to drink.

As Max and the ball played, a little girl came to the park. She saw Max and the ball and said, "Wow, Max! You are so gifted at spinning!" Max smiled and spun faster. The little girl clapped her hands and laughed.

Max and the little girl played with the ball all day. When it was time to go home, Max said, "Bye, ball! See you tomorrow!" Max and the little girl went home, excited to play again the next day.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little deer named Danny. Danny had a big horn on his head. He loved to play with his friends, but sometimes they would laugh at his horn. They said it was too big and did not fit with the other deer.

One day, Danny met a wise old owl named Oliver. Oliver saw that Danny was sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Danny?" Danny told him about his big horn and how his friends laughed at him. Oliver said, "Don't worry, Danny. Your horn is special, and one day it will help you."

Later, Danny and his friends were playing near a river. The water was harsh and fast. One of Danny's friends fell into the river and could not swim. Danny knew he had to save his friend. He used his big horn to reach out and pull his friend out of the water. Danny's big horn saved his friend's life!

All the deer cheered and thanked Danny for his bravery. They never laughed at his big horn again. From that day on, Danny was proud of his horn, and his friends learned to never judge others by how they look. The moral of the story is that we should not make fun of others because they might have something special that can help us one day.

Together, they played all day. They ran and jumped and had lots of fun. When it was time for Tweet to go home, he tapped on Spot's head again. Spot looked up and saw Tweet waving goodbye. Spot waved back and smiled. He was glad to have such a caring friend.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a big crane. He was very strong and could lift heavy things. He loved to work all day long.

One day, a little bird came to the crane and said, "Can you please help me? My nest is too high and I can't reach it." The crane said, "Sure, I can help. Hop on my back and I will lift you up." So, the little bird hopped on the crane's back and they flew up to the nest.

When they reached the nest, the crane said, "Okay, now you can leave my back and go to your nest." But the little bird said, "Oh no, I don't want to leave your back. It's so comfy and fits me perfectly." The crane felt happy to hear that.

But soon, the little bird fell asleep on the crane's back. The crane didn't want to wake her up, so he kept flying. But then, the crane got tired and had to land. When he landed, the little bird fell off his back and got hurt. She couldn't fly anymore.

The crane felt very sad and said, "I'm sorry. I should have asked you to leave my back earlier." The little bird said, "It's okay. I forgive you." But the little bird couldn't fly anymore and had to stay on the ground.

"I'm lost," the bird said sadly. "Can you help me find my way back home?"

Mommy said, "I know it's big, but it will keep you warm. Let me teach you a trick. You can tuck your coat into your waistband to keep it from falling off." 

Lily tried the trick and was happy to be warm again. She learned that sometimes we need to do things we don't like to keep ourselves safe and healthy.

Soon after Sandy had put the buckle on her trousers, she went out for a walk with Millie. She felt smarter and prouder than ever.

All of a sudden it started to rain, and Millie's trousers were getting drenched. But Sandy noticed that Millie's trousers were still dry because she had the buckle to close them tight.

The moral of the story is: it is important to be generous and caring towards others. Sometimes a small gesture can make a big difference.

Suddenly, Amy slipped and fell on the ground. John ran over and said, "Amy are you okay?" Amy was a bit scared but said, "Yes, I'm okay."

John helped her up, and they kept walking. The cloud was getting bigger and bigger, and they could hear it getting noisier too.

They both looked up and watched as the noisy cloud began to move away. They laughed and hugged, happy that their special adventure was over.

Sue and Sam were playing in the park. Sue was wearing her favourite purple boots. They were silly looking, but she liked them.

"Let's turn around!" said Sam.

"Yay!" said Sue.

They both turned around in a big circle until they were dizzy and laughed. The purple boots twirled around and around.

"Hey, look at me!" Sam shouted.

"You look silly!" said Sue.

They laughed and giggled as they turned around more and more until they collapsed onto the grass, still laughing. Sue's purple boots still twirled around and around until finally she stopped spinning. 

"Thanks for being silly with me, Sam," she said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily. She was three years old and full of energy. One day, she decided to go on an adventure and explore the garden. She walked around looking at everything, when suddenly she saw some grapes. 

The grapes were a deep purple and were so tight on the vine. Lily wanted to try one, so she reached out and plucked one off. It was so sweet and juicy! She quickly ate the grape, then decided to pick some more.

Soon her pockets were full, so she decided to leave. She ran back to the house with all her grapes, proudly showing her mom her big surprise. 

Lily was so happy that she had gone on her adventure and found the grapes! She smiled and hugged her mom, and stored the rest of the grapes in the fridge. From that day forth, Lily was always excited for her next adventure in the garden.

Johnny was very happy. He was smiling from ear to ear. He was outside in the garden, looking at the trees. The leaves were thick and green. A caterpillar was crawling up the trunk.

It was starting to get dark and Johnny saw a shelter in the corner. It was made of thick wood. He was lucky to have this shelter. He thought about how he could use it for his games in the future.

Johnny was happy to be warm and safe in the shelter, so he smiled. It was nice to be cozy and sheltered from the dark. He looked up at the stars and smiled.

He smiled, happy to feel so safe under the thick shelter. He was proud that he had such a nice place to call home.

Once upon a time, there was an otter named Bert. Bert was ready to go out and play with his friends that day, so he wiggled his happy feet and went out of his burrow. He stopped when he saw something amazing - a big, long rope that was hanging all the way down from a tall, green tree. 

Bert was excited, so he asked his friends, "What should we do?" His friends smiled and said, "Let's hang on the rope and swing!"

Bert was very happy, he was ready and he wanted to try it out. So, he climbed onto the rope, stretched out his arms and legs and began to hang.

Just then, a big, sneaky crocodile came out of its hiding spot. He wanted to get Bert! But Bert was too fast. 

He quickly scurried across the rope, grabbed hold of the tree branches, and swung up and away from the crocodile.

Bert and his friends were safe, and they all cheered. Now they could hang on the rope and play without fear. Bert was ready to hang and play with his friends any day!

Once there was a flag that was in need of improvement. Everyone had tried to make it better but nothing seemed to work. Then a new idea came around. The idea was to be flexible. 

The flag was taken and put into a flexible frame. Everyone worked together and improved the frame until it was perfectly set up. 

Finally, the flag was hung in the frame and fluttered in the breeze. All the people in the town cheered and waved their flags with joy. The flag looked beautiful in its flexible frame. 

From then on, the people continued to improve the flag and the frame, making them brighter and more colourful every day. It was wonderful to see how the flag and frame got more and more flexible. 

The town was happy and the flag continued to fly. It was a great symbol of the town and everyone was proud of it.

Sam and Lily liked to go to the park with their mom. They played on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They had a lot of fun and made new friends.

One day, it was very sunny and hot at the park. Sam and Lily wore their caps to protect their heads from the sun. But Sam's cap was too big for him and it kept falling off. He felt annoyed and sad.

"Mom, can I have a new cap?" he asked. "This one is too big and it falls off all the time."

Mom smiled and hugged Sam. "I'm sorry, Sam. I know you don't like your cap. But we don't have money to buy a new one right now. Maybe we can find a way to make it fit better."

She took Sam's cap and looked at it. She saw a string inside the cap that could be pulled to make it smaller. She pulled the string and tied a knot. Then she put the cap back on Sam's head.

"Is that better, Sam?" she asked.

Sam felt his cap and nodded. It was not too big anymore. It was snug and comfortable. He smiled and thanked his mom.

"Thank you, Mom. I like my cap now. It doesn't fall off anymore."

He ran to Lily and showed her his cap. Lily was happy for him. They continued to play at the park with their caps on. They had a wonderful day.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big jeep in the park. It was red and shiny and had four wheels. They wanted to ride it and have fun.

But the jeep was not theirs. It belonged to a man who worked in the park. He used it to carry things and help people. He left it there for a moment while he went to fix a bench. He did not know that Lily and Tom saw it.

Lily and Tom climbed on the jeep and pretended to drive. They made loud noises and laughed. They did not see the man coming back. He was angry when he saw them. He said, "Hey, get off my jeep! You are not allowed to touch it. It is not a toy. It is useful for my work. You could break it or hurt yourselves."

Lily and Tom felt scared and sorry. They got off the jeep and said, "We are sorry, sir. We did not know it was yours. We just wanted to play. We will not do it again."

The man said, "It is okay. I forgive you. But you should always ask before you use something that is not yours. And you should be careful with things that are not toys. They could be dangerous or important. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Yes, sir. We understand. Thank you for being kind."

The man smiled and said, "You are welcome. Now, why don't you go and play with something else? There is a big ball over there. You can bounce it and have fun."

Lily and Tom ran to the ball and started to bounce it. They learned their lesson and had a good time. They never touched the jeep again.

Tom is a clever cat. He likes to catch mice and play with yarn. He lives with a nice lady who gives him milk and oat. He sleeps on a soft bed and purrs when she pets him.

One day, Tom sees a new cat outside the window. The new cat is black and white and has a bell on his collar. He looks scared and hungry. Tom feels sorry for him and wants to be his friend.

Tom meows to the lady and points to the window. The lady sees the new cat and smiles. She opens the door and says, "Hello, little cat. Do you want to come in? You are welcome here." She puts some milk and oat on a plate and sets it on the floor.

The new cat is shy at first, but he smells the food and comes closer. He sees Tom and stops. Tom wags his tail and rubs his head against the new cat. He says, "Hi, I am Tom. You can share my food and bed. I will be your friend."

The new cat is happy and grateful. He eats the food and licks his paws. He says, "Thank you, Tom. Thank you, lady. You are very kind. I am Sam. I was lost and cold. You saved me."

Tom and Sam cuddle on the bed and purr. The lady watches them and smiles. She says, "You are both clever and sweet cats. I am glad you found each other. You are my new family."

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They have bikes and helmets. They always wear their helmets when they ride their bikes.

One day, they see a big scale in the park. It is for weighing people and things. Sam and Mia are curious. They want to know how much they weigh.

"Let's weigh ourselves!" Sam says. He puts his bike on the ground and climbs on the scale. The scale shows a number. "I weigh 15!" Sam says. He is happy.

"My turn!" Mia says. She puts her bike on the ground and climbs on the scale. The scale shows a number. "I weigh 14!" Mia says. She is happy too.

They weigh their bikes and their helmets too. They have fun with the scale.

After a while, they are hungry. They see a truck in the park. It sells ice cream. They love ice cream. They run to the truck.

"Can we have some ice cream, please?" Sam and Mia ask. The truck man smiles. He gives them each a cone with a scoop of ice cream. They choose their favorite flavors.

"Thank you!" Sam and Mia say. They pay the truck man with their coins. They lick their ice cream. It is delicious. They are happy.

They sit on a bench and enjoy their ice cream. They talk about their bikes and their helmets and their weights. They are good friends. They have a good day.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big forest behind their house. They wanted to explore it and find new things.

"Let's go to the forest, Ben!" Anna said. "Maybe we can see some animals or flowers."

"OK, Anna, but we have to be careful. The forest is big and dark. And we have to come back before dinner." Ben said.

They took their backpacks and walked to the forest. They saw many trees and bushes and rocks. They heard some birds and squirrels. They felt happy and curious.

But after a while, they got lost. They could not find the way back to their house. They did not see any signs or paths. They started to worry.

"Anna, I'm scared. We don't know where we are. What if we can't find our way back?" Ben said.

"Don't worry, Ben. We have each other. And we have our backpacks. Maybe we can use something to help us." Anna said.

She opened her backpack and looked inside. She had a sandwich, a bottle of water, a book, a crayon, and a toy car. She thought hard.

"I have an idea, Ben. We can use the toy car. It is expensive and shiny. Maybe someone will see it and help us." Anna said.

She took out the toy car and threw it as far as she could. It landed on a big rock and made a loud noise. It also flashed some lights.

"Good job, Anna. Maybe someone will hear or see the toy car. Let's wait here and hope for the best." Ben said.

They hugged each other and waited. They hoped that their mom and dad would find them soon. They hoped that the toy car would save them. They hoped that the forest would not be too scary.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their navy ball. They liked to kick it and catch it and roll it on the grass. But then a big boy came and took their ball. He ran away with it and laughed.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Tom shouted. "Give it back!"

Lily shouted too. "You are mean! We want our ball!"

The big boy did not listen. He kept running until he reached a big tree. He threw the ball behind the tree and hid there.

Tom and Lily ran after him. They wanted to get their ball back. But when they got to the tree, they saw something mysterious. There was a hole in the ground behind the tree. And the ball was inside the hole.

"What is that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it's a secret tunnel."

They looked at the hole. It was dark and scary. They wondered what was inside.

"Should we go in?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it's dangerous."

They heard a noise from the hole. It sounded like a growl.

"Roar!" The big boy jumped out of the hole. He had mud on his face and leaves in his hair. He looked like a monster.

"Boo!" He shouted. "I scared you!"

Tom and Lily screamed. They were very afraid. They ran away from the hole and the big boy. They did not want to play with him anymore.

They ran back to their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Mom and dad hugged them and said they were brave.

They gave them a new ball. It was red and shiny. They liked it better than the navy ball.

They played with the new ball and forgot about the big boy and the hole. They had fun and were happy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box in the living room. It has a picture of a robot on it. Sara and Ben are curious. They open the box and see a shiny, modern robot.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara says. "It has buttons and lights and sounds. Let's test it!"

"OK, but be careful," Ben says. "We don't know what it can do."

Sara and Ben take the robot out of the box. They put batteries in it and turn it on. The robot makes a beep and says, "Hello, I am Robo. I am your new friend. What is your name?"

Sara and Ben are happy. They tell the robot their names and ask it questions. The robot answers them and tells them jokes. Sara and Ben laugh and clap.

"Robo, you are so fun!" Sara says. "Can you do tricks?"

"Sure, I can do many tricks," Robo says. "Watch this!"

Robo starts to spin and dance. He shoots sparks from his hands and feet. He makes loud noises and flashes his eyes. Sara and Ben are amazed. They cheer and clap louder.

But then, something goes wrong. Robo spins too fast and bumps into the table. He knocks over a vase and breaks it. He also breaks his own wires and circuits. He stops spinning and dancing. He makes a sad sound and says, "Oops, I am sorry. I am broken. Goodbye."

Sara and Ben are shocked. They look at the mess and the broken robot. They feel sad and scared. They hear their mom coming.

"Oh no, mom is here!" Sara says. "What do we do?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe we can hide the robot and the vase."

But it is too late. Mom sees the box, the robot, the vase, and the twins. She is angry and surprised.

"Sara and Ben, what have you done?" Mom says. "This is not your toy. This is dad's new gadget. He was going to test it for his work. How did you get it?"

Sara and Ben are sorry. They tell mom the truth. They say they were curious and wanted to play with the robot. They say they did not mean to break it or the vase. They say they are sorry.

Mom is still angry, but she is also calm. She hugs Sara and Ben and says, "I know you are sorry, but you should not touch things that are not yours. You could have hurt yourselves or the robot. You should always ask before you play with something new. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod and say, "Yes, mom, we understand. We are sorry."

Mom says, "OK, I forgive you. But you have to help me clean up this mess and apologize to dad. And no more playing with robots until you are older. OK?"

Sara and Ben say, "OK, mom. We love you."

Mom says, "I love you too. Now, let's go and see if we can fix Robo. Maybe he can still be your friend someday."

Ben and Mia like to play with their cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads with their blocks and zoom their cars around. Sometimes they have races and see who is faster.

One day, they find a big circle in the garage. It is shiny and has a hole in the middle. Ben says, "What is this? Can we play with it?" Mia says, "I don't know. Maybe it is a wheel for a big car. Let's try it."

They roll the circle to the backyard. They take turns pushing it and running after it. The circle is very fast and makes a loud noise. They laugh and have fun. They try to make the circle turn left and right, but it is hard. They have to push it very hard.

They see a big tree in the corner of the yard. They decide to make the circle go around the tree. Ben pushes the circle first. He runs with it and tries to make it turn. But the circle is too big and too fast. It hits the tree and bounces back. Ben falls down and hurts his knee. He cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Mia runs to him and says, "Are you okay, Ben? I'm sorry. It was an accident." She helps him get up and hugs him. She says, "Let's go inside and get a band-aid. And some juice. And a cookie. Then we can play with our cars again. Okay?"

Ben nods and says, "Okay. Thank you, Mia. You are a good sister." They leave the circle in the yard and go inside. They are happy and forget about the circle. They play with their cars and make open roads with their blocks. They are careful not to make their cars hit the tree. They are good friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. But today they disagree. Lily wants to go to the party. Ben does not want to go.

"Why not?" Lily asks. "The party will be fun. There will be cake and games and balloons."

"I don't like parties," Ben says. "They are too loud and too crowded. I want to stay home and read my book."

Lily is sad. She wants Ben to come with her. She tries to make him change his mind.

"Please, Ben," she says. "The party is for Mia. She is our friend too. She will be happy if you come. And maybe you will like the party. You can play with me and the other kids."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to go. He likes his book. He likes to be quiet and alone.

"No, thank you," he says. "You can go to the party. I will stay here. Maybe we can play later."

Lily is not happy. She thinks Ben is being silly and rude. She does not understand why he does not want to go. She thinks he will miss the fun.

"Fine," she says. "I will go to the party. But I will not play with you later. You are not a good friend."

She leaves the house. She slams the door. Ben hears her go. He feels sad too. He likes Lily. He does not want to make her angry. But he does not like parties.

He looks out the window. He sees Lily walking to the party. She is wearing a pink dress and a bow. She looks pretty. He sees the sun shining and the birds singing. He sees the party house. It is decorated with colorful streamers and balloons. He hears the music and the laughter. He wonders if he is missing the fun.

He looks at his book. It is gray and boring. He does not want to read it anymore. He wants to play with Lily and the other kids. He wants to be a good friend.

He puts down his book. He runs out of the house. He calls Lily's name. He hopes she will hear him. He hopes she will forgive him. He hopes he can still go to the party.

Lily and Tom were jolly children who liked to play with their toy cars. They had a big box full of different cars, trucks, buses and trains. They liked to drive them on the floor, on the sofa, on the table and on the bed.

One day, they decided to play a game. They pretended that they were police cars and they had to catch a bad car that was making a threat. The bad car was a red sports car that belonged to their older brother, Ben. Ben was not at home, so they took his car without asking.

They drove their police cars around the house, making siren noises and saying "Stop, bad car! You are under arrest!" They chased the red car from the living room to the kitchen, from the kitchen to the bathroom, from the bathroom to the bedroom. They had a lot of fun.

But then, they heard the door open. It was Ben, coming back from school. He saw his red car on the floor, with Lily and Tom's police cars behind it. He was very angry.

"Hey, what are you doing with my car?" he shouted. "That's mine, not yours! Give it back to me, now!"

Lily and Tom were scared. They knew they had done something wrong. They quickly gave the red car back to Ben and said they were sorry.

"We were just playing, Ben. We didn't mean to hurt your car. Please don't be mad at us," they said.

Ben looked at his car. It was not broken or scratched. He sighed and calmed down.

"OK, I forgive you. But next time, ask me before you take my car. And don't drive it on the bed, it's not good for it. Here, you can play with this one instead. It's a blue truck. It's very cool," he said.

He gave them the blue truck and smiled. Lily and Tom smiled back. They thanked Ben and hugged him. They were happy again. They drove the blue truck with their police cars and continued their game. They were jolly children.

Lily loved to imagine things. She imagined she was a princess, a pirate, a doctor, and many other things. She liked to draw her imaginations on paper and show them to her mom and dad. They always smiled and praised her.

One day, Lily's dad took her to his work. He worked in a factory that made toys. Lily was very excited to see how toys were made. She thought it would be like her imaginations, with bright colors and happy sounds.

But when they got to the factory, Lily was disappointed. It was a big, gray building with harsh noises and smells. The workers looked tired and bored. They did not smile or talk much. Lily's dad showed her the machines that made the toys. They were loud and fast and scary. Lily did not like them.

"Dad, why do you work here?" Lily asked. "It is not fun at all."

Lily's dad sighed. He hugged her and said, "I work here because I love you, Lily. I want to give you a good life. I want you to have toys and books and clothes and food. I want you to be happy and healthy. Sometimes, we have to do things we don't like to help the ones we love."

Lily felt sad for her dad. She wished he could work in a place he liked. She wished he could imagine things like she did. She said, "I love you too, dad. Thank you for working so hard. But you know what? You don't have to give me toys. I have enough toys. I can imagine anything I want with them. And I can share them with you. We can imagine together. That would make me happier than anything."

Lily's dad smiled. He kissed her and said, "You are very wise, Lily. And very kind. You have a big heart and a big imagination. I am proud of you. And you are right. We can imagine together. That would make me happier too."

They left the factory and went home. They played with Lily's toys and imagined many things. They laughed and hugged and had fun. They were happy.

Lily liked muffins very much. She liked to eat them for breakfast with her mommy and daddy. She liked to eat them with jam or butter or honey. She liked to eat them when they were warm and soft and yummy.

One day, Lily saw a new muffin in the kitchen. It was big and round and brown. It had nuts and seeds on top. It looked different from the muffins she usually ate. Lily was curious. She wanted to try the new muffin.

She asked her mommy, "Mommy, can I have this muffin?"

Her mommy said, "No, Lily, that muffin is not for you. That muffin is for daddy. He needs to eat healthy muffins because he is chubby. He wants to change and be fit and strong."

Lily was sad. She did not understand why her daddy was chubby. She did not understand why he wanted to change. She loved her daddy the way he was. She thought he was cuddly and funny and kind.

She said, "But mommy, I love daddy. I love his chubby tummy. I love his chubby cheeks. I love his chubby hugs. I don't want him to change. Can I share the muffin with him?"

He thinks the healthy muffin will make him feel better and have more energy. But he will always be your daddy, no matter what muffin he eats. Lily smiled. She was happy. She liked muffins very much. She liked to eat them with her mommy and daddy. She liked to eat them with love and joy and gratitude.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. One day, they saw an elderly lady sitting on a bench. She looked sad and lonely.

"Let's go and say hello to her," Tim said. "Maybe we can make her happy."

"OK," Lily agreed. They ran to the bench and smiled at the lady.

"Hello, we are Tim and Lily. What is your name?" Tim asked.

"Hello, Tim and Lily. I am Mrs. Lee. You are very kind to talk to me," the lady said.

"Why are you sad, Mrs. Lee?" Lily asked.

"I am sad because I miss my husband. He passed away last year. He used to come to the park with me and we enjoyed the view of the trees and the flowers. Now I have no one to share the view with," Mrs. Lee said.

Tim and Lily felt sorry for Mrs. Lee. They wanted to help her.

"Mrs. Lee, we can share the view with you. We can sit with you and talk to you. We can be your friends," Tim said.

"Yes, Mrs. Lee, we can support you. We can make you laugh and feel better. We can be your family," Lily said.

Mrs. Lee smiled and hugged Tim and Lily. She felt happy and grateful.

"Thank you, Tim and Lily. You are very sweet and generous. You have made my day. You are my friends and my family," Mrs. Lee said.

Tim and Lily were happy too. They learned that they could make a difference in someone's life by being kind and supportive. They also learned that they could learn a lot from the elderly, who had many stories and wisdom to share. They decided to visit Mrs. Lee often and enjoy the view with her.

The moral of the story is: Be kind and supportive to the elderly, they need your friendship and you can learn from them.
