Sara and Ben like to play pirates. They have a big box that they pretend is a ship. They wear hats and scarves and say "Arrr!" a lot. They also have a map that shows them where to find treasure.

One day, they decide to follow the map to the treasure. They take their box outside and drag it across the grass. They look at the map and see that they have to go past the swing, under the tree, and over the hill. They work hard to move their box along the way.

When they get to the hill, they see a big rock with a red X on it. They think that is where the treasure is. They push their box to the rock and look around. They see a hole under the rock. They lift the rock and see a shiny metal box inside the hole. They pull the box out and open it.

Inside the box, they find many things. They find coins and jewels and necklaces and rings. They also find a lemon and a bottle of vinegar. They think these are also treasure. They are very happy and excited. They take out the lemon and the vinegar and try them.

But they do not like them. The lemon and the vinegar are very sour. They make their faces twist and their mouths pucker. They spit them out and say "Yuck!" They do not want these treasure. They put them back in the box and close it.

They decide to keep the other treasure. They lay them on a blanket and look at them. They think they are very pretty and shiny. They pretend they are rich and famous pirates. They have fun playing with their treasure. They forget about the sour treasure. They are happy.

Lily liked to play with her guitar. She had a red guitar that made nice sounds when she strummed it. She played it every day in her room.

One day, her brother Max came into her room. He saw her guitar and wanted to play with it too. He grabbed it from her hands and ran away.

"Hey, give it back!" Lily shouted. She chased him down the hall. "That's my guitar!"

Max ran into the kitchen and hid behind the table. He laughed and stuck out his tongue. He tried to play the guitar, but he did not know how. He made loud and bad sounds.

"Stop it, stop it!" Lily cried. She reached for the guitar, but Max pushed her away. He knocked over a bowl of soup on the table. The soup spilled all over the guitar and the floor. The guitar was filthy.

"Look what you did!" Lily said. She was very sad and angry. She wanted to rest, but she could not. Her guitar was ruined.

Mom heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She saw the mess and the children. She was not happy.

"What's going on here?" she asked. She looked at the guitar and the soup. She shook her head.

"Max took my guitar and made it filthy!" Lily said.

"I just wanted to play with it!" Max said.

Mom sighed. She took the guitar and the soup. She cleaned them with a cloth. She gave the guitar back to Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Your guitar is still good. You can play with it again." she said.

She looked at Max. "Max, you need to say sorry to Lily. You can't take things that are not yours. And you can't make a mess in the kitchen. You need to help me clean it up." she said.

Max pouted. He did not want to say sorry or clean up. But he knew he was wrong. He looked at Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I won't take your guitar again." he said.

Lily nodded. She was still mad, but she forgave him. She hugged her guitar.

"Thank you, Mom. Can I go to my room and rest?" she asked.

Mom smiled. "Yes, you can. But first, give me a kiss." she said.

A big fish heard the little crab's cry. He swam to the huge shell and looked inside. He saw the little crab, scared and alone.

"Hello, little crab," he said. "Why are you in this huge shell?"

"I wanted a new shell, but this one is too huge," the little crab said. "Can you help me get out?"

"Of course, I can help you," the big fish said. "But you have to promise me something."

"What is it?" the little crab asked.

"You have to promise me that you will not try to gain any more huge shells. They are not good for you. You are a little crab, and you need a little shell that fits you well."

"OK, I promise," the little crab said. "Please help me get out."

The big fish used his tail to push the huge shell. The huge shell rolled over and the little crab came out. He was free and happy.

"Thank you, big fish," he said. "You are very kind and smart."

"You are welcome, little crab," the big fish said. "Now go and find a shell that is right for you."

The little crab nodded and waved goodbye. He learned his lesson. He did not want to gain any more huge shells. He wanted a shell that was cozy and comfortable. He searched and searched until he found one. He moved in and smiled. He had a new shell that he loved.

Tom and Lily were sad. They lost their snowman and their rod and their hose. They were wet and cold.

"Let's go inside, Tom," Lily said. "We can get warm and dry. Maybe we can make another snowman later."

"OK, Lily," Tom said. He hugged his sister. "I'm sorry we broke the hose."

"It's OK, Tom," Lily said. "It was an accident. Maybe we can fix it later."

They went inside the house. They took off their wet clothes and put on dry ones. They drank hot cocoa and ate cookies. They felt better.

They still liked playing in the snow, but they learned to be careful with the hose.

"Come on, Ben, let's go see the magic show!" Sara said. "It will be fun and amazing!"

"No, Sara, I don't want to go. The magic show is spooky and dark. There might be scary things inside the tent," Ben said. He held Sara's hand and pulled her away.

Sara was not afraid. She was curious and brave. She looked at Ben and said, "I dare you to go inside the tent with me. If you go, I will give you my candy. If you don't go, you are a chicken."

Ben loved candy, but he hated being called a chicken. He looked at the tent and gulped. He did not want to go, but he did not want to lose the dare. He said, "Okay, Sara, I will go with you. But you have to hold my hand and stay close to me."

Sara smiled and said, "Deal!" She took Ben's hand and led him to the tent. They paid the ticket and entered the tent. It was dark and quiet inside. They saw a stage with a curtain and a big box. On the box, there was a veil that covered something.

Sara and Ben walked slowly to the front row. They sat on the chairs and waited for the show to start. They heard a voice that said, "Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, welcome to the magic show! I am the great magician, and I will show you some amazing tricks. For my first trick, I will make something disappear under this veil. Are you ready?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They were excited and nervous. They watched as the magician lifted the veil and revealed a big rabbit. The rabbit was white and fluffy. It looked at Sara and Ben and twitched its nose.

The magician said, "This is my assistant, Fluffy. He is very friendly and smart. Watch as I make him disappear with a wave of my wand. One, two, three, abracadabra!"

The magician waved his wand and said the magic word. He dropped the veil over the rabbit and the box. He counted to ten and then lifted the veil again. The rabbit and the box were gone. There was nothing on the stage.

Sara and Ben gasped. They clapped their hands and cheered. They were amazed and happy. They looked at each other and smiled. They forgot their fear and enjoyed the magic show. They saw more tricks and had more fun. They learned that magic was not spooky and dark, but wonderful and bright. They thanked the magician and left the tent. Once upon a time, in a big green sea, there lived a little dolphin named Dolly. Dolly loved to play with her friends, the fish and the turtles. They would swim and jump in the water all day long.

One day, Dolly heard a loud roar. She got scared and swam to her friend, Tommy the Turtle. "What was that roar?" she asked. Tommy said, "That was Leo the Lion. He lives on the land and he is very strong."

Dolly wanted to be strong like Leo the Lion, so she swam to the shore and asked him, "Can you teach me to roar like you?" Leo laughed and said, "You are a dolphin, not a lion. You don't need to roar. You are strong in your own way."

Dolly thought about what Leo said, and she realized that she didn't need to roar to be strong. She swam back to her friends and told them what she learned. They all agreed that they were strong in their own ways, too. And from that day on, they all played together, happy to be themselves.

The moral of the story is that everyone is special and strong in their own way, and we should be happy being ourselves.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet lived in a tree with his family and friends. One day, Tweet flew to a big tree to find some food. He found a shiny red berry and ate it. But, oh no! The berry was sharp and it hurt Tweet's tummy.

The doctor bird said that Tweet needed to rest and drink water. Tweet's family and friends made a network around him to keep him safe and warm. After a few days, Tweet felt much better and learned to be careful about eating strange berries.

Lily didn't give up and continued to play. She climbed up the big slide and went down really fast. But when she got to the bottom, she tripped and her clear sunglasses fell off.

She looked for them everywhere but couldn't find them. Lily was very sad because she loved her sunglasses so much. From that day on, she learned to be more careful when playing and to always keep her favorite things safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a new silver necklace that she loved to wear. One day, she went to the park to play with her friend, Timmy.

"Hi, Timmy!" said Lily.

"Hi, Lily! I like your new necklace. It's shiny!" said Timmy.

"Thank you! I got it from my mom. She said it's made of silver," said Lily.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was the sound of a lock clicking. They turned around and saw a man locking the gate to the park.

"Oh no! We're locked in!" cried Timmy.

"Don't worry. We can call for help," said Lily.

They used Timmy's phone to call Lily's mom. She came and unlocked the gate for them.

"Thank you, Mom!" said Lily.

"You're welcome, sweetie. Let's go home and have some ice cream," said Lily's mom.

And they all went home happily ever after. The end.

Benny felt lonely that day and wanted to help someone. He decided to gather some carrots to give to the people in the ambulance. As he was gathering, he heard a loud noise. It was the ambulance coming back. He saw his neighbor, Mrs. Smith, being carried into the ambulance. Benny ran over to give her his carrots, but it was too late. Mrs. Smith had already passed away.

Benny's mommy explained to him that sometimes bad things happen, but it's important to always try to help others. Benny learned that even though he couldn't save Mrs. Smith, he could still make a difference by being kind and helpful to others.

Later, they met a little boy at the park. The boy said, "I like your dress, Lily." Lily said, "Thank you! I like your shirt too." They played together and had so much fun. When it was time to go, Lily said, "Bye-bye, see you later!" and waved goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Lily. Lily liked to explore and discover new things. One day, she saw a shiny rail and decided to follow it. The rail led her deep into the forest where she found a big tree with a hole in it. Lily was curious and wanted to see what was inside the hole.

But as she reached inside, a spider bit her hand. It hurt a lot and Lily started to cry. She realized that following the rail had led her to a dangerous place. The moral of the story is that sometimes, following something that looks interesting can lead to trouble. It's important to be careful and ask for help when we are unsure.

Once upon a time, there was a wise sheep named Wooly. Wooly was very smart and always knew what to do. One day, Wooly saw his friend, a little lamb named Lucy, struggling to jump over a fence. 

"Hello, Lucy," said Wooly. "What's the matter?"

"I can't jump over the fence," said Lucy. "I keep trying, but I can't do it."

Wooly thought for a moment and then said, "Don't worry, Lucy. I have an idea. Instead of jumping over the fence, let's walk around it. That way, we won't struggle anymore."

Lucy was very happy to hear Wooly's idea. They walked around the fence together and had a fun time playing in the grass. Wooly taught Lucy that sometimes it's better to find a different way instead of struggling. 

The moral of the story is that it's okay to ask for help when you're struggling and sometimes there's an easier way to do things.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. But sometimes they would quarrel over who got to play with what. One day, they found a big box of velvet clothes in the attic. They were soft and shiny and had many colors.

"Wow, look at these!" Sara said. "I want to dress up like a princess!"

"Me too!" Ben said. "I want to be a king!"

They both grabbed the same velvet dress and started to pull on it.

"Let go, it's mine!" Sara shouted.

"No, it's mine!" Ben shouted back.

They pulled and pulled until the dress ripped in half. They both fell down and started to cry.

Their mother heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the torn dress and the sad twins.

"What happened here?" she asked.

"We were playing with the velvet clothes and we quarreled over the dress," Sara said.

"We both wanted to be royalty," Ben said.

Their mother shook her head and sighed.

"You were foolish to fight over a dress," she said. "You could have shared it or taken turns. Now you have ruined it and hurt yourselves."

She hugged them and kissed their tears away.

"I'm sorry, mommy," Sara said.

"Me too," Ben said.

Their mother smiled and said, "It's okay, I forgive you. But next time, remember to be kind and gentle with each other and with your things. Now, let's see if we can find something else to play with in the box."

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big cooler near the bench. They were curious. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Ben said.

"Maybe we should not," Anna said. "It belongs to someone else."

"But maybe there is something yummy inside," Ben said. "Or something fun. Come on, trust me. It will be okay."

Ben opened the cooler. He saw a cake with candles. He smiled. He took a big bite. Anna watched him. She felt afraid.

Suddenly, a man came. He looked angry. He saw Ben with the cake. He shouted.

"Hey, what are you doing? That's my cake! I made it for my son's birthday!"

Ben dropped the cake. He felt ashamed. He wanted to run away. Anna felt sorry for him. She wanted to help him.

"I'm sorry, sir," Anna said. "We didn't know. We were just curious. Please don't be mad."

The man looked at Anna. He saw that she was honest. He sighed.

"It's okay, little girl. I know you didn't mean to hurt me. But you should not touch things that are not yours. That's not nice. And you should not trust people who tell you to do bad things. That's not smart."

Anna nodded. She understood. She looked at Ben. He looked sad. She held his hand.

"I'm sorry, too, sir," Ben said. "I was wrong. I won't do it again. And I won't make Anna do it, either. She is my friend. I want to be a good friend."

The man smiled. He saw that they were sorry. He forgave them.

"It's okay, little boy. I'm glad you learned your lesson. And I'm glad you have a good friend. Here, you can have a slice of cake. But only one. And share it with Anna. And say happy birthday to my son. His name is Max."

Ben and Anna thanked the man. They took a slice of cake. They shared it with each other. They said happy birthday to Max. They felt happy. They learned to be more careful. And they learned to trust each other.

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, mom. We are sorry. We will share and lend. We will be kind."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I love you both. Now, let's see if we can mend the coat and the hanger. And then, we can play some more."

"Okay!" Sam says. He follows Lily. They walk around the park. They point the record machine at different things. They record the sounds they like.

They record a bird singing on a branch. They record a squirrel running on the grass. They record a bee flying near a flower. They record a dog barking at a ball.

They are happy. They have many sounds of nature. They go back to the bench. They sit down. They push another button. It makes another beep.

They listen to the record machine. It plays back the sounds they recorded. They hear the bird, the squirrel, the bee, and the dog. They smile. They clap their hands.

"We did it!" Lily says. "We recorded the sounds of nature!"

"We did!" Sam says. "They are beautiful!"

They hug each other. They are proud. They have a new toy. They have a new record. They have a new adventure.

Tom was a little boy who liked to grow things. He had a small garden where he planted seeds and watered them every day. He was very proud of his flowers and vegetables.

One day, he saw a big rabbit in his garden. The rabbit was eating his carrots and lettuce. Tom was very angry and ran to the rabbit. "Stop! Stop! You are eating my dinner!" he shouted.

The rabbit looked at Tom and twitched his nose. He did not stop eating. He liked the carrots and lettuce very much. He thought they were his dinner.

Tom tried to chase the rabbit away, but the rabbit was too fast. He hopped and dodged and ran around the garden. Tom could not catch him. He felt very troubled. He did not want to lose his dinner.

He ran to his house and called his mom. "Mom! Mom! There is a rabbit in my garden! He is eating my dinner! Help me!" he cried.

His mom came out and saw the rabbit. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, Tom. The rabbit is not eating your dinner. He is eating his dinner. You have plenty of other vegetables in your garden. Why don't you share some with the rabbit? He is a friend, not an enemy."

Tom thought about it and nodded. He liked to share and make friends. He picked some carrots and lettuce and put them in a basket. He walked to the rabbit and said, "Here, rabbit. You can have some of my dinner. But please don't eat too much. Leave some for me and my mom."

The rabbit stopped eating and looked at Tom. He saw the basket and smelled the carrots and lettuce. He wagged his tail and made a happy sound. He took some of the vegetables and ate them. He thanked Tom and said, "You are very kind, Tom. You are a good gardener and a good friend. I will not eat too much. I will leave some for you and your mom."

Tom smiled and said, "You are welcome, rabbit. You are a good eater and a good friend. I am glad you like my garden. Maybe you can come back and visit me again."

The rabbit nodded and said, "I would like that, Tom. Maybe I can bring you some flowers and seeds from my home. They are very pretty and tasty."

Tom and the rabbit became friends and shared their dinner. They both felt very happy and not troubled anymore.

"Where is the key?" Tom asks. "Maybe someone hid it."

They look under the chairs, behind the shelves, and in the drawers. They do not find the key. They are sad and tired.

"Maybe we should give up," Tom says. "This book is too hard to open."

"No, we can't give up," Sam says. "We have to study this book. Maybe it has something important inside. Maybe it has a story or a map or a secret."

"But how can we open it?" Tom asks.

Sam thinks for a moment. He has an idea. He runs to the librarian and asks for help.

"Excuse me, can you help us?" Sam says. "We want to study this book, but we don't have the key. Do you know where it is?"

The librarian smiles. She takes the book and looks at it. She recognizes it. It is a very old and special book. She has the key in her pocket.

"Of course, I can help you," she says. "This book is very old and special. It has gold letters and pictures inside. It tells a story about a king and a dragon. It is a very rare and valuable book. I have the key right here."

She takes out the key and opens the lock. She gives the book to Tom and Sam. They open the book and see the gold letters and pictures. They are amazed and happy.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Tom says. "Thank you for helping us."

"We will be careful," Sam says. "Thank you for letting us study this book. It is the best book ever."

They sit down and study the book. They learn the story about the king and the dragon. They see the bright gold letters and pictures. They are very happy. They are the best friends ever.

She climbed on a chair and reached for the bowl. She picked a grape and popped it in her mouth. It was delicious. She picked another one, and another one, and another one. She shook her gently and said, "Lily, wake up. You ate too many grapes. You have to eat dinner and drink some water. You might get sick."

But Lily did not wake up. She was too sleepy. She had a bad dream about grapes. They were chasing her and biting her. She cried and tossed and turned. Her mom felt sorry for her and hugged her. She said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I should have put the grapes away. But you have to listen to me. You can't eat too many grapes. They are good for you, but only in moderation. Next time, I will permit you to have some grapes, but only a few. OK?"

Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I love you." She snuggled with her mom and fell asleep again. She hoped that the grapes would leave her alone. She learned her lesson. She would never eat too many grapes again.

Tom and Anna felt sorry. They had borrowed the wrong jug. They said sorry to Mom and gave her back the jug.

Mom was not angry. She smiled and said, "It's okay, you made a mistake. But next time, ask me before you borrow anything. And don't drink vinegar, it is not good for you!"

She gave them some real juice and some cookies. Tom and Anna thanked her and went back to the garden. They learned a lesson. They would never borrow anything without asking again. And they would never drink vinegar again. It was disgusting!

The fireman came and they saved the cat together. The cat was very happy. The cat let out a big yawn and said, "Thank you, Tom and fireman!" Tom and the fireman were happy they could help. They knew they were a great team. From that day on, they knew they could do anything together.

Tom and Lily felt very bad. They had lost their sunflower and their grandpa's seeds. They had nothing left. They went back to their garden and sat on the ground. They hugged each other and cried.

They felt happy and hopeful. They thanked their grandpa for his gift. They watered the sprouts and watched them grow. They knew they would have many sunflowers in their garden. Jill and Ben felt their heads spin too. They felt their stomachs turn. They felt their faces pale. They stopped laughing and shouting.

"This is awful!" Jill said. "See, I told you it's scary!"

Ben nodded. He felt sick. He wanted to get off. He wished he had listened to Jill.

The big wheel stopped. The man unstrapped them. He helped them out. He saw their faces. He shook his head.

"Are you okay?" he asked.

Jill and Ben nodded. They felt weak. They held each other. They walked slowly to a bench. They sat down. They closed their eyes.

"I'm sorry, Jill," Ben said. "You were right. The big wheel was too fast. It made us dizzy. I should have listened to you."

"It's okay, Ben," Jill said. "You were brave. You wanted to try something new. I should have been more adventurous."

They hugged each other. They felt better. They learned a lesson.

Tom looked at his doll. The hole was gone. The coat looked good. He smiled.

They went back to play with their dolls. They were happy.

"Let's use a chair," said Lily. She pushed a chair to the shelf and climbed on it. She grabbed the jar of honey and opened it.

"Be careful," said Ben. "Don't spill the honey."

Lily took a teaspoon and dipped it in the honey. She licked the teaspoon and smiled. "Mmm, the honey is sweet and sticky."

She gave the teaspoon to Ben and he licked it too. "Yum, the honey is good."

They took turns licking the teaspoon and eating the honey. They did not notice that a bee was flying around the jar. The bee smelled the honey and wanted some too.

The bee flew to the jar and landed on the edge. It crawled inside the jar and looked for the honey. It saw the teaspoon and thought it was a flower. It tried to catch the teaspoon with its legs.

But the teaspoon was not a flower. It was metal and hard. The bee could not catch the teaspoon. It got angry and buzzed loudly.

Lily and Ben heard the bee and looked at the jar. They saw the bee inside the jar and got scared.

"Help, there is a bee in the jar!" they shouted.

They dropped the jar and the teaspoon and ran away. The jar and the teaspoon fell on the floor and broke. The honey spilled everywhere. The bee flew out of the jar and chased Lily and Ben.

They ran to the living room and hid behind the sofa. They hugged each other and cried.

"Mom, dad, help us!" they called.

Mom and dad came to the living room and saw Lily and Ben behind the sofa. They also saw the mess in the kitchen.

"What happened?" they asked.

Lily and Ben told them what they did. They said they were sorry and they learned their lesson.

Mom and dad were not happy, but they were glad that Lily and Ben were not hurt. They told them to never play with the honey jar again. They also told them to be kind to the bees, because they make the honey.

They cleaned up the mess and gave Lily and Ben a hug. They also gave them an orange to eat, because it was healthy and sweet.

Lily and Ben ate the orange and thanked mom and dad. They said they would not be greedy and naughty again. They also said they would respect the bees and their work.

"Tom, I'm scared!" Lily said. "What do we do?"

Tom thought for a moment. He did not want to lose his purple ball, but he also did not want to get hurt by the dog. He had an idea.

"Hey, dog!" Tom yelled. "Do you want to play with us? We have a purple ball. It's very fun. You can have it if you want."

The dog stopped growling and barking. It looked at the purple ball with interest. It wagged its tail and licked its lips.

"Really?" the dog asked. "You will give me the purple ball?"

"Yes, yes, we will!" Tom said. "But you have to be nice to us. You can't bite us or chase us. You have to be our friend."

The dog thought for a moment. It liked the purple ball, but it also liked to bite and chase. It was a hard choice. But then it decided.

"OK, OK, I will be your friend," the dog said. "But only if you give me the purple ball. And you have to play with me sometimes. Deal?"

"Deal!" Tom and Lily said. They pushed the purple ball under the gate to the dog. The dog grabbed it with its mouth and wagged its tail. It was very happy.

Tom and Lily smiled. They had made a new friend. And they had learned a new word: surrender.

But Sara forgot to check the time and stayed outside too long. The sun went down and the air became very cold. Sara started to shiver and her nose turned red. She remembered that she had to go home for dinner and ran to get Lily. But when she picked up Lily, she saw that Lily was also shivering and her face was blue. Sara felt scared and sad. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to leave you in the cold. Please don't be sick. Please don't die."

Sara ran home with Lily in her arms. She hoped that her mom could help Lily. She knocked on the door and cried, "Mom, mom, please open the door. Lily is sick. She needs help."

Her mom opened the door and saw Sara and Lily. She was surprised and worried. She took Sara and Lily inside and said, "What happened, Sara? Why are you and Lily so cold and wet?"

Sara told her mom what happened and begged her to save Lily. Her mom felt sorry for Sara and Lily. She said, "Don't worry, Sara. Lily is not a real person. She is a doll. She can't get sick or die. She just needs to dry and warm up. I will put her in the dryer and she will be fine."

Sara felt relieved and happy. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever. I love you and I love Lily."

Her mom smiled and hugged Sara. She said, "I love you too, Sara. And I love Lily. But next time, don't stay outside too long. And don't forget to bring Lily with you. She doesn't like the cold either."

Sara nodded and said, "I promise, mom. I will take good care of Lily. She is my best friend."

Her mom took Lily to the dryer and turned it on. Sara waited patiently and hoped that Lily would be okay. She heard a loud noise and smelled something sour. She wondered what it was. She ran to the dryer and opened it. She saw Lily inside. But Lily was not smiling and nodding anymore. Lily was melted and burned. Sara screamed and cried. She said, "Lily, Lily, what happened to you? You are not the same. You are not my Lily. You are a monster."

Her mom heard Sara scream and ran to the dryer. She saw Lily and gasped. She said, "Oh no, Sara. I'm so sorry. I didn't know that Lily was made of plastic. I thought she was made of cloth. The dryer was too hot for her. It ruined her. I'm so sorry, Sara. I didn't mean to hurt Lily. I wanted to help her."

Sara was very angry and sad. She said, "You are not sorry. You are mean. You killed Lily. You are a bad mom. I hate you and I hate Lily. I don't want her anymore. She is not my friend. She is a monster."

She threw Lily on the floor and ran to her room. She slammed the door and cried. She wished that Lily was alive and well. She wished that she never played in the snow. She wished that she never got Lily for her birthday. She wished that everything was different.

"Let's hide!" Anna whispered to Ben. "Maybe the dog will go away."

"We have to tell mom!" Ben said to Anna. "She will help us get the ball and make the dog go away."

"But we will be in trouble!" Anna said. "We were not supposed to go near the bushes. Mom said they were dirty and had bugs."

"Come back, worm!" she shouted. "I want to play with you!"

She tried to move the rock, but it was too heavy. She pushed and pulled, but it did not budge. She felt frustrated and angry. She kicked the rock with her foot, but it only hurt her toe.

"Ow!" she cried. "Stupid rock!"

She heard a voice behind her. It was her brother, Tom. He was older and stronger than Lila. He had been watching her from the window.

"What are you doing, Lila?" he asked.

"I want to catch the worm, but it went under the rock, and I can't move it!" she said.

"Let me help you," he said. "We can move it together."

"Look, there it is!" Lila said.

She grabbed the worm and put it in her bucket. She smiled and thanked Tom.

"You're welcome, Lila," he said. "But you know, worms don't like to be in buckets. They like to be in the earth. They need air and water and food. If you keep them in the bucket, they will die."

"Can I put it back in the earth?" she asked.

"Sure, you can," Tom said. "That's the best thing to do. Then it will be happy and healthy. And maybe you can see it again another day."

Lila nodded. She took the worm out of the bucket and put it gently in the hole. She covered it with some earth and patted it softly.

"Bye, worm," she said. "Have fun in the earth. Maybe we can be friends later."

She hugged Tom and said, "Thank you, Tom. You're a good brother."

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was the camera. The camera was a gift from their grandma, who liked to take pictures of them. The camera had a button that made a click sound and a screen that showed the pictures.

One day, Ben and Lily decided to play a game with the camera. They took turns hiding and peeking at each other, and then snapping a picture. They laughed when they saw the funny faces they made on the screen. They had so much fun that they did not notice their mom calling them for lunch.

"Ben, Lily, come to the table, please. Your food is ready," their mom said.

But Ben and Lily did not hear her. They kept playing with the camera, hiding and peeking and snapping.

"Ben, Lily, I'm waiting for you. Your food is getting cold," their mom said again.

But Ben and Lily still did not hear her. They were too busy with the camera, hiding and peeking and snapping.

"Ben, Lily, this is the last time I'm calling you. If you don't come now, you will have no dessert," their mom said, a little angry.

But Ben and Lily did not care. They thought the camera was more important than the food, hiding and peeking and snapping.

Finally, their mom came to their room and saw them playing with the camera. She was not happy. She took the camera away from them and said, "Ben, Lily, you have been very naughty. You did not listen to me when I called you for lunch. You did not appreciate the food I made for you. You did not share the camera with anyone else. You only cared about yourselves. Now you will have no dessert, and no camera for the rest of the day. Maybe then you will learn to be more respectful and grateful and generous."

Ben and Lily felt very sorry. They realized they had made a mistake. They hugged their mom and said, "We're sorry, mom. We love you. We love the food you make for us. We love the camera grandma gave us. We will listen to you next time. We will appreciate what we have. We will share with others. Please forgive us."

Their mom smiled and said, "I forgive you, Ben and Lily. I love you too. But you still have to eat your lunch, and you still have to wait until tomorrow to play with the camera again. I hope you understand."

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "We understand, mom. Thank you for teaching us a lesson. We will be better children from now on."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their parents, to appreciate what they have, and to share with others. It also shows the consequences of being selfish and disobedient.

She found the cookies on the table. She took two cookies and gave one to the doll and one to the teddy. She said, "Here you go, doll and teddy. These are yummy cookies. They will make your stomach happy." She made the doll and the teddy say, "Thank you, Sara. You are very nice. We love cookies."

Sara smiled and ate her cookie. She said, "You are welcome, doll and teddy. I love you, too. You are my best friends." She hugged the doll and the teddy and went back to her room to play some more. She was very happy.

Sara and Ben were twins. They liked to play together, but sometimes they fought. One day, they found a big box in the basement. It was full of old clothes. They decided to try them on and pretend to be different people.

Sara put on a long dress and a hat. She said, "I am a princess. I live in a castle and have a lot of jewels." Ben put on a pair of pants and a shirt. He said, "I am a pirate. I sail on a ship and have a lot of treasure."

They played for a while, until Sara saw something shiny in Ben's pocket. She said, "What is that? Can I see it?" Ben said, "No, it is mine. It is a gold coin. I found it in the box. It is part of my treasure." Sara said, "That is not fair. You have to share. Give it to me." Ben said, "No, go away. It is mine."

They started to pull and tug on the coin. They both wanted it. They did not see the cat sneaking up behind them. The cat was curious. It saw something shiny and wanted to play with it. It jumped on Ben's pants and bit the coin. It tasted bad. The cat spat it out and ran away.

Sara and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at the coin. It was not gold. It was plastic. It had a hole in it. It was just a toy. They felt silly. They said, "Sorry" to each other. They hugged and laughed. They realized that the coin was not important. They had more fun playing together. They put the coin back in the box and went to find the cat. They wanted to pet it and say sorry. They did not care about the old clothes anymore. They were happy with their ordinary pants and dress.

Ben and Lily were curious. They wanted to try the diamond. They took it out of the box and held it in their hands. They felt a warm and tingly feeling.

"I wish for a big cake with lots of frosting and sprinkles," Ben said.

"Me too," Lily said.

They closed their eyes and wished hard. Then they opened them and saw a huge cake on the table. It smelled yummy and looked yummy. They ran to the table and grabbed a slice.

Lily was a naughty girl. She liked to chew things that were not food. She chewed her toys, her books, and even her shoes. Her mom and dad were very angry with her. They told her to stop chewing things or she would get sick.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a lady with a big hat and a shiny necklace. Lily thought the necklace looked like candy. She ran to the lady and tried to grab her necklace. The lady was very scared and shouted, "No, no, no! That is not candy, that is my necklace! You are a very naughty girl!"

Lily's mom heard the lady and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily holding the necklace in her mouth. She was very ashamed and sorry. She took the necklace from Lily and gave it back to the lady. She said, "I am so sorry, ma'am. My daughter has a bad habit of chewing things. She did not mean to hurt you or your necklace. Please forgive her."

The lady was still angry, but she saw that Lily's mom was sincere. She said, "Well, I hope you teach your daughter not to chew things that are not food. She could damage her teeth or swallow something dangerous. She should only chew food or gum."

Lily's mom nodded and thanked the lady. She took Lily by the hand and walked away. She said to Lily, "Lily, you were very naughty today. You scared the lady and almost broke her necklace. You should never chew things that are not food. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I am sorry. I will not chew things that are not food anymore. I will only chew food or gum."

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "That's good, Lily. I love you, but you have to be a good girl. Chewing things that are not food is bad for you and for others. You have to respect other people's things and feelings. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I love you too. I will be a good girl."

The moral value of the story is: Do not chew things that are not food. It is bad for you and for others. You have to respect other people's things and feelings.

The man was angry. He didn't want to keep them, he wanted his box of cardboard. He ordered the bunnies away from his house and back in the box.

The bunnies were very sad, so they hopped away to find a new home. They never found a new home and they were never seen again.

The End.

One day, when the bee flew up to the chimney, she saw a bat perched on the top. The bat also loved to dance, so he and the bee began to whirl around and around the chimney. They danced for hours, going faster and faster.

When the night was over, the bee and the bat said goodbye and the bee flew home. She was so excited to tell the other bees about her fun adventure dancing with the bat at the smelly chimney.

Once upon a time, there was a guard who lived in a small village. He was responsible for keeping the people safe. One night, he noticed a small cry for help coming from the forest nearby.

The guard bravely went into the forest to see who needed rescuing. When he arrived, he saw a miserable little puppy trying to get out of a deep hole. The guard immediately jumped down to rescue the puppy.

Unfortunately, before he could get the puppy out of the hole, a wild animal snuck up behind the guard, and with one powerful swipe the guard was knocked unconscious.

The poor little puppy was left alone and never rescued.

This story has a sad ending, but it also has a moral: no matter how brave you are, it's best to be always on the lookout, even when you're trying to rescue someone.

He introduced himself and the other shrimp were so happy to meet him. They all enjoyed playing around the sharp red rock on the bottom of the pond. The little red shrimp was so happy he could make new friends.

Lily likes to polish her shoes. She has a basket with a cloth and a tin of polish. She sits on the floor and takes out her shoes. She rubs the cloth on the tin and then on her shoes. She makes them shiny and clean.

She is very happy with her shoes. She puts them back in the basket and looks for something else to polish. She sees her doll on the bed. She thinks her doll would like to have shiny shoes too. She takes her doll and puts her in the basket. She finds a pair of tiny shoes for her doll.

She polishes the doll's shoes with the cloth and the tin. She makes them lovely and bright. She puts them on the doll's feet and smiles. She thinks her doll looks very pretty. She hugs her doll and puts her back on the bed. She is proud of her work. She puts the basket away and goes to play.

Lily was a little girl who loved to fly. She liked to jump on her mattress and pretend she was a bird or a plane. She had a lot of fun flying in her room, but she also wanted to fly outside.

One day, she had a big idea. She asked her dad to help her tie some balloons to her mattress. She wanted to fly in the sky with the balloons. Her dad said no, that was too dangerous. He said she could fly with her imagination, but not with her mattress.

Lily was sad and angry. She waited until her dad was busy, and then she sneaked out with her mattress and the balloons. She dragged them to the backyard and climbed on the mattress. She felt the balloons lift her up. She was flying!

She was happy for a moment, but then she saw how high she was. She saw the trees and the houses and the cars below. She felt scared and cold. She wanted to go back, but she did not know how. She started to cry.

Her dad heard her cry and ran outside. He saw her flying away with the mattress and the balloons. He was very worried. He got his car and followed her. He called the firemen and asked them to help. The firemen came with a big ladder and a net. They caught Lily and her mattress and brought them down. They were safe.

Lily hugged her dad and said sorry. She learned her lesson. She learned that flying was fun, but also dangerous. She learned that she should listen to her dad, because he loved her and wanted to protect her. She learned that she could fly with her imagination, but not with her mattress.

Tom liked to write with his crayons. He wrote his name, his mom's name, and his dog's name on a big paper. He was very proud of his writing. He wanted to show his mom.

He ran to the kitchen, where his mom was making a cake. He saw the oven was hot and had a red light. He knew he should not touch the oven. It was not safe.

"Mom, look what I wrote!" he said, holding his paper.

"Wow, Tom, that's very good!" his mom said, smiling. "You are a great writer. But be careful, don't go near the oven. It's very hot and it can hurt you."

"I know, mom. I won't touch the oven," Tom said. He put his paper on the table and went to play with his dog.

Later, his mom called him. "Tom, the cake is ready. Do you want a slice?"

"Yes, please!" Tom said, running back to the kitchen. He smelled the sweet cake and saw the frosting. He was very happy.

He also saw his paper on the table. But it was not the same. It had brown spots and holes. It looked like it was burned.

"Mom, what happened to my paper?" he asked, sad.

"Oh, Tom, I'm sorry. I didn't see your paper when I opened the oven. It was too close to the heat and it got burned. I'm so sorry," his mom said, hugging him.

"It's okay, mom. I can write another one. But next time, I will put it far from the oven. It's not safe," Tom said, learning his lesson.

He ate his cake and wrote a new paper. He was still a great writer. And he was careful with the oven.

Lily and Tom were twins who loved chocolate. One day, they saw a big jar of chocolate on the shelf in the kitchen. They wanted to eat some, but they knew they had to ask Mom first.

"Mom, can we have some chocolate?" Lily asked.

"Not now, sweeties. It's almost time for dinner. You can have some after you finish your vegetables," Mom said.

Lily and Tom were troubled. They did not like vegetables. They liked chocolate. They looked at each other and had an idea.

When Mom went to the living room, they got a chair and pushed it to the shelf. Tom climbed on the chair and reached for the jar. Lily stood next to him and helped him.

"Be careful, Tom. Don't drop it," Lily said.

"I got it, I got it," Tom said.

But he did not have it. The jar was too heavy and slippery. It fell from his hands and crashed on the floor. Chocolate spilled everywhere. Mom heard the noise and came running.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

Lily and Tom looked at the mess and felt sorry. They knew they did something bad.

"We're sorry, Mom. We wanted some chocolate," Lily said.

"We didn't mean to break it," Tom said.

Mom was angry, but also worried. She checked if they were hurt. They were not. She hugged them and said,

"I'm glad you're okay, but you should never do that again. You could have hurt yourselves or cut yourselves with the glass. And you should always listen to me and wait for your treats. Now, help me clean this up and then go to your room. No chocolate for you tonight."

Lily and Tom nodded and said,

"Yes, Mom."

They helped Mom clean the chocolate and the glass. Then they went to their room and felt sad. They learned their lesson. They decided to be good and eat their vegetables next time. Maybe then, Mom would give them some chocolate.

Lily was walking in the garden with her mom. She liked to see the flowers and the bugs. She saw a yellow and black bug on a red flower. She wanted to touch it.

"Mom, what is that?" she asked, pointing at the bug.

"That is a bee, Lily. Bees make honey and help the flowers grow. But you should not touch them, they might sting you if they are scared," her mom said.

Lily was curious. She wanted to meet the bee. She moved closer to the flower, slowly and quietly. She said hello to the bee.

"Hello, bee. I am Lily. You are pretty. Can we be friends?" she said.

The bee looked at Lily. It was busy collecting nectar from the flower. It did not want to be disturbed. But it was patient and polite. It buzzed softly.

"Hello, Lily. I am Bee. Thank you for your compliment. I am glad you like flowers. But I have to work now. Maybe we can talk later, when I am done," it said.

Lily nodded. She understood. She did not want to bother the bee. She smiled and said goodbye.

"Goodbye, Bee. I hope you have a good day. Maybe I will see you again," she said.

She walked away with her mom, happy and proud. She had met a bee and learned something new. She wondered what other bugs she could meet in the garden.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play outside and look at the stars. One night, they saw a big, bright star that shone more than the others. They wondered what it was.

"Maybe it is a movie star," Lily said. "Maybe it is in a movie that we can watch."

"Or maybe it is a spaceship," Ben said. "Maybe it is from a far away place that we don't know."

They decided to follow the star and see where it went. They took their bikes and rode along the road. The star moved slowly in the sky, and they tried to keep up. They passed by many houses and shops, but they did not stop.

After a while, they came to a big field. The star was very close to the ground. It looked like a big ball of light. Lily and Ben were curious and scared. They got off their bikes and walked towards the star. They heard a soft sound, like a hum.

"Hello," a voice said. "Don't be afraid. I am a friend."

Lily and Ben saw a small figure come out of the star. It looked like a person, but with green skin and big eyes. It smiled and waved at them.

"Who are you?" Lily asked. "Where are you from?"

"I am Zee," the figure said. "I am from a planet called Zara. I came to visit your world and learn about it. I saw you looking at me, and I wanted to say hi."

Lily and Ben were amazed. They had never met anyone like Zee before. He was very different, but also very nice. They asked him many questions, and he answered them. He told them about his planet, his family, and his hobbies. He showed them some things he brought with him, like a toy, a book, and a picture. He also asked them about their planet, their family, and their hobbies. He listened to them and learned from them. He liked their things, too.

They had a lot of fun talking and playing with Zee. They forgot about the time and the dark. They did not notice that their parents were looking for them and worried about them.

Soon, Zee said he had to go. He said his star was his spaceship, and he had to return to his planet. He thanked Lily and Ben for being his friends, and gave them a hug. He said he hoped to see them again someday.

"Goodbye, Zee," Lily and Ben said. "We will miss you. Have a safe trip."

They watched Zee get into his star and fly away. The star shone brightly in the sky, and then faded away. Lily and Ben felt sad, but also happy. They had made a new friend, and learned something new. They realized that even though Zee was different, he was also the same. He was kind, smart, and funny. He was a good person.

They got on their bikes and rode back home. They told their parents what happened, and apologized for being late. Their parents were angry, but also relieved. They hugged them and told them they loved them. They also told them to be careful, and not to go too far without telling them.

Lily and Ben understood. They said they were sorry, and they loved them, too. They also said they had learned a lesson. They said they had learned to be curious, but also cautious. They said they had learned to be open, but also respectful. They said they had learned to be friendly, but also responsible.

They said they had learned that the world was big and mysterious, but also wonderful and amazing. They said they had learned that the stars could shine with many colors, but also with many stories.

Lily liked to mail letters to her friends. She had many friends who lived far away. She used crayons and stickers to make her letters pretty. She also liked to draw pictures of her favorite animal, the elephant. She loved elephants because they were big and strong and independent. They could do many things by themselves.

One day, Lily got a letter back from her friend Sam. Sam lived in Africa. He wrote that he saw a real elephant in the park. He sent Lily a photo of the elephant. Lily was very happy and excited. She wanted to see the elephant too.

She ran to her mom and showed her the letter and the photo. She asked, "Mom, can we go to Africa and see the elephant?"

Mom smiled and hugged Lily. She said, "That would be wonderful, but we can't go right now. Africa is very far away. We need a lot of money and time to go there. Maybe when you are older, we can go together."

Lily felt sad. She really wanted to see the elephant. She said, "But mom, I want to see the elephant now. Can't we mail ourselves to Africa?"

Mom laughed and said, "No, we can't mail ourselves to Africa. That's not how mail works. Mail is for letters and packages, not for people. Besides, it would be very uncomfortable and dangerous to be in a box for so long. You wouldn't like it."

Lily thought for a moment. She said, "OK, mom, I understand. But can we mail the elephant a letter? Maybe he would like to be my friend too."

Mom nodded and said, "Sure, we can mail the elephant a letter. That's a very nice idea. Why don't you write him a letter and tell him about yourself and your love for elephants? Maybe you can also draw him a picture of yourself and your family. I'm sure he would appreciate it."

Lily smiled and said, "OK, mom, I will do that. Thank you, mom. You are the best."

She ran to her room and got her crayons and paper. She wrote and drew a letter for the elephant. She hoped he would write back to her soon. She put the letter in an envelope and wrote his name and address. She gave the letter to mom and said, "Please mail this to the elephant, mom. I can't wait to hear from him."

Mom took the letter and said, "OK, Lily, I will mail this to the elephant. I'm proud of you for being so kind and curious. You are a wonderful girl."

She kissed Lily and said, "I love you, Lily."

Lily hugged mom and said, "I love you too, mom. And I love the elephant."

Lily was a little girl who liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She wanted to learn how to cook and bake yummy things. One day, her mom was making a cake and Lily asked if she could help.

"Of course, you can help, Lily," her mom said. "But you have to be very careful. The stove is hot and you can get hurt if you touch it. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will not touch the stove."

Her mom gave her a big hug and said, "Good girl. Now, you can help me by waving this spoon and mixing the batter in this bowl. Can you do that?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, mom. I can do that." She took the spoon and started to wave it in the bowl. She felt happy and proud to help her mom.

But then, she saw something shiny on the stove. It was a silver fork that her mom had used to crack the eggs. Lily thought it looked pretty and wanted to see it closer. She forgot what her mom had told her and reached for the fork.

"Ouch!" she cried. She had touched the hot stove and burned her hand. She dropped the spoon and the batter and started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry and ran to her. She saw what had happened and quickly took Lily to the sink. She ran cold water over her hand and wrapped it in a soft cloth.

"I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry. I touched the stove. It was hot. It hurt," Lily sobbed.

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. It's okay. I'm not mad at you. But you have to listen to me when I tell you something. I tell you because I love you and I want you to be safe. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I love you too. I'm sorry."

Her mom kissed her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You're a good girl. But next time, please don't touch the stove. It's very dangerous. Promise me?"

Lily promised and said, "I promise, mom. I won't touch the stove again. I will listen to you."

Her mom smiled and said, "Good girl. Now, let's finish the cake together. And then we can eat it and share it with dad and brother. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "That sounds good, mom. That sounds very good."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of listening to parents and being careful around hot things.

Lily and Ben crawl inside their leaf house. They are happy and cozy. They have a twig lock and a leaf roof. They are ready for a nap. They close their eyes and smile. They love their leaf house.

Tom sees a big slide. He wants to go on it. He runs to the slide and waits in line. Lily follows him. She is scared of the slide. It is too high and fast for her.

But Tom does not listen. He grabs Lily's hand and pulls her to the slide. Lily tries to get away, but Tom is too strong. He pays the man at the slide and pushes Lily on it.

Lily screams. She feels helpless. She does not like the slide. She wants to get off. She cries and cries.

Tom goes on the slide after her. He thinks it is fun. He does not see Lily crying. He does not hear her screaming.

When they reach the bottom, Lily runs to her mom. She hugs her and tells her what happened. Her mom is angry at Tom. She tells him he was very mean and rude. She tells him to say sorry to Lily.

Tom feels bad. He did not mean to make Lily cry. He thought she would like the slide. He says sorry to Lily. He asks her to be his friend again.

Lily is still sad. She does not want to play with Tom. She says no. She goes to play something else with her mom.

Tom does not like Lily's dress. He thinks it is too girly and boring. He says, "Your dress is not good. It is too pink and frilly. My car is better. It is fast and loud. I can drive it anywhere I want!"

Lily feels sad and angry. She likes her dress and thinks it is beautiful. She says, "No, your car is not better. It is too noisy and dirty. You cannot drive it anywhere. You need a road and a license. My dress is better. I can wear it to a party or a picnic. It makes me happy and pretty!"

Tom and Lily start to argue. They raise their voices and say mean things to each other. They do not want to share their crayons and paper. They pull and tug at them. They make a big mess.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the crayons and paper all over the floor. She sees Tom and Lily with angry faces and tears in their eyes. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting? You should be nice and kind to each other. You should appreciate each other's work. You both did a good job with your prints. They are different, but they are both creative and fun. Can you say sorry and hug each other?"

Tom and Lily look at each other. They feel sorry and ashamed. They say sorry and hug each other. They pick up the crayons and paper and put them away. They look at each other's prints again. They see that they are both good in their own way. They say, "Your print is nice. I like it. Can we play together?"

Mom smiles and says, "Yes, you can play together. You are good friends. You can learn from each other and have fun. You can print more things if you want. But remember to use your words and not your hands when you disagree. And remember to say please and thank you when you share. OK?"

Tom and Lily nod and say, "OK, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."

Mom hugs them and says, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. You are my sweet children. Now, go and play nicely."

Tom and Lily were two otters who liked to play in the river. They swam and slid and splashed all day. They had many friends, but their best friend was Ben, a beaver who lived in a big dam.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a new otter in the river. He was big and brown and had a shiny coat. He said his name was Rex and he was very strong and smart. He told Tom and Lily that he knew a secret place where they could find lots of fish and shells. He asked them to join him and follow him.

Tom and Lily were curious and hungry. They wanted to see the secret place and eat the fish and shells. They said goodbye to Ben and followed Rex. Ben was worried. He did not trust Rex. He thought he was lying and wanted to trick Tom and Lily. He decided to follow them and see where they were going.

Rex led Tom and Lily to a narrow tunnel under the water. He said the secret place was at the end of the tunnel. He said they had to swim fast and not stop. He said he would go first and wait for them. He swam into the tunnel and disappeared.

Tom and Lily followed him. They swam fast and did not stop. They did not see that the tunnel was getting darker and smaller. They did not hear Ben calling them to come back. They did not know that Rex was not their friend, but a foolish and mean otter who wanted to trap them and eat them.

When Tom and Lily reached the end of the tunnel, they saw Rex waiting for them. He had a big smile and sharp teeth. He said he was glad they joined him. He said they were his lunch. He said they were foolish and silly to trust him. He said he was going to eat them.

Tom and Lily were scared and sorry. They wished they had not followed Rex. They wished they had stayed with Ben. They wished they had listened to their friend. They did not know what to do.

But Ben knew what to do. He had followed them and seen what Rex had done. He was brave and clever. He had a plan. He found a big stick and swam to the tunnel. He pushed the stick into the tunnel and blocked it. He trapped Rex inside. He saved Tom and Lily.

Tom and Lily were happy and grateful. They hugged Ben and thanked him. They said he was their best friend. They said they were sorry for leaving him. They said they would never trust Rex again. They said they would always listen to their friend.

Ben was happy and proud. He said he was their friend. He said he was glad they were safe. He said they should go back to the river and play. He said they should forget about Rex and his lies. He said they should have fun and be careful.

Tom and Lily agreed. They followed Ben and swam out of the tunnel. They went back to the river and played. They swam and slid and splashed all day. They had many friends, but their best friend was Ben, a beaver who lived in a big dam.

Tim tried to break the knob with his toy hammer. He hit the knob very hard, but it did not break. Instead, his toy hammer broke into pieces. Tim was very sad and started to cry. The box stayed closed and Tim never got to see what was inside.

One day, a little girl named Sally found a weird mug in her kitchen. It was big, blue, and had a funny face on it. Sally thought it was very funny and wanted to show her mom.

When Sally showed her mom the weird mug, something strange happened. The mug started to talk! It said, "Hello, I am a magic mug! I can make your favorite drink if you say 'please'." Sally and her mom were very surprised.

Sally said, "Please, magic mug, make me some juice!" The weird mug made her some tasty juice. Sally and her mom laughed and had a fun time with the magic mug. They were happy that this weird thing happened to them.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim lived in a small nest high up in a tree. He loved to play with his friends, the butterflies, and spin around in the sky.

One day, Tim saw a big bird spinning in the sky. Tim wanted to spin just like the big bird. He tried to spin, but he could not do it. He felt very ashamed. Tim went back to his nest and hid.

His butterfly friends came to his nest and asked him to come out and play. Tim told them he was ashamed because he could not spin like the big bird. The butterflies told Tim that it was okay, and they would help him learn to spin. They practiced spinning together, and soon, Tim could spin just like the big bird. Tim was very happy and played with his friends every day, spinning and flying in the sky.

Max finished counting and looked for Tom. He heard a loud noise from the box. Max knew where Tom was hiding! He went to the box and opened it. Tom jumped out and said, "You found me! You are so smart!" They both laughed and played in the mist all day.

One day, the elephant saw a tree. The tree was very hard. The elephant wanted to pretend to be a tree too. He stood still like the tree and tried to be hard. He tried very hard to be a tree.

But then, a storm came. The wind blew and the rain fell. The hard tree stood strong. The elephant tried to be a hard tree too. But he was not a tree. The wind pushed the elephant and he fell. The elephant was sad because he could not be a tree. The storm made the elephant learn that he could not pretend to be everything.

One day, a big truck was driving down the road. The truck was very patient as it went slow for the kids playing nearby. The truck driver saw a little dog in the road and stopped. "Woof!" said the dog. The driver smiled and said, "Hi, little dog! Be careful on the road."

Later, the truck driver saw a big tree in the road. He had to stop again. He tried to move the tree, but it was too heavy. He thought and thought. Then, he remembered the little dog. He knew the dog could help him. 

The truck driver went back to find the little dog. "Woof! Woof!" said the dog, happy to see the driver again. "Can you help me move a big tree?" asked the driver. The dog wagged its tail and followed the driver to the tree. With a loud "snap," the little dog broke a branch, making the tree lighter. Together, they moved the tree out of the way. The truck driver thanked the dog and continued on his way, happy that he had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom liked to speak a lot. He would talk all day to his friends and family. One day, Tom saw a big tree. He wanted to know how tall it was, so he tried to measure it.

Tom found a long stick to help him measure the tree. He felt a little uncomfortable holding the stick, but he wanted to know the tree's height. As he tried to measure the tree, a wise old man walked by. The old man saw Tom struggling with the stick.

The old man said, "Tom, you don't need a stick to measure the tree. Just look at its shadow on the ground." Tom listened to the old man and saw the shadow. He learned that sometimes it is better to listen than to speak.

From that day on, Tom talked less and listened more. He became a wise boy who knew many things. The village people liked Tom more because he was not always speaking. The moral of the story is to listen more and speak less.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to swim in the ocean. One day, Lily went to the beach with her mom and dad. She saw a big, scary shark in the water. The shark had sharp teeth and looked very dangerous.

Lily's mom told her to be careful and not to go too far into the water. But Lily didn't listen. She swam out farther and farther until she was in the deep water. Suddenly, the shark appeared and started to swim towards her.

Lily was very scared, but she remembered what her mom had said. She kicked her legs as hard as she could and swam back to the shore. When she got there, her dad scooped her up and hugged her tight. "You're safe now," he said. "That was a close call. Sharks can destroy anything in their path."

From that day on, Lily never went too far into the water again. She knew that the ocean could be dangerous, but she also knew that she was brave enough to face it. And whenever she saw a bitter taste in her mouth, she remembered the scary shark and how she had overcome her fear.

"Hey, that's my purple crayon. Give it back," Ben says.

"No, I want it. It's mine now," Anna says.

They pull the purple crayon. They are angry.

"Stop it. You are not nice. You have to share," Ben says.

"No, you stop it. You are not nice. You have to share," Anna says.

They keep pulling the purple crayon. They are not happy.

Then, they hear a voice.

"What are you doing, Anna and Ben? Why are you fighting?" the voice says.

It is their teacher, Miss Lily. She sees the purple crayon in their hands.

"Miss Lily, Anna took my purple crayon. She won't give it back," Ben says.

"Miss Lily, Ben won't let me use his purple crayon. He is mean," Anna says.

Miss Lily shakes her head. She is sad.

"Anna and Ben, you are friends. You have to be kind and share. You have many crayons and papers. You can use them together. You can make a beautiful picture together. But if you fight, you will break the crayon and tear the paper. You will make a mess. You will not have fun. Do you want that?" Miss Lily says.

Anna and Ben look at each other. They look at the purple crayon. They look at the floor. They see their crayons and papers. They see their picture.

They feel sorry. They shake their heads.

"No, Miss Lily. We don't want that. We want to be friends. We want to be kind and share. We want to make a beautiful picture together," Anna and Ben say.

They let go of the purple crayon. They smile.

"Here, Anna. You can use my purple crayon. I can use your red crayon," Ben says.

"Thank you, Ben. You are nice. Here, you can use my red crayon. I can use your yellow crayon," Anna says.

They swap their crayons. They hug.

"Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are nice. You are good at sharing. I am proud of you. Now, let's finish your picture. It will be wonderful," Miss Lily says.

She helps them with their picture. They use their crayons and papers. They use their blue folder and their orange folder. They draw and color. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big cage. Inside the cage, there was a lion. The lion was thin and sad.

"Look, a lion!" Lily said. "Can we keep him?"

"No, we can't," Tom said. "He is not a pet. He is wild. He can hurt us."

"But he is so thin. He needs food and love," Lily said. "Maybe we can give him some bread and water."

Tom was scared, but he wanted to make Lily happy. He said, "OK, but we have to be careful. We have to open the cage a little bit. And we have to run away fast."

They found some bread and water in their backpacks. They went to the cage. They opened the cage a little bit. They threw the bread and water inside. The lion saw the food. He was hungry. He came to the cage door.

Lily and Tom were happy. They thought the lion liked them. They said, "Hello, lion. We are your friends. Do you want more food?"

The lion did not answer. He did not want more food. He wanted to get out of the cage. He pushed the cage door with his paw. The cage door opened more. Lily and Tom did not see it. They were too close to the cage.

The lion jumped out of the cage. He roared. He was angry. He saw Lily and Tom. He did not see friends. He saw food. He ran to them. He bit them. They screamed. They could not run away. They could not keep the lion. The lion kept them.

They go to the living room. They see their mommy and daddy on the couch. They are reading a book. They look bored and tired. Anna and Lily have an idea. They run to them and show them the photo.

"Look, mommy, daddy, this is you!" Anna says.

"You are so pink and happy!" Lily says.

Mommy and daddy look at the photo. They smile and remember. They hug Anna and Lily. They thank them for the photo.

"Can we take a photo with you?" Anna asks.

"Of course, sweeties, let's unite and smile!" Daddy says.

He takes his phone and puts it on a table. He sets a timer. He joins mommy and the girls on the couch. They wrap the scarf around their hands. They look at the phone and smile.

Click! The phone takes a photo. It is a photo of a happy family. They wear pink clothes and hold hands. They love each other. Anna and Lily are happy. They made their mommy and daddy happy too. They are like their mommy and daddy.

Tom and Sue were not happy. They did not want toast and jam. They wanted sausages. They looked at the plate. They looked at each other. They had an idea.

They waited until Mom went to the bathroom. Then they ran to the table. They grabbed some sausages. They stuffed them in their mouths. They were hot and juicy and yummy.

They heard Mom coming back. They ran to their room. They hid under the bed. They thought they were clever.

But they were not clever. They were naughty. They did not know that Dad had a special sauce on his sausages. The sauce was spicy and strong. It made their mouths burn and their eyes water. It made them cough and cry.

Mom heard them. She went to their room. She saw them under the bed. She saw the sausages. She was angry.

"What did you do? You ate Dad's sausages. You did not listen to me. You were selfish and greedy. You are in big trouble," Mom said.

She took them out of the bed. She made them drink some water. She made them say sorry. She made them go to the corner. They had no breakfast. They had no fun. They had a bad day.

Tim and Jen nod. They say, "We will learn. We will listen. We will be careful. We will not do this again."

But the cricket refuses to come out. It likes to be free and hop around. It does not want to live in a jar.

Ben shakes his head. He does not like the snail. He thinks it is boring and icky.

"No, thank you," he says. "I want a pet that is fun and reliable. Like a dog or a cat."

Anna and Ben decide to leave the bugs alone. They go back to the house and ask their mom for a real pet. Maybe she will say yes.

"Look at my doll, Ben!" Mia said. "She is so pretty and adorable! She can dance and sing!"

They showed each other their toys and tried to make them play together. But the gorilla and the doll did not get along. The gorilla was too rough and the doll was too delicate. The gorilla knocked over the doll and made her cry. The doll slapped the gorilla and made him angry.

"Stop it, gorilla!" Mia shouted. "You are mean to my doll!"

"Stop it, doll!" Ben shouted. "You are rude to my gorilla!"

They started to argue and pull their toys away from each other. They did not want to share or be friends.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It was their mom, who was baking a cake. She had spilled some flour and made a mess.

"Oops!" Mom said. "I need some help here. Can you two come and help me clean up?"

Ben and Mia looked at each other. They felt bad for fighting and making noise. They decided to put their toys aside and go to help their mom. They ran to the kitchen and saw the flour everywhere.

"Wow, what happened here?" Ben asked.

"I was trying to make a cake, but I dropped the flour bag," Mom said. "Can you help me sweep it up?"

"Sure, Mom!" Mia said. "We are sorry for being loud. We were playing with our toys."

They grabbed a broom and a dustpan and started to sweep the flour. They worked together and made it into a pile. They were about to throw it away, when they noticed something strange.

"Hey, what's that?" Ben asked, pointing to the pile.

They looked closer and saw their toys. The gorilla and the doll were in the pile, covered in flour. But they were not the same size as before. They were much smaller. They had shrunk!

"Wow, how did that happen?" Mia asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe the flour made them shrink."

They picked up their toys and brushed off the flour. They were amazed by how tiny they were. They looked at each other and smiled.

"They are so cute!" Mia said.

"They are so funny!" Ben said.

They held their toys in their hands and felt a new love for them. They realized that they did not have to be strong or pretty to be fun. They could be friends and play together.

"Can we keep them like this, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Can we, please?" Mia asked.

Mom looked at them and laughed. She saw how happy they were and how they had learned to share and be kind.

"Sure, why not?" Mom said. "They are adorable, just like you two."

"Come on, Lily!" Max says. "The bike is fun! You can sit behind me!"

Lily shakes her head. She does not want to sit behind Max. She wants her ball. She is angry.

"Max, you are not nice!" Lily says. "You took my ball! I don't want to play with you!"

Max stops. He sees Lily's face. She is crying. He feels sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Max says. "I didn't mean to make you cry. Here is your ball. You can have it."

He gives the ball to Lily. Lily wipes her tears. She smiles.

"Thank you, Max," Lily says. "You are nice. Do you want to play catch with me?"

Max nods. He likes Lily. He likes the ball. He likes the bike. He likes to play.

"OK, Lily," Max says. "Let's play catch. But can we ride the bike later?"

Lily nods. She likes Max. She likes the ball. She likes the bike. She likes to play.

"OK, Max," Lily says. "Let's play catch. And we can ride the bike later."

They play catch. They have fun. They are friends.

Lily and Sam went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. Lily liked the elephants best. They were big and gray and had long noses.

"Can I feed the elephants, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. Here, take this apple and hold it in your hand. Then lean over the fence and reach out to the elephant. He will take it gently with his nose," Mom said.

Lily did as Mom said. She leaned over the fence and held out the apple. She saw a clear eye and a long nose coming closer. She felt a soft touch on her hand and the apple was gone. She heard a happy sound from the elephant.

"Wow, that was fun! Thank you, elephant!" Lily said.

Sam wanted to try too. He took another apple and leaned over the fence. But he leaned too far and lost his balance. He fell over the fence and landed on the ground. He was scared and cried.

"Help, help! I'm in the elephant cage!" Sam shouted.

Mom and Dad ran to the fence and called for help. The zookeeper came and opened the gate. He picked up Sam and brought him back to his parents. He checked if Sam was hurt. He was not, but he was dirty and wet.

"Are you okay, Sam?" Mom asked.

"I'm okay, Mom. But I don't like the elephants. They are too big and wet and scary," Sam said.

Lily hugged Sam and said, "Don't worry, Sam. The elephants are nice. They just wanted to say hello. Maybe you can try another animal, like the monkeys. They are small and funny and cute."

Sam nodded and smiled. He liked the monkeys. He and Lily went to see the monkeys with Mom and Dad. They had a good time at the zoo.

Lily and Tom are scared. They do not like the dog. They want to get away from it.

Tim and his mom went to the store to buy some food. Tim saw a big cake with red and white frosting. He wanted to eat the cake very much. He asked his mom, "Mom, can we buy the cake, please?"

Mom looked at the cake and said, "Sorry, Tim, we don't have enough money to buy the cake. We only have enough money to buy the things we need, like bread and milk and eggs."

Tim felt sad. He wished he had more money to buy the cake. He looked around the store and saw a man drop his wallet on the floor. The man did not notice and walked away. Tim ran to the wallet and picked it up. He saw many green papers and shiny coins inside. He thought, "Maybe I can use this money to buy the cake."

But then he remembered what his mom taught him. She said, "Tim, you should always be honest and helpful. If you find something that does not belong to you, you should give it back to the owner. That is the right thing to do."

Tim decided to listen to his mom. He ran after the man and said, "Excuse me, sir, you dropped your wallet. Here it is."

The man was surprised and happy. He said, "Thank you, young man, you are very helpful. You saved me a lot of trouble. How can I thank you?"

Tim said, "You're welcome, sir. I don't need anything. I'm just happy to help."

The man smiled and said, "Well, you are very kind and generous. I want to give you a reward. Here, take this money and buy yourself something nice."

He gave Tim some of the green papers and coins from his wallet. Tim thanked him and ran back to his mom. He showed her the money and said, "Mom, look, the man gave me this money for being helpful. Now we can buy the cake!"

Mom hugged Tim and said, "I'm so proud of you, Tim. You did the right thing. You were honest and helpful. And you were lucky, too. The man was very nice to give you a reward. Let's go buy the cake and share it with our family."

Tim and his mom bought the cake and went home. They had a delicious dessert and a happy day. Tim learned that being helpful can provide good things. He also learned that cake tastes better when you share it with the ones you love.
